I've thoroughly enjoyed playing Crusader Kings 2. It's like playing a beefed up version of Lords of the Realm 2. The only downside (depending on your point of view) is the lack of direct control over combat between armies. But the trade off of that is the fact that you can have  32 player multiplayer game going on. That's right, up to 32 people running their own empires, kingdoms, duchies and counties...in addition to all the npcs running their own little slices of the world.
This Game took a while to get into. Eventually you will get it and then it is like cracked cokaine and you have to play just one more turn.

It doesn't get any better than this.
Each map is unique in its setting and objective concept (the cyberpunk theme of the game is greatly enhanced by excellent skybox's and background noise that draws you into the level). They require good team co-ordination in order to win. Especially since aspects of the objectives take place in 2 parallel worlds that affect each other in real time [Meatspace - physical world: similar to most fps with a cyperpunk theme (weapons like laser rifle, tesla rifle, ion cannon), 3 class types (v.balanced) and deus ex like implants, inc increased speed, thermal vision, medic, stealth(invisi). Cyberspace - think system shock 1 or tripping on acid: req decking implant; deckers speed thru cyberspace hacking objectives, adding security and fighting off enemy deckers in low grav/high speed combat using in essence quake railgun, lightening gun and rocket launcher.]
The game does have a high learning curve, there are game guides on the community hub:
If you have questions when your in game most players will answer them, generally speaking the community is pretty friendly.
If you find that you keep going on and servers are empty recommend you join this group:
Matches are organised and announced through this and sometimes when public games are going on there is also an announcement to indicate a server is populated.
This game last had a major update at the end of 2013.

For Game of Thrones fans, the best way to describe Crusader Kings II is to call it "The Official Tywin Lannister Simulator." The purpose of game isn't to simply gain land, but to build a powerful dynasty through political intrigue, diplomacy, marriages, and outright war.
The things you can do--and the depths of villiany you can sink too--to advance your family's political interest is complex and wideranging. From murdering babies who can one day claim your throne to slowing inciting civil wars in other kingdoms by pitting different lords against one another, Crusader Kings II is also an insightful reflection of what people can do to win.

A suprisingly entertaining, fun, and challenging RTS game with lots of replay value, based on the early Human-Covenant War years of the Halo Universe.
Anyone that already played it on the Xbox back then and wishes to remeber the good ol' days will really appreciate it truly being a proper PC port. The only issue is that some of the controls are rather awkward (Mainly regarding troop selection), you can still tell this was originally intended for consoles only.
The campaign is good. It adds something new every time, and it gets pretty challenging towards the end. As you play in the harder difficulties you'll get increasingly more frustrated, but after beating each level, you will be even more satisfied.
The multiplayer is lonely and unbalanced af, if you don't have a good strategy
by your foes. (That's if you even find a public game available) Tbh it's best to play with friends, but it's more likely that you'll end up playing skirmish. However you play, you should have fun after all.
The Halo chronology, skulls and other easter eggs are pretty cool too. Unmistakably Halo.
Yet all of this isn't even the best thing about the very existance of this game. The best thing about this game is that it
hopefully it's an attempt from Microsoft and 343 to understand the potential and marketability of Halo in other platforms.
If you like RTS games, the Halo Universe, just want to have fun with friends, or have been begging for Halo to be properly ported to PC by Microsoft and 343, then this is a must buy. 10/10
As a side note: If you want to have a taste of 'remastered' Halo for PC, you should probably check CMT's The Silent Cartographer: Evolved and similar projects.

One of the best, most addicting games on Steam. Short of Civ V and Skyrim, I think this is the game I have clocked the most hours on on Steam. You can make the game challenging for yourself, or just see what kind of crazy alternative history scenarios you can create.
The expansions (the DLC that cost a bit more than the others) have crazy value and the other dlc you can buy is just nice toppings if you care about what they have. I myself have mostly bought the songpacks, because I love the music they bring, but you can enjoy the game entirely without the packs. The expansions unlock more play options in the game, so I highly recommend you get them at least after you've played the game for a bit, as they are complete gamechangers.
Heck, if there's a deal like I'm seeing right now for winter sales, pay a little extra for the CKII Collection and get most of the stuff cheap. Right now the base game is 9,99€ and the collection, which includes at least four expansions and a lot of content packs is 19,99€. What a deal! That said, the base game is certainly worth the full price too.
What better review for the game than to give some real stories of great moments?
1. One of my earliest crazy alternate history scenarios was this: I started as the King of Scotland. Eventually I ended up (through intrigue and deceit) being married to the Empress of Byzantium (one of the most prestigious positions in the historical setting). This of course resulted in my daughter becoming Queen of Scotland and Empress of Byzantium.
2. With the Legacy of Rome expansions you can achieve one of the most rewarding things you can ever do in gaming. You can start off as a count in the Byzantine Empire and slowly make your way to becoming Emperor. You'd think that'd be enough, but no. You can then proceed to invade Jerusalem, Alexandria and other holy lands thus restoring the Pentarch and making Orthodoxy the de facto form of Christianity, allowing you to outright turn Catholism into a heresy! But wait, there's more. You are Emperor of Byzantium, also known internally as Rome. It's time to make everyone accept you as the Emperor of Rome. How? Reclaim the old areas, invade Rome and recreate the Roman Empire! First Rome, then the world.
3. The Empire of Scandinavia!

*Disclaimer* I don't claim to be an expert on halo wars or any other RTS, this review will be from the perspective of a first time RTS player.
Halo wars was my first and only RTS I have played to date, and I've enjoyed every second of it. Have you ever wanted to muster an army? Command an army to obliterate an enemy in intense combat? If so, this is the game for you.
When you enter a game you're presented with an unbuilt base, from there you use what resources you're given to build the necessary infrastructure to help the production of your base and army.  Whist you're preparing your base and army, you can't help but feel vulnerable, you have no idea what your opponent(s) are doing. The uncertainty is a thrill, "Will they attack?" "Do I need to work on my defence?","The enemy seems dorment, maybe I should attack now, but what if they launch a counter attack?"  Once you have concocted your battle plans and army, you may decide to launch an attack, as your army moves on, you know along the path you'll most likely come into contact with an army, you're feeling confident, your army is too big to be overwhelmed, but wait, you're minutes away from your base what if they launch an air attack that'll take you by suprise and leave you in a compromisable postion?  So many possibilities in a single round, this is what makes this game so fun.  You have to excersise all these possiblities, or you may die.  You gotta act as a true battle commander, you have to be quick smart or you'll perish.
THINGS YOU MAY WANT KNOW.
1. There are 2 factions in halo wars, UNSC and Covenant , there are 3 leaders on each side. Each faction offers a different style of playing, one not being a re skin of the other, despite these differences, they offer a fair playing field. Each leader in their corresponding factions will provide different​ factors such as specific units or passives skills. Overall providing a different but fair playstyle.
2. Each map has its own layout and look so they all provide a different strategic advantage and/or diadvantage.
3. If you're worried about out playing all the set difficulties, no need to worry, they have a difficulty called "automatic", which means everytime you win, your "automatic" score goes up, which will increase the difficulty, this will last a LONG time, always providing a challenge, suited to your skill level.
4. The campaign is actually quite fun to play, especially if you're interested in the lore or have enjoyed any other Halo games. I haven't finished the campaign but so far it has been a blast, it isn't tedious at all and after every mission, you feel more invested into the storyline.
Overall 8/10

Chivalry is truly the only game of it's kind. For all you who have a skeptical mind about these sorts of games, don't. If you're looking for an amazing medieval combat experience where you actually feel like you're swinging a weapon rather than playing preset animations, then buy the game. HOWEVER, like everyone else is saying, you will die. You will die a lot. And by a lot I mean 10 times more than you'll kill someone.
You will improve, over time. I've played about 1,100 hours of the game and I still consider myself a novice. Thus if you wish to be great at fighting, chances are you'll need a lot of patience and practice. It's not like an ordinary hack and slash game like others of its genre. Don't go into chivalry expecting you'll be good at it after playing something like Mount and Blade, or War of the Roses. They are great games too but they are incomparable to chivalry. First off, chivalry is much more responsive(providing pings are fine). It is very fast paced, and very punishing if you make any mistakes.
The combat is unique, it's really hard to explain for there's no game existent to compare it to. You will need to practice like a medieval swordsman or an ordinary athlete practices at his craft. There are many things that you must consider and take account for in order to become an exceptional killer. You will need to understand the basic psychology and strategies in combatant engagements, feetwork, and timing above all.
I guess to conclude this review, I'd say:
If you want to play a very fun hack and slash game with your friends, get chivalry. You'll all die a lot but it'll be well worth it. The game is very comedic and is very good for a few laughs.
If you want to play a skill-based competitive game(if you're a serious gamer and into immersion) get chivalry.
Chivalry is VERY rewarding when you kill someone, and gets your heart pumping like no other game I've ever experienced.
If you don't like getting killed a lot while ascending the VERY, VERY steep learning curve, or if you don't have the patience and get upset easily, don't waste your money. Hit that back arrow key now and go play something that isn't as time demanding for adequacy.

Although a bit over-priced considering it being so short (I didn't stress through the game what-so-ever and still beat it in three hours) I recommend this game, but I would advice picking it up when it's on sale, since three hours for 14 euro is a bit on the expensive side. A beutifully designed game, with an engaging and sad little story about a young girl. Filled with economical issues, romantic affairs, mafia-involvement and drama.  With heavy elements of film noir, and with a graphic style that in many ways resembles a german expressionist silent film, with a touch of Tim Burton-esque quirkiness as the beutiful cherry on top. The humoristic elements such as hidden mature jokes really made me happy and sometimes I even laughed out loud. The puzzles are interesting, all though not that hard if you're used to puzzle-solving in games. But I still feel this game brought something new to the puzzle-genre. The gameplay mechanics are very well scripted and you quickly forget what buttons you have to click and just do it on impulse, immersed in the quirky little world that the game takes place in. Overall I really enjoyed this game, but it's far too short.

I would have to say Contrast is one of my favorite games. The art style, music and time setting are right up my street and the whole game takes place in a slightly surreal 'Alice In Wonderland' style. I'll explain. The world seems to be made of of floating islands floating in a night sky, it looks lovely but detracts the game from normality, that being said playing as an imaginary friend who can jump in and out of shadows ins't exactly normal so this floating island surreal-ness actually adds to the game, pushing it away from normal and closer to dream-like.
As I have said the music is also fantastic if you enjoy cabaret style music. There are also some lovely other tracks later in the game, one of my favorite plays during the carousel puzzle.
The whole jumping between shadows and normal world is an awesome mechanic. Not exactly new but it is still nicely done and it creates some interesting and genuinely challenging puzzles that stumped me for an embarissingly long time. One thing I will say is that it can be a bit trickey at times. The switching between the shadow and real worlds is tricky especially when jumping. If you don't time it right when jumping you will land half above, half in the shadow which gives you another 50/50 chance of clipping onto the shadow or being forced back into the real world which will probably spawn you into a death pit. After 6 or more times this gets annoying. The run animation is also odd too and the main character moves like she has a rocket attached to her back and strides like the Striders from Half Life 2.
Aside from those 2 tiny nit picks the story is good, visuals great and soundtrack fantastic. Pick it up, play it and you'll be glad you did.

I love LA Noire.
There's the open world. Not the largest map ever, but big enough- all in accurate 40's style, with people, buildings, and NPC's that make the city come alive.
There's the plotline, with the cases, which is very good, and interesting. The partners are wonderfully developed characters whom you grow to either hate or love (Rusty is my favourite).
Then there's the small things, like the huge array of detailed vehicles which you can drive (and run over stuff with), and the street crimes (simple spare-of-the moment apprehending criminals).
Overall, it's a wonderful game and the only downside is the fact there are huge loading problems, caused by various things, with various fixes that have varying degrees of effectiveness.
Sometimes it works, sometimes I have a painful process of changing this and that, restarting etc- but I'll say this: it's worth all the effort to play this game.

Noir games are often hit-or-miss because of the amount of stereotypes the genre builds upon, and Contrast followed the routine noir atmosphere and plotline.

Cool game with pretty graphics, great and atmospheric music, a unique gameplay mechanic making for fun puzzles, and a neat little story. Only rating it an 8/10 however because of bugs and other issues (note: my computer exceeds the recommended requirements and played the game fine on high settings). At times, Dawn will slide around at high speeds or suddenly stop moving due to some invisible obstruction. That's annoying while walking down the middle of the road, but downright frustrating when trying to solve puzzles, especially while in shadowland. These movements sometimes cause Dawn to shift out of shadows at inopportune times as well, requiring restarting entire puzzles. The worst issue, however, are the occasional times when something that is supposed to sparkle (such as an item that can be used or a collectible) does NOT sparkle, and thus can't be used. Collectibles don't stop you from completing the game, but the usable items not sparkling certainly will. I was able to solve this issue by restarting the game, but it's still annoying and meant lost progress.
All in all though, I would still recommend Contrast.

So, yeah... Warframe...
I'll just get right into the pros and cons.
PROS:
- Great movement/combat control
- Tons of customization
- Many different weapons
- Many, MANY weapon mods to choose from
- Match-making that works
- Thriving online community
CONS:
- Can get grindy
- Not much is explained to you
At the time of writing this I've put in about 90-ish hours. In this time I have aquired 5 Warframes with one of them being Prime (some Warframes/weapons have a "Prime" version that is better and harder to get), quite a few weapons, and I've just recently found all the parts to a new ship. This was not, however, done without platinum, Platinum is an in-game currency, but I've only spent it on cosmetic stuff like shaders, helmets and capes. I also used some to buy a Rhino Prime part as he's currently vaulted and to rush a few crafted items.
If you enjoy this game for any more than 30 hours and plan to keep playing it, I highly reccomend buying some platinum to support this FREE game. Don't buy full price though. Every time you log in, you'll get a log-in reward and on a few of those you'll recieve a 25%-75% off coupon.
TL;DR A fun game with a fair business model that makes you feel like a space ninja. Can be grindy if you're looking to build a specific frame/weapon. I also recommend playing with a friend/someone to help you understand how things work.

Pros:
The game looks beautiful. The fact that it was made by filming real paper construction gives it a distinctive look, and makes it look more real than a lot of CGI.
The puzzles are fair. If you have to resort to a walkthrough, you won't be shaking your head, wondering how you were supposed to figure that out.
Cons:
I said above that the puzzles are fair. But some of them are tough. At least, harder than I enjoyed.
The in-game help system uses simple equations to give a page number in the manual that Lumi carries with her. For instance, "Number of cogs x 100"; if there are three cogs in the puzzle that this refers to, the solution would be on page 300. But some of these clues are ambiguous: are you supposed to count the cogs that were already placed for you? Or just the ones you need to place yourself? And maybe it's not clear what constitutes a cog.
Bottom line:
A fun puzzler with beautiful visuals.

I will try to make this review short and sweet while still giving it a good review.
Honestly I don't get how this game get's the amount of hate that it does. Of course reviews on games vary but I love this game. I've had the game for just over a week and I've already put in 13.5 hours.
When playing this game there are several things to consider.
FIrst, when you start this game you WILL NOT be good at it. This isn't your typical game where you start it up and you get the hang of things within 10 minutes of playing because quite frankly it isn't that simple. The tutorial does a great job of giving you the basics and learning all the controls and how to use them but when to use certain attacks is the part you need to wrap your head around.
Chances are when you start this game you will be a tker (Team Killer) even if you don't intend to. The biggest complaint EVERYONE has including myself when playing this game is that people will run into group battles and keep left clicking or slashing and hitting every teamate with every swing killing enemies and teammates. It's usually the newer players that do this and it does get annoying at times. The easiest way to avoid it is using the mouse wheel for attacks. If you get this game you'll about these things fairly quickly.
The community on the game is surprisingly for the most part really good as well. Even if you team kill by mistake or what have you, you don't have those people yelling and screaming at you, everyone is pretty forgiving. The other amazing part is that even though there is friendly fire always on, you don't really have people running around cutting down there teammates and if there is a guy doing that he's kicked within 10 seconds of doing it.
The game is very noob friendly as well. There are servers that allow only rank 0-15 to be in them. This helps the new comers play with people that are less experienced. Keep in mind that once you get to about Rank 5 you have a decent grip on the game. With that said Rank 10-15's will be pretty good.
In my time played I've already reached rank 11 that's in 13 hours so it does take some time. I got the hang of the game fairly quickly but I am a fairly quick learner, so some people may find it a bit harder.

Time for another Timeraider Reviews :P  (SMALL SPOILERS INSIDE, NONE STORY-RELATED THOUGH) (30-11-2014)
So.. Contrast. Lets first get some things and negative points out of the way:
The game is very short. About 3-4 hours, 4-5 if you want to get all the collectibles.
I bought it during a 75% off sale, thus i cant judge well if it would be worth the full price. I would advice to wait for a sale .. like 50%-75% off :D Do keep in mind.. this is only based my normal 1 euro = 1 hour of gametime, nothing else.
Though it plays fine with a keyboard and mouse and has not a single problem while using those devices, as always i would advice playing a platformer with a controller. (Game has amazing controller support btw, even switching from keyboard to controller in the middle of a tutorial text, the line will change the keys the text redirects you to)
Now the good things:
The music is amazing. The jazzy style with some sweet vocals now and then made me finish this game quicker then expected due to being able to play longer without getting bored.
The atmosphere in the game is the other big part. It feels as if you got trown back into the past.. back to the time of the blues, gangsters and burlesque. Alot of the game being darker colored with not that much massively bright colored objects make it an amazing experience.
Now the platforming. When i started playing i felt trown back into another one of my favorite games in the past years.. Alice: Madness Returns. A 3D world from third-personview with platform elements while getting you further into the story in between. Even though Contrast doesnt hold any combat, the platforming parts are quite active... it doesnt just stop with moving platforms..nooooo.. because Contrast has something else.. shadows.
You are able to go into the light reflecting on walls etc. and go inside of your own shadow, allowing you to go alot further then just walking on physical objects. Combine this with being able to dash and be able to become a shadow even when mid-air makes for some exciting puzzles. Its not THAT hard but i can see some people taking their time at some puzzles for sure.
The story is great. Because your own personage stays on the background, you get fully emerged in the story of the child you are taking care of. Lets just say it has some nice twists and emotions (Not as emotional as Brothers: A tale of two sons (of which im not afraid to admit is the only game in history that literally made me shed a tear for a sec) with a good plot (though it might be slightly confusing for some ;D). I wont spoil anything of the story so enough about that!
Now the conclusion. Great game, nice controls, gameplay and atmosphere feel amazing and suck you in. Not supermemorable game that will change your life entirely but still a very very well-made game.
I would rate this game 7.5-8/10.
Not sure if i would pay full price since im a cheapass :P but at least worth looking into and certainly worth buying with any discount.
Its on 75% discount till 2 December (2014) btw.

Interesting world, shadow people, and art style
Great 2D/3D combine puzzle mechanic
Interactable objects are highlighted well
Light sources for building your 2D terrain are easy to find and manipulate
Easy to "slip out" of 2D puzzles
Camera angles matter when dashing in 2D
For those interested in the collectibles, you can't backtrack if you miss something
Puzzle objectives aren't always clear
Running in the 3D world sometimes feels too fast while walking feels too slow
Game textures and model polygons could've been a little higher res
The artistic world and 2D/3D blended puzzles are the big selling points of Contrast. The game has a solid 1920s feel complete with gangsters and big show biz. For some of the main story puzzles that are timed (you have to finish it before another character does something), you can find out some interesting alternate-ending-esque information by letting time run out. The 2D/3D puzzles were my big attraction to the game. I think the concept is really great and the dynamic manipulation of the 2D landscape using light is pretty terrific, but a little buggy. It's unfortunately easy to fall out of the 2D world, particularly when dashing over anything slopped, and bumps in the wall itself can create unexpected shadows that'll knock you out into the 3D if you walk into them. I could see all these things easily being fixed in a sequel with better collision detection and a little more optimization of the 2D world. No unexpected weirdness was encountered in the 3D.

Dystopia is a free cyberpunk First Person Shooter based on the Orange Box engine. The maps are objective based, with objectives unique to each map. The game is also exceptionally unique in it's addition of a "cyberspace" element in which your character's body is left in "meat space" while you become a person inside the wires of the network. Cyberspace lets you fight other players for dominance of the system in which you can utilize functions that affect meat space. Essentially, cyber gives you a leg up in the meat space world (which varies map to map). This game also takes an incredible amount of skill as far as an FPS goes. With 3 different classes and 4 weapons per class, mastery is quite a ways off.  However, though the learning curve is steep, it is extremely rewarding. The game also has a payoff for working as a team. You spawn as a team, you survive as a team. Not to mention when you shoot people, you get bleep noises. This game is fun, unique and well done, period.

Warframe, a universe thriving with lush, hidden lore. The place where a species of technologically crude, and industrious Grineer have made home. The place where a plutocratic, advanced, and money greedy Corpus have made home. The place where a technocyte plague known as the Infestation has made home. Ah, and of course.. the place where you, the noble, honorable, Tenno; have made home.
Warframe is a free to play done right, everything in this game can be earned for completely free. You know how I know? Well, I've been getting EVERYTHING for free, and have spent a fair amount of hours to get this info!
This game has thousands of mods. Unlike its 'comparable' Destiny, this game has more than a dumbed down skill tree. This game has a modding system. One which lets your power have billions of stat combos.
This game allows for player to player trading. Whether you're looking for 'prime' gear, or platinum (premium currency), trading has you covered. There are people willing to trade you for mods, gear, and platinum.
The UPDATES, now this is a big one. This game Warframe has had so many updates, nearly on a monthly basis that it could EASILY have had a Warframe 2 by now. For a game being completely free, these updates are WELL worth your time. I mean hell, for the first time, we're getting an enormous expansion adding open worlds! (which we all know will be expanded to every planet).
The memorable moments. One, undeniable fact, is that this game gets sweeter as time goes on. With monumental quests such as The Second Dream and The War Within, this game will blow you out of your socks. Though, for some, this can take up to 100-200 hours to get to. It's crazy, but gives you the best feeling and memory afterwards.
Your Space Mom. Every Tenno needs to feel like they have someone.. SOMEONE! For the longest time, in the game, I was closest to my dear space mom. The Lotus!
The soundtrack is absolutely gorgeous, I know this is a random one but it can really hit you in the feels later on. Try looking up "This is What You Are - Keith" <- It'll bring you to a Warframe song that is too good..
The grind can be unrelenting for some. For people like me, the grind was never bad because of my constant progression, but for people who aren't patient or want things quickly (in a progression system) this might be a bit too much.
The lore is very hidden. There is a story, but for some major lore, and theories on it, you'll have to look it up on YouTube. If you'd like a good series I recommend StallorD
The enemy scaling. For some people who love a hard challenge, the enemy scaling might be too much. Not exactly the ENEMY itself, but more specifically the ARMOUR on an enemy. It can be insane to even damage an enemy after level 100.
Dojo improvements. I think Tennogen should be introduced for the Dojo, more decorations should be added, AND massive group builds. I'm talking about decorations that require a load of resources. That way if you have a large and active clan, you'll have special things that show your true power, and riches!
On 'Finisher' animations for the Nikana backslash, a mark/bodysplit hould happen. What I mean is that you do a diagonal slash across the enemies back, yet no deep cut appears, or body splitting? I dunno, just a request!

So this review used to be positive. I used to love this game. I've spent countless of hours playing it and having fun and now that's not possible anymore. Why you say? Performance issues, a ton of them. The developer team has continously ignored the request of fans to get some optimizations. Answering their posts on the forum is not the same as fixing the problem.
And so on to the second reason. It has become evident to me that the skilled designers are no longer working on this game. With new games such as Stellaris and Hearts of Iron 4 being Paradoxes priority they have unfortunately let this game into the hands of incompetent people. They have left it to die. Perhaps there is a crusader kings 3 that I don't know about and they are simply trying to keep milking the "greatest" medieval game some more without any effort.
This brings us to my third reason. The milking. Instead of creating content with real value, we get empty filler content like the black plague. Something that was already in the game, something we all dreaded. Something that was perfectly fine to begin with. Sure the randomness added to it in the new dlc is fine along with the rest of the content, but that's it. It's "fine". But is this really what paradox is capable of? An entire dlc dedicated to disease with less content in it than any of the previous ones. Even less content than the horselords dlc. But hey, at least that one added a culture even if the mechanics of that culture is still broken, gamebreaking and in need of fixing. I appreciate the realism it adds. But it doesn't add anything interesting to the gameplay. It just adds an annoying chore that each player must dedicate time to instead of focusing on important matters, like killing your incompetent son. Oh and btw, why am I not allowed to kill my son anymore? Your reason was that it made the game too easy and all you did was stop us from being able to do so. Why not add a more serious consequence if people find out you murdered your son. Like having honorable vassals turn against you because, well, you disgust them. It would be pretty easy for them to rally support if news got out the king stabbed his own son to death because he wasn't good enough in the kings eyes.
Too many times have the devs decided to just cut content from the game instead of finding an interesting and fun solution. Like consequence. I'll say it again, consequence. It's a great realistic "concept".
While the game is still playable for those of us that never spent our money on Conclave I'm sure it's evident to anyone that new players to the game will have an even harder time getting into it. Not to mention that keeping your vassals super happy and supporting of your rule is impossible now. That's not necessarily a bad thing, except for the fact that without conclave there are no interesting decisions for players going through this process.
So to sum it up, if you're really going to buy this game, buy conclave as well because otherwise there is a huge chance you'll be disappointed and left wondering what dlc you're missing to make the game whole again.

Now before all of you whopping super duper review readers pin me down and hit my head with a bottle for sharing a different opinion about multiplayer. I'm going to say that this PC port is wonderful, and the way they created multiplayer is a truly fantastic idea for such a smaller community. Let me tell you the pros and cons of this game in my opinion, and why I believe you should play this game.
As a highly experienced player, with over 3000+ hours on it (It's literally the same game as the 360 console, with the exception of a different multiplayer lobby setup) I can say this is one of the most balanced games that has different leader powers and different ways to play such as UNSC/Covenant. While many believe that this is not true, there is no main meta character that people choose, as all seem to be equally important depending on the strategy at hand. No one can choose all 3 of the same person and win with ease.
Before you buy this game though, please realize that this is a smaller community, and that a lot of people on multiplayer are experienced individuals such as myself. Also, many, but not all, will be very mean once you have been defeated. I've experienced many times just due to my avatar. Come on Halo Wars community you're better than this.
Pros:
- Heavily Balanced Game
- Maps are diverse and unique
- Community does help new players learn how to play (I help newer players and will create videos!)
- Amazing PC port, in which the game has not crashed even once for me!
- A unique multiplayer experience differing from Halo Wars Console Edition
- Campaign is quite the playthrough, and is definitely worth the money on it's own
- Automatic A.I. in skirmish that learns how you play, and is able to combat you forever. Never stops growing in difficulty
- Lots of lore about the halo universe, and an entirely different part of the UNSC you can only read
Cons:
- Multiplayer does allow experienced players and noobs to play together.
- Boosters using multiplayer acting like pros and being little hillbillies due to their meaningless boring rank
- Hawks.
- Game can be hard to get into at first.
Now, I'm going to go a little more in depth about multiplayer and kind of try and explain why I believe 343 chose this decision. Now that players are able to "host" their own multiplayer lobbies, it allows people to play the game-mode and map that they wish and open it up for any or all players to join. In many RTS games, you are already facing pros and forced to learn how to survive first hand. This is natural, especially for RTS games with such a lower population. Adding a matchmaking system with less than 10,000 people will end up in people never finding games. There's not many lobbies being hosted as is. The population is slowly increasing, however it won't be like when the game first came out. So the people who were expecting it to, are leaving a negative review about the matching skill system. However, I do believe ranks could define actual skill so players can know what kind of player they will be facing. There is no reason to deny that the current multiplayer setup is bad, however it is the best one for a game with such a small community. It allows many of the game-modes and maps to be played without the hassle of waiting on people for hours. A lobby is there, and people will most likely join. That's what's wonderful about this.
However, I do believe that the host should not be able to kick people from ranked games, and that a timer should be created in the lobby once it's full. It's ranked, why the hell is the host allowed to kick? Who even thought that was a great idea? Once people are known to be more skillful, they will just be kicked and struggle finding a lobby. I've been kicked out of over 50 games. heh.
Over-all the multiplayer setup is a smart move. It'll keep the small community active for a long time. I do truly believe this is the right step for reviving this game.
Well, that's all from me. Thank you for taking your time reading. If you want to learn more about the game, don't hesitate to add me or leave a comment!

Nearly no one is playing this game. (At my last check there was 454 players. How strange...)
This wouldn't be a problem if people were actually playing it, but as is, there's nobody playing a game that has very little replay value in the campaign mode after you've finished it once. And it's for this reason that I've requested a refund and am also not reccomending it. If you're thinking of getting this for the campaign and maybe to play Co-op then by all means go for it. But if you're after a new RTS and craving multiplayer, don't get it. It's dead on arrival.

Took me 9 hours to finish and find all collectibles and all Steam achievements. If you're used to this kind of game it might take even less, so maybe some people will probably think the game is too short.  Except for collectibles and achievements you probably won't play it more than once... However I see it as reading a short novel in a very interactive way. So if I'd pay for a book that would maybe take me 8 or 9 hours to read (and that I wouldn't read again too soon), why not pay for a game as fun as this one? I loved the story and how it unfolded.
The puzzles in the beginning are very easy, but later start getting harder. Since it's a short game I definitely don't recommend reading/watching walkthroughs. The feeling of accomplishment in a game like this one is important and puzzles ARE reasonable.
The only time I watched a walkthrough was in a part when I was sure there had to be a way to move a light beam and that that would help me find the solution, but I wasn't able to move it. I confirmed that that was the case and figured out by myself that I had to use the mouse (as when moving the camera) because of some probable incompatibility with the controller.
So, two hints (no spoilers) you might need that for me were not that obvious and got me stuck for a long while:
- Sometimes you have to get very near something to interact with it.
- If you use a controller, you might still need to use the mouse every now and then to move the camera and light beams.
Other than that, I got no issues with the game. The atmosphere reminds me of Grim Fandango, one of my favorite games of all times!
I strongly recommend this game.

Had this game on my Xbox 360 and didn't finish it, because it was on 3 DVD's and the third got broken.
I bought this game a couple of weeks ago and it couldn't run. Was very dissapointed  in Rockstar, because they obviously knew that a vast majority of people couldn't even see the start screen.
Today I found there was an unofficial fix by Nightbreed (all hail our lord and saviour). There are 4 registry files, the second one fixed the start-up bug.
Now let's talk about the game:
I've finished 2/3 of it on my 360, the story was something between Zodiac and True Detective (in hindsight). It's not GTA V, nor is it trying to be. You play a good cop who goes up the ranks in the LAPD. There are sporadic flashbacks that provide backstory for the main character and secondary ones that you meet as the plot progresses. You can still steal cars, but you can't pick up hookers. If you run someone over with your car, you'll get a penalty in your current case.
The main issue I read with the PC port is that the FPS is locked at 30 FPS. Currently, I'm able to switch to 60 FPS from the settings without 3rd party applications.
On max settings the visuals are pretty beautiful. At the beginning I was scared this 5 year old game would suffer, but if you have a good PC, the light effects and scenery are simply marvelous.
Another thing I need to point out -  LA Noire was one of the first games to feature face capture technology on all characters (which are  a lot by the way). A big part of gameplay is reading facial expressions, you can probably guess how much work they put into a technology which recently only Uncharted 4 can compete with.
There are a couple of different missions you'll encounter:
1. Find clues in a crime scene
2. Chase a shady fella through rooftops and kitchens
3. Interrogate witnesses/suspects
4. Gunfights (GTA style combat)
It was kind of underwhelming at first that you jump over obstacles and climb ladders automatically, but as the game progresses you will see why. Can't really speak about bugs yet, but I remember the 360 version to be totally bug free.
The game's soundtrack is a dark jazz experience few games have provided me (sava e gei). If you're not a conosieur of the Noir movie genre or those cult detective novels (pre-80s), this game is a gateway to a perfect world where there is no right or wrong.
I would recommend this game to anyone who liked: Indigo Prophecy, Heavy Rain, Wolf Among Us or any other story driven game that has a strong protagonist and excellent supporting cast.
As the recent unofficial fix made the game playable again, I hope more people will experience the magic that is LA Noire.

Coming from the same developers as R.U.S.E., Wargame: European Escalation may feel familiar in its large scale. Fully real-time, Wargame is a RTS game focusing on a fictional escalation of the Cold War into a full-scale war between NATO and the Warsaw Pact.
This game features zero base-building. Positioning (flanking, cover, ambushes) is everything: several well-placed infantry units in a forest can wreck enemy tanks, and a pair of hidden heavy tanks can tear up targets from long range. Deployment of units is handled with command points, gained through control of sectors.
The starting allocation of units is determined by your active deck- one deck for the NATO player, and one deck for the PACT player. Decks are expanded through Command Stars, gained through campaign progress and multiplayer EXP. New units, such as the T-80 tank or the ubiquitous M1 Abrams, are purchased with Command Stars.
The game is tough and has a steep learning curve, but few games are more satisfying to master.

Was it as good at the first? Personally speaking, not really. The game itself is graphically spectacular but the idiotic AI and the HUD elements are terrible. The old Metro had a reasonably basic HUD that felt 'in feature' with the game, it fitted in with your surroundings and looked like it was meant to be there. The new HUD looks like something from a space age arcade shoot'em'up and doesn't fit at all, takes a little getting used too. This coinsides with the weapon selection screens and upgrades, purchases etc. The old system was perfect, it looked good and fitted in well with the scenery. Now, suddenly, everyone and their mother is carring portable 'weapon slides on a train' where as you approach them to purchase a weapon or anything your greeted by the gun on a movable slide which, if you select the next weapon, slides out of the way to reveal another weapon like pages in a book. On the back of a train. Underground. In a warzone. Really?!
The battery charger in the original was a nice little feature, it served a purpose and you actually had to work at it to charge. The new one is annoying and pointless, 3 clicks and your fully charged. I know it seems daft to pick at a handful of clicks on a mouse, but it was a feature in the past game that added a level of depth and complexity and realism to the game. Now it's just, as I've mentioned, pointless and poignant.
The storyline is a bit bland as well, it's gone from being a first person shooter to first person 'stealth mode sneek past but knock out/kill everyone silently in the process' game. The parts where you interact with other people, enemies, are no longer combat areas but more like 'ammo supplies on legs' You can clear entire levels without firing a single shot and just pick up and collect all of the ammo along the way to trade later. The stealth aspect is poorly implemented where there are some areas where stealth is recommended but pointless because no sooner do you trigger the next main event, everything that you've just snuck past is alerted at the same time including what you've just triggered. Oh, and the weapons you've got are simply pointless anyway as you have to ram your way through clip after clip just to kill anything
The game reminds me a little of Doom 3 and it's 'monster closets'. You can now walk into an area and as soon as you see the little 'disc' image spinning away in the bottom corner of the screen you think, 'here we go again' and out pop some men or Nosaliases or watchmen or something. It gives the game away in it's entirety.
Also, the arena feel really dulls down the game. Since when, in 2033, did you ever walk into a MASSIVE 'arena' style area? It's a dead giveaway pretence that there's going to be some ugly boss fight. I actually don't remember boss fights in 2033, it was more consistent than anything which I liked. Boss fights are soo 1990 and died with the likes of Doom and such like.
I've hit the recommend button simply for the fact that it is the follow up story to Artyom after the missile attack and it was interesting to see what happens next. I'm glad however that I bought it for £8 on ebay as a gift rather than full price in the store because it simply isn't as enjoyable as the first.
Loved it, now please please bring Halo wars 2 to windows 7.

Had this game on my Xbox 360 and didn't finish it, because it was on 3 DVD's and the third got broken.
I bought this game a couple of weeks ago and it couldn't run. Was very dissapointed  in Rockstar, because they obviously knew that a vast majority of people couldn't even see the start screen.
Today I found there was an unofficial fix by Nightbreed (all hail our lord and saviour). There are 4 registry files, the second one fixed the start-up bug.
Now let's talk about the game:
I've finished 2/3 of it on my 360, the story was something between Zodiac and True Detective (in hindsight). It's not GTA V, nor is it trying to be. You play a good cop who goes up the ranks in the LAPD. There are sporadic flashbacks that provide backstory for the main character and secondary ones that you meet as the plot progresses. You can still steal cars, but you can't pick up hookers. If you run someone over with your car, you'll get a penalty in your current case.
The main issue I read with the PC port is that the FPS is locked at 30 FPS. Currently, I'm able to switch to 60 FPS from the settings without 3rd party applications.
On max settings the visuals are pretty beautiful. At the beginning I was scared this 5 year old game would suffer, but if you have a good PC, the light effects and scenery are simply marvelous.
Another thing I need to point out -  LA Noire was one of the first games to feature face capture technology on all characters (which are  a lot by the way). A big part of gameplay is reading facial expressions, you can probably guess how much work they put into a technology which recently only Uncharted 4 can compete with.
There are a couple of different missions you'll encounter:
1. Find clues in a crime scene
2. Chase a shady fella through rooftops and kitchens
3. Interrogate witnesses/suspects
4. Gunfights (GTA style combat)
It was kind of underwhelming at first that you jump over obstacles and climb ladders automatically, but as the game progresses you will see why. Can't really speak about bugs yet, but I remember the 360 version to be totally bug free.
The game's soundtrack is a dark jazz experience few games have provided me (sava e gei). If you're not a conosieur of the Noir movie genre or those cult detective novels (pre-80s), this game is a gateway to a perfect world where there is no right or wrong.
I would recommend this game to anyone who liked: Indigo Prophecy, Heavy Rain, Wolf Among Us or any other story driven game that has a strong protagonist and excellent supporting cast.
As the recent unofficial fix made the game playable again, I hope more people will experience the magic that is LA Noire.

Contrast is a 3D puzzle\platformer that takes place in a world full of magic, cabaret singers, and burlesque shows. It utilizes a 1920's 'French Noir Film' art style that is unlike any other game I've played. The character design is beautiful, the voice acting is amazing, and the jazzy soundtrack fits the world perfectly. I can't stress enough how much I love the look and feel of this game. Yet, I can't recommend it, which is particularly disappointing considering how much there is to like here.
You play as Dawn, a woman trapped between the worlds of light and darkness, and who cannot be seen by anyone except for a little girl named Didi. Didi's parents have broken up, and with the father out of the picture, her mother works at a nightclub to pay the bills. This, of course, means nobody is watching the little demon-spawn and it's up to Dawn to keep her out of trouble. Easier said than done, since she insists on roaming around the city at all hours of the night, refusing to listen to reason, and all you can do is enable her.
The entire game revolves around a shift mechanic that allows you to become a shadow, an ability you will need to solve puzzles and progress through the game. Adjusting light sources to cast shadows to interact with is this game's bread and butter, and you'll be doing a lot of it.
The problems with Contrast start almost immediately. While the puzzle mechanics are unique and interesting, they are a bit buggy, and simple platforming can be difficult with controls that don't feel tight or responsive. Dawn has a tendency to get stuck in the environment and other shadows as well. There are even a couple of places where dropping an object in the wrong spot could result in the player not being able to progress further, forcing them to load the last checkpoint.
Once the game defines the parameters on the first couple of puzzles, it doesn't change them up much and they can become repetitive fast, which really shouldn't happen in a game this short. Which brings me to the biggest issue Contrast faces. The entire game can be completed in under 3 hours, and the ending is exceedingly abrupt. All of these issues combined leaves me with a feeling that the game is unfinished. Almost as if Compulsion Games ran out of money for the title half-way through development. Obviously, I do not have firsthand knowledge that this is the case, but I can't shake the feeling that I'm playing an Early Access game, and not a full release.
Altogether, Contrast is a game that should have been a one-of-a-kind, beautiful experience. When a bad idea becomes a bad game, it's expected, but when something that starts off this amazing falls flat, it's all the more frustrating. I expected better, as did most gamers, and in the future I hope Compulsion learns from their mistakes, and releases games that shows us all what they're really capable of.

Warframe is a horde shooter RPG with a large number of creative weapons, abilities, and mission objectives. It is F2P with microtransactions, including the most well-done cosmetic system of any game I have personally played. It has fun, agile gameplay which other studios are only attempting to mimic with limited results, years after Warframe's release. It also has a creative and inspired storyline, albeit one that Digial Extremes purposely hides details of (to encourage player speculation). Additionally, for a game of this size, it is incredibly bug-free (except for the Jordas Verdict, ♥♥♥♥ that). However, this game is not without its flaws.
Again, the greatest strengths of Warframe are is its creativity and customizability, be it builds, choices of weapons, or cosmetic design, and its fluid movement and aiming system. Digital Extreme's work here is nothing short of incredible, and you'll have to play the game to understand what I mean.
My two flaws with the game revolve around enemies. Firstly, enemy design generally lacks depth. In the Grineer faction for example, a vast majority of normal units possess hitscan or homing weapons. To make the game interactive, DE adds an accuracy limit to enemies, causing them to miss more against faster-moving targets. I feel like this is a "band-aid" style of design and should simply be remedied by the introduction of enemies with non-hitscan attacks. Secondly, enemy power generally scales in an uncreative fashion similar to Diablo 3, where health, armor, and damage levels of the same enemy types simply increase towards infinity as you progress.
Lastly, there are multiple small flaws, such as the attainability of orokin catalysts for new players, or the inconsistency of no-scoping on a sniper rifle. I feel like these are small errors that should be made known to Digital Extremes and improved upon.
By and large though, this remains my favorite RPGs on steam and one of my favorite games of all time. With over 1.6k hours clocked into the game and over $1000 happily spent to support the game, I think it speaks for itself. Happy hunting!

CK2 is at its best when just going with the flow, making choices not because it's the strategically sound thing to do; it makes sense that your lunatic ruler would dump all the salt he could into the mead.
Strongly supported not only by its fervent community but also Paradox Studios themselves (aside from the cash-grabbing DLC), CK2 is probably the most acessible and possibly best grand strategy title from the studio to date.

Lumino City is a great puzzle game.
It provides a fairly expansive environment to explore, with a wealth of puzzles to solve, and the great thing is: They're actually puzzles. This isn't just some "run around until you can find the item that you need to progress, then combine them in just the right way" type of game. The tools you need are provided in each scene of the game, and you are left with a puzzle that you need to solve in order to progress.
The puzzles themselves range from fairly easy, fitting cogs onto a board in the right way, to fairly tricky puzzles requiring  logic. All of them (bar one, in my case) were solvable without resorting to trial and error until the solution was found, which is a good thing in a puzzle game like this. There is also an in-game help book that can give you hints if you're stuck, without giving too much of the solution away.
A big strength of this game is the art. The visuals were actually created in real life, then photographed into the game, which gives it a really unique look that I haven't seen much of elsewhere. This coupled with the great sound and music design make for a very nice play through experience. The writing of the story is also very good, with a lot of humorous elements combined with some more sincere ones, it adds a lot to the characters of the City.
My one (and only) major gripe with the game is that there are parts of the game where you can solve a 'scene' in different orders. Say there are 3 puzzles. If you solve it in the order with the third last everything is fine. But there are cases where, if you solve the third puzzle first, the game either refuses to let you progress or it simply crashes on you. You then have to resort to the forums to see what exactly the 'correct' solution is.
Aside from that, this is a very good game if you like actual puzzles without all of the running around aimlessly looking for the solution, and it just looks and feels great.

Awesome game! I'd give it a 7 despite it's awesomeness, but only after I really try to reflect on this game's weaknesses.
1) (Time flow)
One thing I dislike is how time flows so quickly in this game. Like you could literally waste more than a day making videos without noticing.
2) (Team/Staff Management)
Another thing I dislike or rather something that I hope would be a feature in the game is team management. What I mean by this is this:
a) When I hire a collaborator and tell them to make videos, apparently they are the ones IN the video. Like how does this make sense? If that is so then I am more a PRODUCER than a PERFORMER. This means I'm trying to make a Studio and I'm not trying to. I'm not saying this feature should be removed, but perhaps you guys should consider giving the players options to be a self-employed youtuber or the head of a company.
b) A continuation to my previous argument. If, hypothetically speaking, I want to hire someone to my team, I would like to have a feature where they have their own specializations. For example: Editor, Cameraman, Producer, Writer, etc. This way, I can just record and then leave it to my team as I want to have a life outside of youtube too, you know? I don't like the idea of having SOMEONE ELSE playing video games and upload it to my fans, that's just wrong...
c) ONE MORE THING: I noticed that u can befriend the top youtubers and ask them to "collaborate " with you, which makes no sense at all. Of course the collaboration ii mean is the part where you hire them as a team collaborator and not having a feature guest.
3. (Views and Subscribers)
So in this game, after you publish a video, you have to wait for a period of time before the video reaches its "peak" and then we receive the rewards from that. But a thing that bothers me is that, not all the views (in real life not in this game) are received within a set period of time. Some may take more than a couple months to reach its peak. Additionally, don't you think that the views keeps on growing even after the said "peak"? I don't know about you, but I do watch the same videos again after some time, plus, not all subscribers watch your videos right after u upload it. This is especially true for music videos since you won't be viewing it just once.
4. (Viral Videos)
Are there any possibilities of making a "hit viral video"? Some channels grow over time rather steadily like the #1 youtuber right now without having viral hits. While some channels are more known for those hit videos, where they can receive 2-5 times than their average videos, and then all of a sudden they get tons and tons of subscribers. I just feel like this should be a feature to the game, being able to hit a viral video.
5. (Video Editing and Recording Session)
If you've played the game, then you'd be familiar with the recording mechanics and I'd like to believe you have the same problem as me. 90% OF THE TIME, I NEVER EVEN GOT TO THE LAST PART WHICH IS THE ENDING. so 90% of my videos are actually without outros, some might not even be "finished" per se. This should be fixed man, and I think giving us the option to skip the events without waiting 15+ secs is a good idea; because again, 15 secs in our world is like 5 hours in the game! that's too unbalanced.
6. JUST A PERSONAL COMMENT: (Money)
Another thing that bothers me is how much money we receive from videos. I know money is a bit of a controversial subject but I get around 4k if a video gets around 2M views. I feel like this doesn't make any sense, because there are channels which uploads just around once a week and I don't believe that they only make ~200k/year. Moreover, channels that uploads once a week are usually channels that requires some work like comedy sketches, and as generally known, these channels requires A LOT of team members, so that 200k will be split again. Although it's true that we do not know how much money youtube gives us in real life, it still feels like an understatement when u only get ~200k a year or 16k a month or 4k for every 2m views.
I personally recommend the readers of my review to only take 50% of what I say to sleep, because I know I might be rambling too much. However, I'm just putting to text what I believe is lacking in the game. Whether it is deemed essential to the game or not, its up to the devs.
Now, I know that there are still other types of channels yet to be updated such as cooking, lifestyle, music etc. So I think that this game still have so much potential to grow. But as of now, I'm giving it a 7/10.

By and large, one of the most interesting games I've played for a long while. Instead of the classic reliance on violence, explosions, car chases, bullet time and skimpily clad anime girls, this game 'ACTUALLY' does what it set out to do, and did it rather well considering just how difficult it must've been to release this in the way it was intended; as a detective simulator.
The game has 3 styles in one: Interrogation/Interviewing , Open World Transportation , Crime Scene Investigation.
Open World Transportation is rather simple...You drive around in your 1950s or something automobile copcar, with your partner whose usually a complete♥♥♥♥♥♥ And you go from place to place depending on where the case takes you, be it a gunshop, a grieving widows home, an axe murderers back yard, or the filthy hard drive of a delusional waifu hunter weeaboo's hard drive(Not really).
Crime Scene Investigation is part 2 to Open World Transportation. You arrive at the crime scene, and you wobble around the place looking for clues, such as bloody hand guns, Newspaper clippings, bullet casings, or used condoms with banana flavor (Not really).
Interrogation/Interviewing is the selling part of the whole game, and obviously where the most time and effort was dumped in. The faces of the characters in the game were enchanced with live-action motion mapping of an actual actor's face, to help one determine what they're thinking. It makes tell-tale characteristics, like fidget eyes, a nervous lip twitch, or even something subtle like a quivering eyebrow, more evident and easy to determine. In this way, the game went above and beyond, and really makes the process of deciding whether someone is telling the truth or lying, a treat.
The graphics are hard to determine in a singular way due to the fact that the developpers have been so picky-choosey with what they focus their attention and effort on. For example, buildings are pretty damned bare-bones. You don't really look at the wall texture and go "THIS IS AMAZING", as they never really stand out enough for you to even notice them. They're just there. Cars and bodies are a little bit better, although movement and shooting a hand gun still looks rather robotic and unnatural. Meanwhile, the faces are a whole different level of quality and attention to detail, which honestly looks a bit weird and kind of crappy when you think about it. Crappy everything else, except for the faces which are smooth and perfect in every way?....Talk about playing favorites guys, jeez, at least TRY to make it less painfully obvious next time.
All in all, the game's fun, and you'll get tons of hours of fun out of it if you're into detective work and such, but don't be super impressed by the game's execution as a whole. Take it for what it is, a detective simulator. It's not Grand Theft Auto, and don't expect it to be.

This game needs love, and this game needs more of a community, but sadly that probably won't happen.

A fantastic objective based game based on William Gibsons Neuromancer,easily one of the best FPS games out there.
Each map has a side defending and one attacking.There are objectives that members of each team must fufill in order to advance their spawn points,and some may even be taken back and forth.
An understanding of how cyberspace and meatspace reflect on each other is important as well.Deckers(hackers) can jack in to Jack In Points,bringing them to control of their cyberspace avatar which has health equal to the deckers energy pool.Attacks/getting attacked in cyberspace drains your energy pool faster,and getting forcibly ejected is somewhat harmful.
The deckers main objective is to navigate cyberspace and to open doors,toggle defense turrets,and set off traps in meatspace so their team can advance,or prevent the enemy from doing so.
Implants are customizeable and more implant space is available to the lighter classes.These are essentially superpowers like Stealth,Silencer,AoE Health Regen,Sound Wave Triangulator(see footsteps through walls),Superjump,Cyberdeck for Decking,etc and really add a nice spice to the game.Its also fun to jump onto a deckers head while hes hacking,and superjump his head into the pavement.
That said,the combat is brutal and intense,with unique and creative weapons like the Tesla Rifle,the formidable Basilisk,or my personal favorite the Smartlocks. The maps are well thought out and have high replay value.
Thats why,in my personal opinion,Dystopia is a game that should have been included in the Orange Box,and does not get enough press for how fantastic it is.

The idea of using shadows as platforms is an interesting one; shifting your character back and forth between shadow and light adds new variety. The 3 hours of gameplay doesn't allow enough time for this idea to evolve. Most "puzzles" end up being nothing more than jump - shift - jump - shift. To make matters worse, platforming is a bit clunky. I felt like my character was alittle too big for the world. Missing an easy jump and falling to your death is infuriating, but the game is really forgiving, almost always reloading near the last jump. The main plot, although nothing more than a mellowdrama, hid behind it the more interesting subplot of the player's identity. This, sadly, is only hinted at in clues in the environment and pointless 'collectables'. Then the game ends, not really concluding anything, even the main plot.  I really wanted to like Contrast, but there isn't enough of a game here to recommend to anyone.

I did not play the previous game Lume and I still enjoyed this game very much. I recommend it. There is not any part of it that I think is 100% negative, so I have elements set in "positive" and "Half and half."
POSITIVE:
THE PUZZLES: There is a nice variety of puzzles. They are all different and some of them are pretty unique. I just wish there were a few more.
THE ENVIRONMENT: The city is hand made and filmed, so it is like you are playing in a real place. It looks great! It is also a highly ineresting and unique place to expore.
Additionally, as you explore and find things, there is some stuff lying around that you do not need but adds a lot to the game. It can tell explain some of what is going on and/or provide some great humor. This subtle humor reminds me a lot of the type you find around the enviroments of the Portal games. Very funny.
The PUZZLES and the ENVIRONMENT also connect. The environment is often a part of a puzzle or is the puzzle. And things you need do not necissarily stand out, so you actually solve the puzzles yourself. No hand holding, unless you use the manual included in the game.

Great little adventure/p&c click indie gem. Good puzzles, unique and amazing artstyle, fitting and relaxing music.
I'm a point & click veteran and I can't praise this game enough. It had everything it needed plus more.
Let's start with the puzzles (most important part imo): They are logical (you don't have to jump through idiotic hoops to solve them), they are not too easy but also not too hard. Overall you get the same difficulty level throughout the game.
The art is amazing. It's some mixture of props and computer animation. While I've seen this before, I have to say it's done extremly well in Lumino City, while also fitting it's world. The lovely atmosphere is underlined by the relaxing music.
The plus(ses): Contrary to most puzzle/adventure games this game runs without a direct hint/help system. At the beginning you find a book that includes solutions/hints for the main puzzles. The crux of the matter is that you can only access them by solving another puzzle/math problem. The restricted accessibility encourages you to give it another try while it doesn't destroy the mood by giving solutions too willingly. Imo a great trade-off, done superiorly to any game I've seen before.
Great gaming experience. Hard to explain, but the game comes with a lovely atmosphere and great puzzles that never pull you out of the fluid/smooth experience. The only time I came across something similar was in Brothers: A Tale of Two Sons.
Ending thoughts: This game is mostly about it's puzzles, so you shouldn't expect too much character/story wise. Little girl solves puzzles to find her grandpa, that's mostly it (you also run into characters with side stories but nothing too big). There are end credits that also give you more of a background. Overall the game ran pretty well on my system (win7 64bit) and I ran into no bugs or crashes (feb '16).  Only thing I've noticed was the (partly) juddery end credits.

Amazing Classic. Never played much detective games so story driven like L.A. Noire but this was my very first. Glad I played it....
But the frustrating optimization issues, lag, refusal to launch issues is really what degrades this masterpiece from receiving a good review. I ended up not finishing the game because it doesn't want to start anymore. Great.
Pros:
- Highly immersive
- Very story driven with a 1950s theme
- Enjoyable arcadic detective gameplay
- Free Roaming L.A.
- Dramatic cutscenes (movie-like)
- Life-like facial animation & expressions
- Diverse & influencial characters
- 1080p support (for an old game this is a huge plus so thx for doing this)
- Engaging cases
Cons:
- Very poorly optimized (Newer OS struggle to run this game properly in its locked 29.97 fps)
- Refuses to launch (for reasons unknown to this day I can no longer get the game to load)
- Not made to be played in PC port (clearly designed for consoles)
- Doesn't take advantage of multithreads/unable to run directx11 (stuck with directx9)
- Have to spend too much time tweaking/finding fixes just to make the game work smoothly
- Unrealistic driving
- Forced to listen to copyrighted music (no option to turn off radio music or a way to separate game music from 3rd party music)
- Interrogations limited to 3 options only. Feels dumbed down
- Sometimes facial expression cues don't match with their previous statement, leading to a misunderstood decision during interrogations.

Best spin on RTS gaming I've played in a while.
Think of this game as a sort of "Total War: Cold War Gone Hot"
Since tastes greatly differ, I'll just list some points here that stood out to me in comparison to standard-fare RTS games.
> No base building
> Very little micro-ing on unit-level
> Focus on tactical placement/cover
> Huge(!) selection of military gear
> Huge armies
> Huge maps
> Easy to learn, hard to master
> Strong focus on multiplayer
Pro:
+ Good, fluid controls/UI/camera control
+ Good visuals, good sound
+ Good performance
+ Excellent zoom levels/transitions
+ Satisfactory impact of weapons
+ Autonomous units act clever most of the time
+ Good pacing of gameplay
+ Multiplayer is fun even for beginners
Con:
- Campaign is a bit short
- Campaign difficulty can be a bit hard for new players
- Unit placement in cover _can_ be a tiny bit fiddly at rare times
- Not much handholding/tutorial help (lrn2play, nub :P)
- Music is a bit weak, but not grating
I'm loving it!

Played this when it first came out. Enjoyed it immensely at the time and was my first RTS. They released it with better visuals and all the content it had for $20? ON PC?? Hell yes! I believed I would enjoy it as much as I had originally, but to my disappointment. I've played many games since then, obviously. I'm older now and my tastes have refined. I don't remember how it played exactly, but I suppose my expectations have gone above what the game can do now.
1) Camera. I'm accustomed to camera views such as seen in the Total War line up. I can see my entire army from a high vantage point and react accordingly to any enemy movement. Not so with this, for obvious reasons. My memory of the camera view is higher than what the game currently has. Entirely my fault.
2) UI. When I hard group units, I can't see the group, let alone the type and number of units in the group. We have the ability to group our units, but not see them? It becomes tedious having to press each group key each time I have casualties. Group 1: No casualties. Group 2: 1 unit dead. Group 3: 1 unit dead, 2 wounded. Replace dead units in 2 &3. Rinse and repeat for further dead units and groups.
3) This is what♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥me off rather than just being irksome. Units going off to fight on their own. They don't stay where I wish them to. I want some soldiers to stay in the back to watch the flanks, but still remain in firing range of the frontliners. Won't happen. They all clump up in one area trying to kill a pack of Grunts.
I know I haven't played the PC port much, but just these issues leads me to believe I won't be able to accept them as just part of the game. I'd rather just delete a game to save space than be frustrated. It's not my cup of tea. Unfortunately, there is only Like/Dislike, no in-between. I'd give this a "meh" because I did derive some enjoyment from the overall gameplay.

TL;DR: Check it out.
THE GOOD:
• Gameplay:  Contrast is a truly unique concept; I can't think of anything that does something similar: shifting from a 3D environment to a 2D one using the shadows on the wall.  Shadows can sometimes be manipulated by moving light sources.  It's neat!
• Story:  The story isn't masterfully told, but it is an interesting one, and I'm glad I stuck around to see it through to the end.
• Art:  Contrast is beautiful to admire and its music is always a pleasant companion.
• It's Indie!:  Support your local indie game developer!  Especially when they're doing awesome work like this!
THE BAD:
• Game Feel:  As cool as traversing the shadows as a platformer is, Contrast has a tendency to be real finicky.  On some puzzles, I would get so frustrated falling out of the shadows, I would question if I was performing the task correctly; in every case, I was.  It becomes easy to slip out from the 2D world and fall to your death, and not even be sure why it happened.  I managed to finish every puzzle, but I would have had a lot more fun if the mechanics had been fine-tuned a bit more.
• Acting:  The voice acting could've been a little more convincing, but--  Ehh! What'r'ya gonna do?

First review I've ever actually felt compelled to write.  I enjoyed this game thoroughly for the 17 hours I played it, but it's definitely not for everyone....including me.  This is a true survival MMO; it's not fast-paced and there's some serious grinding, but instead of grinding quests and killing goblins, you're farming stones and wood, killing for food, building a shelter, expanding your technology, etc.
In my first day playing, I logged 9-hours of gameplay.  Over the next week, I'd log on and build my base, slowly creating an extremely small camp with a wood hut, a cage, and a small fenced in area where I built a campfire and some other things. My character was up to level 37.  Then I log on and found some guy who was level 284 wiped my entire camp and stole all my stuff.  I get that this is part of the game, but that's why I said; this game is definitely not for everyone...including me.
There needs to be some balance to the PVP and grinding aspects of the game.  If you play single-player, the game simply isn't enjoyable in many ways because it's extremely slow paced and systematic; you completely lose any sense of urgency or need for awareness.  If you play on the official servers, you can spend half a weekend and a few nights of grinding only to be wiped out while you were gone and against someone you'd have no shot against anyway.
I might try it again, but I've never been so turned off by a game so quickly.

I was very disappointed with this game. I wouldn't say it's bad, but pretty much everything felt underwhelming or out of place. You would think that in a puzzle platformer the platforming would be really fleshed out and feel good, but in reality it's super clunky. Even the 2d bits once you enter the shadows feel bad and bugy. The dashing ability makes no sense. Why would the players character be able to do that. Maybe if it was just for platforming and mobility, but you are braking fences with that ability. It's just silly. Same goes for the players ability to carry big boxes like they are made of cardboard. As game mechanics they are fine, but they don't feel right in the games world.
Considering the length of the game I think it could have benefited form just flushing out the basic platforming and shadow stuff and leaving out all the other tiny mechanics. In my mind having a solid platformer with a shadow gimmick would be much better,  than a clunky platformer with a bunch of flimsy mechanics that are used only handful of moments in the game. Moving objects to manipulate shadows was very interesting, but again, it was used only two times in the game and wasn't all that sophisticated. It would be so cool if the game had a bigger emphasis on this aspect.
The story is nothing special either. It's very simplistic. I really didn't care about it. It was frustrating that the mystery of why only the players character and Didi have physical bodies is addressed only at the very end of the game.
The only positive aspect of the game is its aesthetic. The Art Deco/cabaret stile is relay cool. And some of the level design visually is very interesting. Though I was a bit disappointed that in a game about shadows the shadows them selves ware a bit ugly at places.
In conclusion - get it on sale if the screenshots look really tempting to you, but stay away if you want super tight gameplay.
