Warframe is definitely a game worth checking out because the game design and gameplay is so different from most other games. Warframe at its core is a looter game. The end game is basically grinding for prime loot (a.k.a. legendary loot in other games). I personally don't care about the best loot so grinding for the best loot is not why I play this game. I play it because it's a fun game to play with friends and most importantly it keeps getting major updates.
When most developers add 'expansions' to their game it's usually just new areas and bosses. They never try out new things because they never know if players like it, so they just use the same old tired formula for expansions for years (sometimes even decades). That's where Warframe developers shine. They take risks, they add new things to the game and they truly try to expand the game not just add the same content over and over again. That imo makes Warframe really fun because you never truly know what the future updates will add to the game.
Now to pros on cons:
Pros:
-It's not a P2W game
-Major updates
-Fun with friends
-Character/weapon customization (a.k.a. Fashionframe)
-Complex Weapon modding
-Lots of weapons and warframes with a lot variety
-Good graphics, audio, visuals and voice acting.
Cons:
-Terrible new player experience. I had to google over 90% of the things I know about the game today.
-The lore and story is great but the way the story and lore is presented is imo terrible. Too much exposition in a story can be bad but if there's basically none.. then it's even worse. Too much of Warframes story feels mysterious and unknown and that doesn't fit into a sci-fi game like Warframe imo.
-Bad colliders. There's a lot of jumping in this game so I get stuck on doorframes all the time. I want to go through the door not stand on the doorframe. Hopefully they fix that problem in the future.
-In-game currency is overpriced so it's only worth buying if you get -75% discount token in the game through daily login rewards.
At the end of day all I can say is that it's definitely worth checking out. Even if you don't end up liking the game you still get to experience something pretty unique.

I really do have to say that WARFRAME, aesthetically, is one of the best games I've ever played. So many things that are so...aesthetically unique in WARFRAME, from the guns, swords, equipment, maps, factions, and enemies. They all look so different from other games, it fascinates me IMMENSELY. I especially like the GRINEER and their aesthetics, just the industrial, gritty, messy and dirty look to them, GRINEER is probably one of the things that really keep me hooked into WARFRAME! The shapes and designs of WARFRAME are very dynamic and artistic, it's just...great!
Ofc, gameplay, it's rather pretty good, you shoot, you kill, you hack and slash, you slide and jump from point A to point B, finish objectives and so on and so on. Things get a bit too fast sometimes but of course, WARFRAME is a very fast paced game and I can't really complain about it.
Though I honestly don't know if it's one of those games that is the most fun when played with friends...in my perspective anyway. Like I mean friends like talking through voice chat and stuff, not just Public matchmaking random players and such. Warframe is very fast and most of the times, you're gonna be going everywhere, doing your own thing and such, everyone will. It's not an entirely hard game.
When you get to a certain point in the game, things are pretty darn automatic for you and yeah. It isn't like Overwatch or anything where communication is quite crucial if you really want to win a game. Warframe isn't really like that, everyone is pretty much independent and can handle themselves alone, as far as I know. For a lot of the cases, there isn't really a point in....grouping up with your squad...if you can because it's really hard, most of the times, you really can't stand still.
Of course, that ain't really the ONLY case in WARFRAME haha, but I'll let people figure that out when they get to that.
And yeah, the GRIND is REAL. That's a pretty core part of Warframe and a lot of people know that so yeah.
So...YEAH! I recommend this game but eh, you do you. I do have to say that AESTHETICALLY!? Warframe is very unique and beautiful. Without its awesome aesthetics, I don't think I'd have gotten 2k3 hours into the game!

I love this game so much that I find it an insult it's only rated 93%.
What can I say? It's one of those games that you can just sit back, relax and get lost in.
Gameplay:
You're basically on a linear path to find your grandpa and there are tons of puzzles along that you need to solve to move forward. The puzzles have been implemented seamlessly into the story which gives you a very satisfying feeling when you complete a section. That said, some of the puzzles can be a little cryptic or just damn make no sense, luckily you have a handy little book that helps you along the way if you get stuck.
Music:
Music is a huge part of this game. I'm not one of those people who pays too much attention to game music but when it's there I really appreciate it. Lumino City has some of the best music I've ever come across from any game. Not only is it pleasing to the ear, it matches the mood of whatever is going on in the game - sometimes even syncing to the games sound effects. Make sure to play this on a device that is capable of delivering good quality bass.
Art:
The artwork looks like it's all been done by hand and painstakingly animated into the game. A lot of love and attention has clearly gone into creating the visuals and I have to say they've come out perfect. All in all It looks unlike any game I've seen before, a true work of art.
Conclusion;
I recommend this game to anyone who likes a bit of puzzle solving. Five minutes in and you'll be hooked.
Something that I haven't seen mentioned a lot is the game's ability to recover from a crash. I'm not saying the game crashes a lot, because it doesn't (at least for me), but when it does crash, it brings you back to exactly where you were before. It basically constantly autosaves so you will never end up doing the same thing twice.
There is one thing that does bug me about the game though, I wish it gave you the option to choose the speed in which you read the dialogue.  Although it gives you more than enough time to read before moving on, you end up missing some stuff because you may have been distracted for a second.
Please note that I've played this game for a lot more hours than it says up there. I played it before at a friend's house and nearly finished it so I decided to get it myself.

This is really good for an early access game, this review will reflect just that; Early Access.
I found out that I suddenly had sunk ~20 hours into this game, which ironically is one of this games biggest flaws at this stage; Time.
You are given a bunch of tasks, and a very short time in which to complete them. When the ingame-clock progresses when you're in menus, changing clothes or creating videos, this makes you feel like you have to be on your toes every split-second. Before you know it, an in-game week has passed and you were nowhere near able to complete the tasks you were given, seeing as you in that time also need to sleep, eat, work and study.
It gets a little better once you can afford hiring collaborators to make videos for you, but when you yourself decide to chip in (afterall, you are the big cahuna), it feels like the in-game clock discourages you to do so. Because while you are editing, picking clips to use and putting them together, time still runs and you cannot upload your collabs videos until you're done yourself.
This game still has a ways to go to iron out some minor flaws, but it's definately worth checking out. If the above seems discouraging, try once the game has been released.

Neolithic survival game Ark: Survival Evolved. The epic combination of PVP and survival aspects put together to make one of possibly the greatest survival games of all times... Are you up for the challenge?
When I say challenge, I don't mean it sarcastically or light heartedly, this game is challenging in all aspects. You may have already read the reviews from those with 5000 hours plus. The game is difficult, demanding, and downright brutal most of the time. It would be a lie if I said I hadn't bought the game and was questioning my sanity at the one hour and fifty five minute mark, the ledge before I could get my money back. Im happy to say that I did not refund this game and have never regretted it. There have been times that I have alt - F4'd out and been angry at the spawn killing dinos, out of losing hours of work on a base a T-Rex decided to demolish, or a slew of other aspects in the game that can ruin your experience, but I regret none of them.
At the end of the day when you buy and play a game, you have to ask yourself is it worth the money. The simple way is to say how many hours of gameplay did you get out of it. If you pay $60 for a game and only play 3 or 4 hours, its a waste. But paying $30 for countless hours of content, exploration, gameplay features and content, you have to say its damn worth it.
I will say what you have probably read dozens of times already, the multiplayer is a brutal, unforgiving challenge that will demand hours of your time if you want to ever be good. It will demand that you sell your real life body and mind to a tribe for hours of grinding labor to prove your loyalty to a Alpha tribe to let you in. At its core, Ark is like Rust, Dayz, and so many other survival games. 99% of the game is grinding, collecting resources, exploring, and so on. The 1% is hardly what anyone can call PVP. PVP requires a shootout, or actual player on player interaction. Ark does not offer this, what it offers is a fatally flawed system like every other game that includes persistant worlds and base building, offline raiding. A smoking crator of what was once your pride and joy will await you as you reconnect. If you are lucky, you will sometimes get to be the person who makes the crator, but thats all online play really is.
Singleplayer or COOP with a group of friends offers the greatness of Ark as it was intended to be. The maps all offer countless hours of gameplay. The hours I have logged at writing this (42 hours) are all on one single map as of now (Ragnarok). If playing with friends to explore and take over a world in which you are the only tribe doesn't appeal to you, I suggest you take a good look at what the game has to offer and what I mentioned above, as that is what awaits you in this game. At it's core, this game is about survival, exploration, and resource gathering. To me, PVP was a natural part of the game as well, but has morphed into a horrible mess that is what I described earlier. Offline raiding is rampant and can't be blamed as it is the easiest method to kill another tribe.
The singleplayer value of this game alone is worth the price. The multiplayer in my opinion is cancerous, but extra bang for your buck. It's a decent game with a lot of single player value to it that earns it's price in hours of gameplay.

The end game is basically grinding for prime loot (a.k.a. legendary loot in other games). I personally don't care about the best loot so grinding for the best loot is not why I play this game. I play it because it's a fun game to play with friends and most importantly it keeps getting major updates.
When most developers add 'expansions' to their game it's usually just new areas and bosses. They never try out new things because they never know if players like it, so they just use the same old tired formula for expansions for years (sometimes even decades). That's where Warframe developers shine. They take risks, they add new things to the game and they truly try to expand the game not just add the same content over and over again. That imo makes Warframe really fun because you never truly know what the future updates will add to the game.
Now to pros on cons:
Pros:
-It's not a P2W game
-Major updates
-Fun with friends
-Character/weapon customization (a.k.a. Fashionframe)
-Complex Weapon modding
-Lots of weapons and warframes with a lot variety
-Good graphics, audio, visuals and voice acting.
Cons:
-Terrible new player experience. I had to google over 90% of the things I know about the game today.
-The lore and story is great but the way the story and lore is presented is imo terrible. Too much exposition in a story can be bad but if there's basically none.. then it's even worse. Too much of Warframes story feels mysterious and unknown and that doesn't fit into a sci-fi game like Warframe imo.
-Bad colliders. There's a lot of jumping in this game so I get stuck on doorframes all the time. I want to go through the door not stand on the doorframe. Hopefully they fix that problem in the future.
-In-game currency is overpriced so it's only worth buying if you get -75% discount token in the game through daily login rewards.
At the end of day all I can say is that it's definitely worth checking out. Even if you don't end up liking the game you still get to experience something pretty unique.

A special gaming experience.
The 2 Metro games are not ordinary shooters. They have great story, they are atmospheric as hell and they are very immersive. Both of the games have good and bad endings, and the good one is obtainable only if you interact with the world: listen to people, help them, explore the areas and sparing enemies life using stealth where it is possible. I personally don't play with shooters however enjoyed every moment of these games. The experience of gaming was unique. If you don't want to pick both of them, definitely take Last Light though. Metro 2033 (I played with the redux) in overall a  more difficult experience where every level needs to be completed with a different strategy. The gameplay is fantastic and also cruel sometimes but the story is not that great, the game is more a puristic, old school experience. Last Light however has a great, complex story with fantastic storytelling. The gameplay is a slightly more casual, more arcade style, but the storytelling which makes it better than it's predecessor. Also Last Light is quiet difficult though, running and shooting is not enough. You need to explore and scavange corpses, bags, boxes for bullets, air filters and medikit in order to survive and sometimes you will definitely feel that you fight for survive. You will be frustrated a lot, but you will get tons of enjoyment at the same time.
However there are some issues with the game: it has some annoying bugs. They start to appear at a certain level (Bandits). In my first playthrough at this level the game crashed constantly, so I couldn't continue. I needed to restart the chapter and the game worked fine afterwards. On my second playtrough from the same level the stealthy kill/knock out didn't work anymore. Which is frustrating because for good ending the pacifist playthrough is necessary, but with this bug it will be impossible probably. And also the stealthy approach is one of the strongest aspect of the game, so without this the experience is not so complete.
But even with the annoying bugs still recommend the game, because it's a classic.

BIOSHOCK 2 - REMASTERED
Bioshock 2 may not be the most thought-provoking game in the series and was a product i didnt really care for . Being developed by 2k marin whilst irrational games worked on the next big bioshock entry this game was used to bridge the gap between the long development cycle . So is bioshock 2 as low as the oceans floor lets find out .
1. Settings and options ( including controls )
If you thought Bioshock 1 was sparse for it's settings and customizable controls then Bioshock 2 take's the Adam . You have a total of FIVE graphical settings among them are Windowed mode , Vertical Sync , Antallasing and topping them off are the resolution slider which goes up to 4k and Anisotropic Flitering which maxes out at 16x . As far as tinkering the controller settings to your personal preference we have a small amount of input with a total of only FOUR settings these range from controller sensitivity , inverted look and ending with vibration support and use the gamepad. Its suprising that they didn't add any new graphic options given the fact the base game was released in 2010.
2. Gameplay and Graphics
If Bioshock 1 was a test in human endurance and psychological horror , Always peaking around the next corridor in search of the unknown , checking ceilings and creaking floorboards as you methodically trudged through the decaying ruins of a utopia gone wrong with a study in due diligence then Bioshock 2 is the Cod of the sea . Bioshock 2 is a straight up action game you find weapons quickly blast though enemies and sit through set pieces . At points its bombastic throwing more enemies at you at a frantic rate and can become monotous at times the predictability factor can reach such dazzling heights you would think your a psychic . As for gameplay does it hold up, well Arkane studios helped out with its development cycle the guys behind dishonoured and digital extremes also put their two cents in so you would think the answer would be yes . But sadly the answer is no though rose tinted glasses i remembered the combat and movement being a lot more fast paced and chaotic but in reality it comes across as clunky . But what's a game without its graphics , How to they fair well Bioshock 2 might of had the most spit and polish in this collection as we see a notable difference from our previous entry its not massive changes like other remaster's on this list but very tiny small changes like lighting and scratches on the weapon's you gather thoughout the world , Scratches on weapons being industry speak for '' We improved the game by adding this little texture '' other than that nothing is really changed which adds to my theory that this is a HD collection masquerading as a remaster
3. Story
If you haven't played Bioshock 2 and are reading this review you are probably asking yourself what the heck is the story well without spoilers the story goes like this . Two years prior to Jack's soggy adventure you play as subject delta a big daddy with a huge drill ( not an innuendo) after a series of events your little sister is taking from you by meryl streep lookalike sofia lamb a clinical psychiatrist who claims the sister belongs to her. The one thing bioshock 2 does right is switching the sexes round , Bioshock 1 nearly all of the antagonists were male and in this secord game nearly all of the bad guys are replaced by bad girls which i feel is very progressive in this industry . Anyway's back to the story after a cracking headache you awake to get your little sister back all the while having flashbacks of a girl and being stalked by a new threat the big sister.
4. Added Extras and DLC
Some things have been missed out of this game making it feel barren and not the complete bioshock 2 experience . This watered down version of bioshock 2 leaves out the vast MULTIPLAYER component found in the original. A fun and hectic game to play with a variety of game modes and customizable options for you to tailor your character its been the inspiration for many other single-player games with tacked on multiplayer components and in my personal opinion was probably the best part of the second game . There was nothing more scarier than capturing a flag just to hear the howls of a player who found the big daddy suit the balancing was perfect and came with a large collection of maps to mess around in also it gave a welcome change from the loneliness of Rapture and swapped it out for rewarding team-play and ingenuity . However what is included is the two DLC packs they are as follows the protector trials similar to the trials found in Bioshock 1 is a collection of challenges with the plot centring on harvesting as much adam as possible. And finally we have Mlnervas den bioshocks 2's well received expansion which tells the twisted tale of charles porter.
5. summary
Missing a lot of what made Bioshock 2 a great game the remaster does very little to warren a glance .Rapture isn't the only thing decaying at the bottom of the abyss so does the lack of effort that went into the remastered collection and that's the real shame here . As far as the games go Bioshock is still one of the most respected shooter out there with a Fantastic story , perfect voice acting and balanced gameplay making for an exciting thrill ride experience from start to finish but the remaster might as well of been constructed by actual blind squirrels because there's nothing that says this is what bioshock would look like if it was released today.

This is really good for an early access game, this review will reflect just that; Early Access.
I found out that I suddenly had sunk ~20 hours into this game, which ironically is one of this games biggest flaws at this stage; Time.
You are given a bunch of tasks, and a very short time in which to complete them. When the ingame-clock progresses when you're in menus, changing clothes or creating videos, this makes you feel like you have to be on your toes every split-second. Before you know it, an in-game week has passed and you were nowhere near able to complete the tasks you were given, seeing as you in that time also need to sleep, eat, work and study.
It gets a little better once you can afford hiring collaborators to make videos for you, but when you yourself decide to chip in (afterall, you are the big cahuna), it feels like the in-game clock discourages you to do so. Because while you are editing, picking clips to use and putting them together, time still runs and you cannot upload your collabs videos until you're done yourself.
This game still has a ways to go to iron out some minor flaws, but it's definately worth checking out. If the above seems discouraging, try once the game has been released.

I really do have to say that WARFRAME, aesthetically, is one of the best games I've ever played. So many things that are so...aesthetically unique in WARFRAME, from the guns, swords, equipment, maps, factions, and enemies. They all look so different from other games, it fascinates me IMMENSELY. I especially like the GRINEER and their aesthetics, just the industrial, gritty, messy and dirty look to them, GRINEER is probably one of the things that really keep me hooked into WARFRAME! The shapes and designs of WARFRAME are very dynamic and artistic, it's just...great!
Ofc, gameplay, it's rather pretty good, you shoot, you kill, you hack and slash, you slide and jump from point A to point B, finish objectives and so on and so on. Things get a bit too fast sometimes but of course, WARFRAME is a very fast paced game and I can't really complain about it.
Though I honestly don't know if it's one of those games that is the most fun when played with friends...in my perspective anyway. Like I mean friends like talking through voice chat and stuff, not just Public matchmaking random players and such. Warframe is very fast and most of the times, you're gonna be going everywhere, doing your own thing and such, everyone will. It's not an entirely hard game.
When you get to a certain point in the game, things are pretty darn automatic for you and yeah. It isn't like Overwatch or anything where communication is quite crucial if you really want to win a game. Warframe isn't really like that, everyone is pretty much independent and can handle themselves alone, as far as I know. For a lot of the cases, there isn't really a point in....grouping up with your squad...if you can because it's really hard, most of the times, you really can't stand still.
Of course, that ain't really the ONLY case in WARFRAME haha, but I'll let people figure that out when they get to that.
And yeah, the GRIND is REAL. That's a pretty core part of Warframe and a lot of people know that so yeah.
So...YEAH! I recommend this game but eh, you do you. I do have to say that AESTHETICALLY!? Warframe is very unique and beautiful. Without its awesome aesthetics, I don't think I'd have gotten 2k3 hours into the game!

I can't recommend this game yet, due to its bugs, the rough state of balancing, and the awkward gameplay flow.  To go into more detail:
- I was forced to start a new game twice within a couple of hours due to gamebreaking bugs which prevented me from starting new  videos.
- The game world hours progress extremely quickly and are very hard to keep notice of.  It will seem like an evening has passed, but actually a week has.  In this week you have likely eaten once, not slept, played 1.5 games, studied once... you get the idea.

- Those hours progress at that speed *no matter what*.  Even when you're in menus deciding on things, or choosing clothes to wear to an event, time is rapidly trickling away.  This creates an almost tangible blanket of stress that covers the whole game.  At all times you feel rushed and unable to sit back and think about your next move.  It feels contrary to what a laid-back simulation ought to be about.  A sims-style game speed setting (1x speed, 3x speed, 10x speed etc) with vastly reduced base rate of time advancement would go a long way to solving this, as would time pausing in most decision-making menus.
- As a particularly frustrating example of the above: sometimes you are given tasks to do by friends, which generally are expected to be completed within a week.  Due to the above time issues, you could go to an evening event, get home, record the video and have the task expire before it finishes uploading because most of a week passed during that evening's (short) event.
- There are a lot of bugs.  Courses just seem straight-up broken; most of the time I resumed a course, my character would be putting time down against nothing.  The tutorial system often breaks and leaves the game in a broken state.  Sometimes after starting a game, you get interrupted and can't resume or create new games.
- The tutorial flows feel tacked-on.  For instance, it shows a tutorial bubble while you create your first video.  It describes what the screen does and how you select reaction cards for your video.  But the cards are not well explained, matching the cards up with symbols is not explained, power you spend on reactions is not explained, and worst of all while you're reading the text, a countdown timer appears to force you to make a decision.
These are easy enough to fix in time and I look forward to updating my review with a positive recommendation.
If you're particularly adventurous, feel free to give it a buy; it's not the worst game out there even in its current state.

ARK is one of the first games I have enjoyed playing when I first joined steam and bought it. Unfortunatly, my computer can only run it on the lowest settings. It is hard seeing such a beautiful game on ugly graphics, but I manage to have fun with it. An issue I would like to point out, that has been a recurring problem for me and many of my friends is the issue of mods. Though fun and many useful mods have been created that improve and add new and exciting things to the base game, there is a price. That cost is the mods varying sizes and the time it takes to download those mods to join a server. Though many servers tell you what mods they may have in their title, only so much can be seen before being cutting off by the other information. It is difficult trying to find a server that has no mods or specific ones you can run with your computer. I feel that it would be an improvement if when clicking on a server you would see a status screen with info of that server concerning eveything from mods, to useful server info, and even a quick BIO of the server if desired. Something that would help people know what they are getting into rather than clicking and joining a server and having to download 50 mods that they had no clue about before hand. People that have horrible internet that join a server with overwhelming mods are waiting hours or even days to play again until the download is finished with no effective way to cancel them. ARK is a great game, it has a lot it needs to improve on before becoming a complete game and until then, I feel like informing people on what kind of server they are joining is a right step in that direction.

So.... have you played an endless 4X game before? if so, this is a refreshed version, with some improvements, but very much more of the same. There's a story, quests and all you came to expect from this franchise. You know what you get into.
For the others, this series (Endless Legends and Space) offers some fresh ideas to the 4X genre.
Negative :
_ Yes the battles come down to a crappy double rock paper cisors decision that is only relevant if sides are of equal strengh, but you're not playing a 4x game for the battles. Here at least you have the option for a nice cinematic after picking your cards. One would argue that a straight up resolution would be faster and more efficient as after 1 or 2 times, the novelty wears off. I also found sieging to be over long and messy (it takes forever to get rid of a pirate camp).
_ AI, people always complain about this in 4x games. In diplomacy, the others play a hot/cold game based on pressure you apply on them (border, military threat, score)... so in short, if you're ahead, they'll all try to kill you... unless you are politically alligned with them and that won't happen if everyone else attacks you as your elections will push to military anyways. As for the game's intelligence... well the computer will play based on it's race's attributes (pacifist/agressive) and whether you are politically inclined with them. Even if you're 3x the computer size with tripple their score, they will make demands and threaten you.
_overpopulation.... Rarely a problem in 4x.... well i played a short game and was overrun by population, even after colonizing all my planets. I actually resorted to gene splicing more than I wanted as a population control measure...
Positive :
_ the interface feels fresh, unique, yes confusing at times, but once you get to know it, it flows nicely.
_ good story, immersive with the quests.
_ interesting mechanics on some races (gene splicing, tree race expansion).
_ good game overall.
Probably not renewed enough for old timers, this game is however a real change for people not familiar with the endless formula. As such i'll recommend it.
If you're an old timer... wait for a good deal (as in you'll feel like your buying an expansion with new races, not a brand new game). Yes that is true for most sequel games in the 4x genre.

This game is very hit and miss. It usually does things amazingly well, or very poorly, sometimes both at the same time.
The best thing about this game is the art design. The world is very attractive, and you can tell that a lot of time and work has gone into making the world and puzzles. The manual you get is also very detailed and impressive.
The worst thing about the game is the character movement. A lot of the time you don't know where you can and can't go, and even worse, when you click the wrong spot, it won't let you pick a new spot until you've arrived at the wrong spot. This along with the character's slow movement speed is a mild form of torture.
The puzzles were very creative and some were quite rewarding. The downside is that some were simple and tedious, meaning that you would know exactly what to do, but it took a while to complete all the actions required to solve the puzzle. Others had somewhat arbitrary solutions. The gear puzzles were awful for this, because you could connect gears to turn the gear at the end, but it would have to be done in an exact way. There was no flexibility for multiple solutions. Worse yet, there were times where you had to add gears that did nothing at all. That's just pointless and it ruins the puzzle for people who have a brain and aren't solving it with a solution guide.
The story and music were underwhelming. The plot without spoilers is that you play as a child fixing problems for adults who are too incompetent or lazy to fix them for themselves. I wanted to enjoy the game more, but it was just too tedious for the most part, and the fulfilling puzzles were too scarce.

I purchased this game during it's early access, so I have been able to compare every update and watch the game evolve over time. I'll just get straight to the point. The game was not very good at launch. While it had a solid foundation, it was plagued with issues from the get go. Long turn times, abysmal AI that literally broke the game, glitches and occasional crashes as well as poor overall performance. Has all these been fixed? If you want a 100% honest answer then YES, this has all been fixed with free and more importantly regular updates to the game.

In fact, the latest update 'Statecraft' pretty much saved this game for me. My biggest gripes with the game in the past was with the diplomacy system. It was always one rule for the AI, one rule for you. You ended up just going to war with every AI because they were just so stupid. They would make demands, declare war even if they stood no chance of winning, blockade your systems then retreat the second you engaged them, only to come back and do the same thing again. It was very frustrating and in the end I put the game down and refused to come back until it was fixed.

When I saw the new update being released and I read the change list I was very intrigued. Could this be the update that propelled this game to it's originals former glory? Oh boy, it did more than that. I haven't put the game down since. Diplomacy is now massively improved. Pesky AI has a fleet in my territory? I can ask them to remove it. If they don't, I can either ignore or apply some kind of negative political pressure on them... while I forcibly remove their ships from my space of course *evil laugh*.

Alliances feel like they have weight to them now. You can actually rely on allies now as well as coordinate your forces much better. AI is more open to trade and will actually accept good trade deals. Before they used to laugh in your face even if you was giving them the world and a bit on a plate just to get a few resources.

What I feel has improved the most from this game is the ability to play without going to war. You can now use political pressure to keep the warmongers at bay. You won't always be able avoid war, but most of the time you can if you play your cards right.

Moving past the diplomacy part of the new update, many bug fixes and quality of life improvements have been made overall to help simplify the experience and offer a fresh and new experience in the X4 strategy genre. The game is rendered in beautiful 3D. Watching those space battles between two massive fleets is like watching your favorite action sci-fi space battle, only you get to have some say in how it plays out.

Everything you could want out of a space strategy game is here. I see people comparing this game to Stellaris a lot and the truth is, I prefer this game. Stellaris gets boring very fast and all games end up turning into all out war just for something to do. Stellaris games also last about a century so you end up having to dump your girlfriend or get a divorce and quit your job to make sure your mighty empire rules the stars! So, I've recently purchased "Youtuber's Life." This is one of the best and worst purchases of my life. I've wanted to be a Youtuber ever since I saw "SkyDoesMinecraft" when I was five years old. I just never had the guts to show my face or voice on the internet. So I bought this game thinking it would be like an actual Youtube career, but easier, becuase You gain hundreds of subs, no matter what you post. Also, at the moment, You are only able to do Gaming channels. I imagine, possibly, that you have to earn other types of channels later on in the game, or they aren't even added to the game yet, as it is Early Access. So I started my "Not-Real-Youtube" Career. You start in your mother's house. Not the basement, which I am sad about. You say, "hey, les make som vidja gaem vids." So you start with the only game on your shelf. You gradually gain money, study, do jobs to earn money, and decorate your room in this phase of the game. Pretty fun, right? This is everything I thought Youtube would be like ever since I was a kid. Eventually, one of your friends invites you to stay in a bigger apartment, which allows you to gain more levels, however, you need $160 on the spot and from there on, $80 dollars a month. I bought the upgrade, and as soon as you move in, you no longer have unlimited food, you can go in debt easily with the $80 a month, because as soon as you have atleast $160, the game prompts you into buying, and you can't really progress unless you buy the apartment. So, you unlock The Grocery Website, and The Clothing Website, which lets you buy food and clothes respectively. After this, the game shifts into MADNESS. You constantly have to buy new gaming platforms, even though nowadays, PC game dominates Youtube, buying games for those platforms, and managing your food. I was always trying to manage my channel, but I would run out of money from buying games, upgrading my PC to edit my videos, and keeping up with the $80 rent. I tried mainly focusing on my channel, because thats whats this game is about! I was always accepting offers to play games and upload them to my channel, because I was constantly out of money, also, once you move into your apartment, you can recieve offers for games, you don't have consoles for. So if you want the money that you need very much, you can't get it unless you earn about 200-375 dollars. So this is where my story kicks back in. I was invited to go to the movies with my friend, as you can go to parties and gaming cons, which I think is really cool, and I accepted, because I thought I had time to earn my rent, as it was the day before the end of the month. I went to the movies and tried to socialize with everyone, thinking my channel would grow from that when I got back to my room. I walk into the movie hall to watch the movie. GAME OVER. START OVER FROM THE BEGINNING OF YOUR APARTMENT! "Oh no! It seems you've missed rent twice. Screw you." Oh yeah, I missed rent once because of all the games I had, were outdated, so I wouldn't earn any money from them. Why does the game advance in Game Time instead of Real Time when at events. That is so stupid. I was furious. I have no words. Literally, I can't think of anything else to say about that. I'm writing this review 3 hours later, and I'm still♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ WHY. Ok, enough about that, time for things this game needs to fix/add/remove. Add all types of channels from the start. Did NerdyNummies start out as a gaming channel? Probably, but I really don't care about that channel, so I'm going to assume she didn't. Add Flash Games! The first thing you see when you open your game, is a guy that looks pretty much like PewDiePie! One of his most popular game series is "Happy Wheels" and look where that got him! 20mil+ subs! When at events, make them run in real time. If it runs in real time at parties, why doesn't it run in real time in other events? Fix the computers in this game. Remember how I said I was constantly doing jobs instead of making videos? Well, I did that for about... 4 in-game days, didn't touch the PC once, because I was loaded with the only affordable food, Sandwiches. The PC broke! So that costed me $20 to repair. Money is crucial in this game. I understand thats what happens in real life. Youtubers need the money once they go independant, and if they fail, there's not much to climb back up on. However, that's no excuse to make this game about only making money. The Youtubers I see, are, most of the time, having fun with their friends when they make videos. This game, is being the Youtuber only doing it for money. Thats just not fun to me. Unless Online Multiplayer is added, where everyone has their individual lives, but everyone can interact with each other, I just don't see this game being that fun. This game is just MySims, but restricted to one room. In my opinion, that really is as boring and lonely as it can get. Also, I have to mention this, the games you buy in this game, have silly and goofy names, yet the merchanise you can buy on the in-game website for your room, is literally called "Mario Shelf" and I saw a Pikachu hat that looked exactly like the one I have so, I don't get why they tried to avoid copyright, but they put copyrighted material in the game. Bye.

I hate the new Halo trilogy. I hate Microsoft. But I want my old Halo games on Steam, so I had to support this.
Halo Wars was and still is a great game. Although its development p­issed off Bungie because Microsoft went behind their backs, Ensemble was respectful to the story and worked with Bungie to make it sensible. It's a shame Microsoft destroyed Ensemble's budget, forced them to lay off so many people during development, and killed them after release. I am glad Bungie left. And I am glad to play this great game again, AND on PC from Steam!
The FOV is a bit small and zoomed in, but this can be fixed with cheat engine.
The port is solid with only a few bugs existing, like the mouse cursor disappearing. This can be fixed with a restart.
The gameplay is simple, but that is what made it great on console. You can have sandbox fun with all your favorite units from the Halo story, with a few extras to boot.
The story is on point. Although it's a one off, I think this is good because had the game failed it wouldn't have affected the main story at all. You follow three characters: Captain Cutter of the UNSC Spirit of Fire (a colony ship modified for war), Professor Anders (protige and rival to Dr. Catherine Halsey), and Sgt. Forge (badass Marine and who Bungie would base Spartan-II Jorge on). They attempt to defeat the Covenant in their attempts to unlock Forerunner secrets found within the ancient structures on Harvest.
(I respect Ensemble for keeping the story in its own little section versus games like Halo 4 and Halo 5 which resurrected a dead [finished according to Bungie] story, put it on life support, and butchered a lot of great characters in what people claim to be "they finally added character and story to the Halo games". Even if that added character and story means turning the confident and walking tank that is Chief into a depressed, asocial emo guy who magically forgot all his friends, a Cortana going through menopause and rampancy [again], as well as the UNSC still warring with the Elites, and the Forerunners hating both the humans [their legacy] and the Precursors [their predecessor role models].)
p.s. Halo was originally meant to be an RTS similar to Myth. Even though a lot of fans already know this, somehow many more forget. So imagine this as a what could have been.

In the real world (or should I say 3D), you get around just like any 3D platforming game. While in 3D mode you can move objects or light sources to arrange shadows in a way that could help you through some obstacles. The combination of 3D and 2D platforming make for interesting puzzles and a unique gameplay.
Definitely, a game worth buying, sale or no sale.

An excellent, fresh-feeling 4X TBS. Feels solid all around, from an expansion, military and tech perspective, but the standout features are population management and politics. Politics tend to be a secondary system in these games, providing passive boosts, with little in the way of interesting tradeoffs. Also, the politics of your empire are almost entirely under your control. In this game, the politics system feels like its own beast, with the player only able to influence the political leanings of the empire, not dictate it. The hardest, most interesting part of the one game I played was when a quest line made me pass a law from a party that was a distant fifth in my empire. I had to pull out all the stops to push them into a leading position, and it conflicted with other goals I had. It was fascinating. There's also some truly inspired sci-fi world building, with some truly wild ideas for factions. The cons I see for this game: a few minor bugs, I had one crash, and it doesn't quite escape the 4X trap of only officially winning long after you've taken control of the game. The UI is excellent overall, but there were some places where it was hard to find the information I needed.

PROS:
* Beautiful design and artwork
* Gorgeous music
* Interesting and engaging story
* Good puzzles with solutions that are on the right side of "not obvious" and "not frustrating"
* In game hint system that's neither too tempting nor too difficult to access
* Female protagonist without centering around her gender...
* ...who deserves and receives the respect she earns through the game
FAILINGS:
* Some puzzle frustrations: lack of clear goals, difficult to see/find targets, timing puzzles with awkward handles
* A few hangs and crashes, two of which were reproduceable on my system (don't open the steam overlay when working with the water tank)
* No audio/visual options, couldn't adjust sound-levels in game (music was too loud in the endgame for some reason)
OTHER:
* Puzzle difficulty leans towards "easy" but I'd rather easy than frustrating
* Some of the stranger puzzles can be frustrating when you don't "see" what needs to be done right away, but every single one of them made sense by the completion of the puzzle. None need to be solved by pure trial and error

Wow, what a spectacularly dull game. To all those complaining you can't get it to launch, youse are the lucky ones... well that's not true but the game's not great.
First of all Cole Phelps is just an extremely dulll and unlikeable character. His smug, smarmy facial expressions are captured perfectly with the only real reason to take a glance at this game. The facial animation is still better than most today however the texture quality has not aged well and coupled with the choppy framerate it just doesn't look as good as it once would've.
The story doesn't seem to be going anywhere interesting after more than six hours (I've played an hour or two offline as well), it just seems to be a kind of episodic deal. Crime or two, promotion, another crime or two. If you're into detective stuff and noir style then maybe, just maybe you can get into this as there is kind of a gap in the market for this stuff. Just don't expect much in the way of action.
This game essentially plays itself during any action sequences. You just hold the trigger down and move forward until the other guy stops running. The shooting is very basic, not bad in any real way, there's just nothing to it. There's nothing really noteworthy to say about the driving either.
The meat of the gameplay is the detective stuff. This consists primarily of listening to people talk and using the advanced facial capture stuff to read faces and determine if they're lying, with the help of evidence and context of course. Oh and bad acting works to your advantage too sometimes. You literally just pick Truth, Doubt or Lie which is just doubt but you have to pick a bit of evidence to back it up. You also walk around picking things up and looking at them with great interest. The thing that bugged me the most with this is the fact that it immediately tells you if you got the dialogue tree wrong which just compels me to retry until I get it right and subsequently I end up hearing the same bits of dialogue a dozen times. It'd be more immersive if it just sort of went forward with no specific indication, at least not until the end of the case. For the last one I just used a walkthrough but that made it thrice as boring which is when I realised that I was not enjoying it enough to play anymore.
Long story short, don't play it if you're autistic.

Contrast is game that I liked, but I can easily see why some people might dislike it, and why it got so low score on Metacritic.
1) Gameplay
Contrast comes up with a great concept, but it's been poorly made. The idea of changing from 2D to 3D really inovates (even though there was already a game that came with a concept a lot like that called Perspective, it's a f2p game, go and check it yourself), and brings lots of great moments, but also buggy ones. There were moments where the puzzle wasn't the challenge it self, but the glitches.
There were also mechanics that could have been more exploited.
2) Art/ Soundtrack/ Voiceacting
The atmosphere of the game is well built by the scenario and the sound track, art desgin really fit's in, but there are problems. The animations weren't much organic (and seem really half baked), there were buggy shadows and some halfbaked props, missing collison on places where it clearly should have something.
The voice acting actually impressed me. It's not exceptional, but it fits in to the characters really nicely.
3) Story
The story of Contrast may be for some one of the strogesnt points, but I have to disagree a little bit on that one.
The story really intrigued me, and it really got me thinking, but there were some really strange moments.
Sometimes it's to obvious that the developers didn't have in mind much about the story, only about the gamplay. But it's a nice story, and the gap for theories are wide open for interpretetions. There are some people making some deep theories, but to  be honest, I don't think they really thought about all that.
4)Conclusion:
It's a nice expirience, but it seems like the game was rushed, it's short and there are lots of things that could have been more polished. It's worth a try

Crusader Kings II is not Civilization. And, unlike other Paradox games such as the Europa Universalis series, it is not hard to learn. You play as a ruler, of a county, a duchy, a kingdom, or an empire. You choose initially from the set of rulers available at the start of the game, which is by default anyone in power in 1066 CE Europe (Further back with the Old Gods expansion) and from then on, things get rough. If your ruler dies, you then play as your immediate heir. If you have no heir, then you lose the game, so the simplest goal would be to have your dynasty survive the lenght of the game (some 400 years). Only there's so much more to do than survive. You have to plan marriages for your daughters and sons, deal with an often angry Pope, vicious neighbors with claims on your lands, angry subordinates who may be plotting to kill you or usurp your titles, a derelict king or queen who thinks they're posessed by the devil and are putting the kingdom you belong to on the fast track to destruction, an angry horde of mongols rapidly advancing, a holy war tearing apart a nearby kingdom, and so much more. It doesn't take long to get immediately caught up in the scheming and politics of even the tiniest duchy, and before you know it two hundred years have passed, kingdoms have risen and fallen, assassins have come and gone, plagues have ruined your best laid plans for succession, and you realize it's eight AM and you've been caught up in medieval rulership for all night.

This entry to the Metro series is a massive improvement over the last one. It sets the graphical standard for games to come in the near future. You return as Artyom as he continues in his battle against the mutants throughout post apocalyptic Russia while also trying to shelter his people from them. Gun combat now feels more solid and authentic than last time, you get some new weapons to play with and the story takes different twists and turns throughout the game. As with the weapons, a lot more enemy types are also introduced and have become a lot more fierce than the ones in the previous game.
Overall, the atmosphere created in this game is amazing and it feels truly that you're barely surviving the harsh post apocalyptic environment and may give up at any point in the game. Its totally worth experiencing it through to the end and is highly recommended by me.

First, with the Pros:
True to the games' description by the author, this is a horror survival game. Progress is determinded by how well you can survive. Elements of stealth, reconnaisance, resource utrilization and conservation, atmospheric and lighting will be key in exploration and survival.
The gameplay is pretty straight-forward. Hand-holding is minimal, and the challenge progression is non-linear. Even on amateur difficulty level,Metro Last Light requires considerable skill and attention to detail to muster even the very first parts of the game. Its' a good primer for these well versed in first person shooters. On highrt levels of difficulty, the key is stealth, frugality in expending resources and firepower, and speed. Of note is the realism bhrought on by environmental factors such as lighting ( notes for stealth), radioactivity, uninhabitable atmosphere ( reminds you to keep check on filters and inventory), and the various monsters you'll face in-game. Each is a challenge unto its' own, blended into a perfect blend of horror.
This, in my opinion, is one of the best horror survival games I've played in a while, and compared to the Resident Evil franchise from Capcom, Metro Last Light just stole my personal record of a horror survival game from Resident Evil.
The graphics options are modest, and a recent gaming rig with a mid-range GPU should be able to handle the game on Low to Medium, without appreciable loss in visual quality. For these with high-end NVIDIA GPUs, turn on Advanced PhySX for realistic physics. You'll want to leave this "Disabled" on AMD GPUs and APUS. VRAM is also significant on Ultra Setting Details and resolutions above 2k-4k.
Game length: Adequate and balanced. Jump right in and survive. Its' all that matters in the Metro.
Caveats: On some scenery, persistent flickering of textures may be prevalent and at times, intermittent. May cause visual strain. Exasberated by playing the game in Stereoscopic 3D. Recent updates and patches have reduced this problem. However, its' still present. If flickering lights trigger epileptic episodes and syncope in the player, take note of this problem.

So.... have you played an endless 4X game before? if so, this is a refreshed version, with some improvements, but very much more of the same. There's a story, quests and all you came to expect from this franchise. You know what you get into.
For the others, this series (Endless Legends and Space) offers some fresh ideas to the 4X genre.
Negative :
_ Yes the battles come down to a crappy double rock paper cisors decision that is only relevant if sides are of equal strengh, but you're not playing a 4x game for the battles. Here at least you have the option for a nice cinematic after picking your cards. One would argue that a straight up resolution would be faster and more efficient as after 1 or 2 times, the novelty wears off. I also found sieging to be over long and messy (it takes forever to get rid of a pirate camp).
_ AI, people always complain about this in 4x games. In diplomacy, the others play a hot/cold game based on pressure you apply on them (border, military threat, score)... so in short, if you're ahead, they'll all try to kill you... unless you are politically alligned with them and that won't happen if everyone else attacks you as your elections will push to military anyways. As for the game's intelligence... well the computer will play based on it's race's attributes (pacifist/agressive) and whether you are politically inclined with them. Even if you're 3x the computer size with tripple their score, they will make demands and threaten you.
_overpopulation.... Rarely a problem in 4x.... well i played a short game and was overrun by population, even after colonizing all my planets. I actually resorted to gene splicing more than I wanted as a population control measure...
Positive :
_ the interface feels fresh, unique, yes confusing at times, but once you get to know it, it flows nicely.
_ good story, immersive with the quests.
_ interesting mechanics on some races (gene splicing, tree race expansion).
_ good game overall.
Probably not renewed enough for old timers, this game is however a real change for people not familiar with the endless formula. As such i'll recommend it.
If you're an old timer... wait for a good deal (as in you'll feel like your buying an expansion with new races, not a brand new game). Yes that is true for most sequel games in the 4x genre.

I'm going to recommend this game, but I will give a caveat - I bought it on a good sale, when it was under 4 bucks.  At that price, it's well worth it.  At full price... probably not.
This is a nice little game, with a really fantastic concept - the idea of shifting in and out of a 2D shadow world, and solving puzzles by moving objects and lights in 3D in order to properly align their shadows in 2D is very clever.  The music and atmosphere is quite nice as well, and the voice acting is well-done.  The story is a little thin, but I can't complain too much about that.
Now, the down sides.  First off, the game is quite short.  I completed it in just a few hours, and I'm sure many players could do it in even less time.  Also, the controls are a little... I don't know how to describe it, exactly.  Often, when working in the 3D world, the camera will drift a little oddly, and you end up running into a wall unintentionally.  In the 2D world, you find yourself occasionally falling out of the shadows for small things - bumping into the wrong shadow, jumping across a wall of a darker color.  Not consistently, and not enough to ruin the game, but enough to make it a little frustrating occasionally.  Control just doesn't always feel right.
While there are some good puzzles, and the atmosphere is quite interesting, often it feels like the designers weren't quite sure what to do with the concept.  Finally, gameplay is interrupted far too often by cutscenes.  I understand the desire to tell the story, and to set the stage for each new area, but it is annoying when control is taken from you every 5 minutes or so.
This review ended up seeming a lot more negative than I actually feel about the game.  As I said at the start, if you get it on sale for less that 5 dollars or so, I think it's worth it, if you enjoy casual puzzle games with a unique atmosphere.  Ultimately, though, I would love to see this concept fleshed out more in another game.  It's a great idea that this game just couldn't quite do justice to.

I purchased this game during it's early access, so I have been able to compare every update and watch the game evolve over time. I'll just get straight to the point. The game was not very good at launch. While it had a solid foundation, it was plagued with issues from the get go. Long turn times, abysmal AI that literally broke the game, glitches and occasional crashes as well as poor overall performance. Has all these been fixed? If you want a 100% honest answer then YES, this has all been fixed with free and more importantly regular updates to the game.

In fact, the latest update 'Statecraft' pretty much saved this game for me. My biggest gripes with the game in the past was with the diplomacy system. It was always one rule for the AI, one rule for you. You ended up just going to war with every AI because they were just so stupid. They would make demands, declare war even if they stood no chance of winning, blockade your systems then retreat the second you engaged them, only to come back and do the same thing again. It was very frustrating and in the end I put the game down and refused to come back until it was fixed.

When I saw the new update being released and I read the change list I was very intrigued. Could this be the update that propelled this game to it's originals former glory? Oh boy, it did more than that. I haven't put the game down since. Diplomacy is now massively improved. Pesky AI has a fleet in my territory? I can ask them to remove it. If they don't, I can either ignore or apply some kind of negative political pressure on them... while I forcibly remove their ships from my space of course *evil laugh*.

Alliances feel like they have weight to them now. You can actually rely on allies now as well as coordinate your forces much better. AI is more open to trade and will actually accept good trade deals. Before they used to laugh in your face even if you was giving them the world and a bit on a plate just to get a few resources.

What I feel has improved the most from this game is the ability to play without going to war. You can now use political pressure to keep the warmongers at bay. You won't always be able avoid war, but most of the time you can if you play your cards right.

Moving past the diplomacy part of the new update, many bug fixes and quality of life improvements have been made overall to help simplify the experience and offer a fresh and new experience in the X4 strategy genre. The game is rendered in beautiful 3D. Watching those space battles between two massive fleets is like watching your favorite action sci-fi space battle, only you get to have some say in how it plays out.

Everything you could want out of a space strategy game is here. I see people comparing this game to Stellaris a lot and the truth is, I prefer this game. Stellaris gets boring very fast and all games end up turning into all out war just for something to do. Stellaris games also last about a century so you end up having to dump your girlfriend or get a divorce and quit your job to make sure your mighty empire rules the stars! With Endless Space 2, you can do all this while retaining your social life and source of income.

Purchase this game and support these great developers. They listen to player feedback, they are active in the forums and they do not sell you pieces of the game as DLC. They have kept good on their promise to continue to improve this game since launch and they have done just that.

Child-murder, religious wars, incest, assassinations and good old fashioned imperial expansion! This game has it all.

That said, I'd like a more interactive papacy. Give me the ability to not only set up an anti-pope (which is possible) but also control him. Allow me, upon controlling the Vatican, to move it to a city in my nation, as was historically precedented.
Too, the lack of naval battles is infuriating. I may have 160 ships in my imperial navy, but I have no way whatsoever to inhibit enemy troops from disembarking or sinking their armies at sea.
Another complaint is just how *little* there is of the world past Europe and some of the Near East and North Africa. Give me more chunks of the world to scheme against!

Your infantry is sweeping the forests, hunting down the enemy tank destroyers who're keeping your tank column from advancing. You have anti-air vehicles rushing to meet your advance, hoping they'll arrive before the enemy sends in the helicopters. Twenty kilometres to the rear, your artillery is desperately rushing to a new location while IFVs are on their way to protect them from the enemy special forces pouring out of the woods, and artillery rockets are falling everywhere, shattering morale.
Your infantry gets bogged down by enemy troops, and the tank destroyers have long since relocated. You order your tanks to give the woods a wide berth so they don't stray within range of the enemy ATGM troops. The AA has fought off a few helicopter attacks, but you've already lost a few tanks. Then your recon vehicle finally finishes its careful creep through the forests, and arrives in the enemy base zone. You call in your artillery, now safe, and sit back as dozens of shells start flying.....

Crusader Kings II is not Civilization. And, unlike other Paradox games such as the Europa Universalis series, it is not hard to learn. You play as a ruler, of a county, a duchy, a kingdom, or an empire. You choose initially from the set of rulers available at the start of the game, which is by default anyone in power in 1066 CE Europe (Further back with the Old Gods expansion) and from then on, things get rough. If your ruler dies, you then play as your immediate heir. If you have no heir, then you lose the game, so the simplest goal would be to have your dynasty survive the lenght of the game (some 400 years). Only there's so much more to do than survive. You have to plan marriages for your daughters and sons, deal with an often angry Pope, vicious neighbors with claims on your lands, angry subordinates who may be plotting to kill you or usurp your titles, a derelict king or queen who thinks they're posessed by the devil and are putting the kingdom you belong to on the fast track to destruction, an angry horde of mongols rapidly advancing, a holy war tearing apart a nearby kingdom, and so much more. It doesn't take long to get immediately caught up in the scheming and politics of even the tiniest duchy, and before you know it two hundred years have passed, kingdoms have risen and fallen, assassins have come and gone, plagues have ruined your best laid plans for succession, and you realize it's eight AM and you've been caught up in medieval rulership for all night.

It's been a pleasure playing this game, but it has its flaws.
First, the bad notes: there are many tiny imperfections in the game that could be removed with little work, but in the context sound like a bad note in the symphony. Many times while moving in the shadows I was pushed out with no reason, like when passing over a semi-column in the lab; in many sections you can catch Didi in a T-pose, and even Dawn's position when using the umbrella is clearly a T-pose with an umbrella, and that really ruined the atmosphere.
But the game itself, especially for being a small production, is really good and enjoyable. The story is fascinating and, even if not the most suspence-filled noir plot, keeps you playing even just to know what's gonna happen. Deep characters and very nice voice-acting, the light-shadow system has it's flaws but its overall is quite good and fun. I bought the collector edition and I'm happy I did so, because the OST is very very nice. Finally, the way the game slowly shifts in a surrealist note is, at least for me, simply beautyful.
Maybe €15 are too many, but I recommend this game. You'll learn eventually that, if you stop demanding for extreme graphics and gory shootings, and start enjoying the little things, this game has a lot to offer.

Contrast gets a hesitant thumbs up. It's a game that I'm dying to love, and while I completed it and did enjoy parts of it... it's hard to say I loved it. But it might be worth your time and money. Read on...
On its surface, the game has a lot going for it: the art style is superb, the "phase shift" gimmick is really neat, and the storyline is decently interesting. The game, for a short experience, builds a nice little world and it does a solid job of make you invested in the characters. Also, the music is fantastic.
However, a couple minor issues and one major issue gum up the experience. First, the game took me just over three hours (which included a few chunks of paused game) to complete, in its entirety. That means every achievement. I think I spend more time hunting down Easter eggs in Gone Home, frankly.
Secondly, while the story segments are good, there's seemingly as much or more of them than gameplay. Especially early on, when the story is trying to establish itself, you walk ten feet and cutscene. Walk ten more, cutscene. Walk outside, another cutscene. I wanna play!
Also, and this may just be me, but the "phase shift" gimmick was never used to its full potential. There are a few moments where you do something really cool, and everything falls in place, and it feels great. But those moments are more rare than they ought to be. Most of the puzzles or silly in their simplicity, which some of the tougher ones being more about fighting the way shadows work rather than being brain benders.
And lastly, this is the big one. The controls... aren't great. If you're in shadow and run out of a space, you pop out. But it doesn't always work consistently. And collision detection is off at times. Also, I died a number of times when I didn't phase in like it was supposed to.
At a couple of the later puzzles (the rotating wall in particular), I felt like I spent more time fighting the controls and shadow detection, as opposed to the puzzles. And felt myself pulled out of the story due to frustration.
Now I know, that's a laundry list of problems. But most of them are because the premise and setting were so good... I wanted more. I wanted more puzzles, more areas to explore and more stuff to do. I got it on sale for just a couple bucks, and frankly am glad I'd waited. For a few bucks, it was a nice diversion over the weekend that left me ultimately satisfied.
But for full price, for those easily frustrated or for those expecting a long, polished experience. Maybe watch a Let's Play and pass. So as stated above, I give this one a very cautious thumbs up, with a big ol' asterisk next to it.

I took part in the free play weekend.
First, most of the reviews I’ve read on Stream by players have not helped me make a purchase decision, so was happy get the opportunity to sample the game itself.  In an effort to not repeat the same mistakes regarding a review, I’ll compare this games it to other games of what I consider to be a similar type.
The good:
Its depth of story and nuanced game play goes much farther than the latest “Masters of Orion” game in my opinion and as such, is more entertaining for me.  There are also game mechanics in place to curb / prevent “Doom Stack” vs “Doom Stack” combat game play which I find is also a relief.
The different races in the game, just don’t have difference abilities, but they been taken further so that they have their own race unique game mechanics to go along with them, i.e. they’re not just skinned differently with a +2 here and a -1 there to stat X and Y.  Race “A” actually accomplishes the same task leveraging a different game play mechanic / strategy from race “B.”  Planetary colonization is an example of this.
The not so good:
The game is a bit crippled from what I call the “Civilization Dilemma” which is having to start over and over again until you get game that gives a fair chance and worth continuing – especially if you do not disable the pirates.
There’s a bit too much game mechanic focus on empire happiness as well as punishment for playing with an expansionist play style, so be warned if that’s something you like to do.
All in all, I found it to be quite enjoyable game I’ve decided to add it to my library.

Lumino City is a puzzle adventure game which is the sequel to Lume. While you do not need to play the excellent although a bit short first game to enjoy the outstanding second one (which has a solid length of around 10 hours), I would recommend playing both in order as both games are excellent. Lumino City features physically hand-made environments that are filmed at various angles to provide the backdrop and the results are nothing short of spectacular: bright and popping colours, superb vistas as the camera pans around and the outstanding visual design delights at every turn. The sound design accompanies the puzzle solving perfectly and enhances the feeling of strolling through the various areas calmly solving the brain-teasers along the way. The puzzles themselves are very inventive and the presentation is very polished without being excessively easy or - for the most part - excessively hard. The story is also well presented and the witty dialogue by the people you come across even in the background conversations and little bits of information scattered around in the flavour text (such as how a harmonica works) is all very interesting. I encountered a few minor bugs that required me to reload one area without progress loss but did not find other bugs in the otherwise highly polished game. This game won the many awards listed on its store page for good reason, everything from its delightful presentation, solid gameplay, entertaining story and setting to the unique and excellent visuals punctuated by equally excellent sound design and music make it a must have, highly recommended!

With all the simplified games coming out nowadays, this game is pretty refreshing with a few complex features in its gameplay and the fact that it's not another FPS game. Wargame is a realistic RTS game with large scale battles and a huge list of units to choose from.
Gameplay: Choose units that you want to deploy (from a list of units that is customizable) and choose there locations. Start by capturing sectors for a slow income for reinforcements (sometimes sectors can reinforce too). The team who destroys the most points of units wins.
Few notes: Maps are huge, unit travel can take a while and requires smart positioning. Their isnt much microing and speed involved in this game compared to games like Starcraft but rather involves more strategy in position and right timed attacks.
I'd say this RTS game is great and if you liked any of the games listed above, this game may be worth checking out.

Lumino City is basically a game built upon clever and almost realistic puzzle problems. I say almost realistic because it grounds its puzzle logic in basic arithmetic and mechanical systems but still exagerating it for fantastical effect. Think of the logic in say a Rube Goldberg Machine. And that's what I love about this game. Fun yet challenging puzzle solving.
Another striking thing about the game is the stop motion aesthetic and graphics. Lumino City is set in a mixture of exagerated 1950's tech but with a nice of touch of an English countryside town. While playing this, I've felt that charm and  grabbing wit of say the film, Toy Story. Good old wholesome aesthetic that really captures the imagination of why a community would be built around such strange and wonderful machinery. However the graphics ties in nicely with my biggest gripe with the game. It runs at locked 25 fps. I guess that's because they filmed the stop motion animations at something like that. And I'm fine with my AMD R9 290 chugging a pitiful 25fps if the game kept it at that. But during level transitions, cutscenes, and ordinary scenery object movement, it constantly halves it the framerate to like 12 fps. That's bad especially when you have a few puzzle dependent on precise point n' clicking. Which brings another gripe, input seems so vague. My guess is because the game was built as a mobile game instead of your average PC adventure game. I often miss clicked points of interest just because what you click is based on a general area and not the point you clicked. Think of touch screen input and the problems with that and you'll have an idea as to my problems with input in the game. Also, there is no resolution options, audio options, or any of that stuff in the game. Just defaults to your primary displays resolution. Again, a sign that they mostly built the game around mobile devices.
But after all that I still love the game. The first game they made, Lume, was charming but a fleeting experience. And this one seems to have taken the charm, wit, and fun of the first one and just amplified it for a lasting effect. Sure, my completion time says this is a short game. Hey, a lot of adventure games are short so why would you expect this to be 200 hours long like a Civilization game or DOTA2. But that's beside the point. If your a fan of the genre you'd understand why adventure games have a different pace to them compared to other games.
Oh, about the story of it. There's not much plot other than say the Lumino City's story. Your not going to be having exposition long cutscenes. You do talk to characters but mostly it's a one off thing. Characters are tied to the environment and scene they're in so you mostly won't see them again. But that doesn't really bother me because I realize that the story of Lumino City itself is a lot more engaging than the individuals you meet. Though they are interesting enough to reinforce that environmental story telling the game's got going for itself.
, I love it and I hope that if you've read this review I manage to inform you as to why I think it's a great game. Oh, and the soundtracks fantastic so get that soundtrack edition if you can.

Crusader Kings II is not Civilization. And, unlike other Paradox games such as the Europa Universalis series, it is not hard to learn. You play as a ruler, of a county, a duchy, a kingdom, or an empire. You choose initially from the set of rulers available at the start of the game, which is by default anyone in power in 1066 CE Europe (Further back with the Old Gods expansion) and from then on, things get rough. If your ruler dies, you then play as your immediate heir. If you have no heir, then you lose the game, so the simplest goal would be to have your dynasty survive the lenght of the game (some 400 years). Only there's so much more to do than survive. You have to plan marriages for your daughters and sons, deal with an often angry Pope, vicious neighbors with claims on your lands, angry subordinates who may be plotting to kill you or usurp your titles, a derelict king or queen who thinks they're posessed by the devil and are putting the kingdom you belong to on the fast track to destruction, an angry horde of mongols rapidly advancing, a holy war tearing apart a nearby kingdom, and so much more. It doesn't take long to get immediately caught up in the scheming and politics of even the tiniest duchy, and before you know it two hundred years have passed, kingdoms have risen and fallen, assassins have come and gone, plagues have ruined your best laid plans for succession, and you realize it's eight AM and you've been caught up in medieval rulership for all night.
