So I decided to pick Endless Space 2 up in a recent sale, having really enjoyed the original.
I'd heard it had some issues and the devs were tending to it, but I thought it had been long enough as well that anything serious would be done.
Unfortunately I feel I was wrong in that hope.
So to start with the positives, Endless Space 2 feels as if a AAA company took ES1 and spent 2 years focusing on nothing but pure immersion. The game looks spectacular and the old narrative feeling is back.
Gameplay is relatively similar, though combat has been overhauled to some extent, with tactics being a once-a-battle thing now and it's decided before-hand not mid-battle.
The new combat is great by the way. The new land battles helps add to the flavor of the game, though sometimes I feel it doesn't make sense, such as when you want 30% of your army to be aircraft and you end up with loadouts you can't control where you might have 80 infantry, 30 tanks, and 2 aircraft.
From there we get onto some more disappointing points.
Firstly is performance. A game of Endless Space 2 is meant to run about 300 turns. If you play on slow, about 450 turns. But with my own specs of an i7-6700K, GTX 1080Ti and 16GB RAM, on top of having the game on an SSD, performance becomes sloppy inside 150 turns with ease. Battles start having random stutters and turns themselves slow down to some extent (Though I will give it credit for not being anywhere near as bad as Firaxis' trademark mega waits for Civilization turns)
We come to the two points now that I feel are the most critical in why I'm unfortunately disappointed so far:
1: The AI.
The AI feels incomplete. It mocks you every few turns like clockwork, simply tells you what it's going to do in a few turns (Like going to war), and its ability to build up its own empire is...strange at best.
The AI manages to expand rapidly at the start. I'm not the most experienced player but on normal I definitely felt the AI outpaced me by miles in the early-game periods. However that quickly changes as the AI gets bogged down over nothing and thus doing nothing. An AI can go to war with you and simply never try to attack, or when they do it's for the one system they seem to want and that's it, or they just want to abduct people for 30 turns.
From a diplomacy standpoint the AI is full-on idiotic. An AI declares war on you due to having the opportunistic trait and you are at war already, but you take 10 systems off of them and they will still simply refuse peacedeals point blank when the war is about to wipe them out the game. It simply feels like the AI barely takes anything into account, and ultimately after about 100+ turns I feel like the AI just falls apart entirely.
On a side note, if you get an AI ally, they will go to war without saying anything, then insult you for not helping every 3-4 turns, but there is simply no way to be asked to join a war or offer, you just have to know who they are at war with and do it manually. It might work but it's impractical in this day-in-age for a 4X game.
For the second point, we have UI and events.
I enjoy the atmosphere of Endless Space and I like the overall gameplay, but I swear that I have *never* seen a game with such blatant disregard for player input as Endless Space 2. The standard 4X events are practically full-screen on this game, and they will pop up almost randomly. Sometimes a start-of-turn event will popup 10-15 seconds after you are navigating some other menu. There is no coherency between menu panels because you will get an option to go see something, click it, and then it has simply replaced it with a new event to go see something else.
Ultimately the events could outspam a dedicated spambot on reddit, with the game basically mandating that you try and manually turn off as many of the more pointless events as possible so you can feel sane when you click end-turn.
Update: So I've put a bit more time in, another 5-6 hours and found a few new issues. Some petty, some outrageous:
- The AI shutting its borders whilst you blockade them appears to despawn your blockading fleet from the game, but it keeps it in your lists and keeps charging you for it, you effectively lose the ships permanently. If this is otherwise, the game is not saying. (So I just lost about 1.2M dust worth of ship value and it's now draining 9,000 manpower a turn at random. Seems to be 100% broken)
-AI's late-game tactics appear to be trying to spam one planet with 5-6 bad fleets so that they can keep it permanently guarded and keep getting land battles in, even though they cannot win a single space battle
-Even trying to work out what treaties you have with everyone is a serious hassle. You might as well write them down because unless you are allowed to cancel it right now, you can't see what treaties are there.
-Performance has become cripplingly low in terms of turn timers and just trying to get battles to load, this is by turn 200-210 on a 300-turn game on a large map with 8 players...
-Nothing and I mean *nothing* scales properly in this game. I make 9,000 dust a turn but the AI offers me peace and 39 dust per turn. At the start of my latest game, with 3 systems in my empire, a minor system asked me to build 18 buildings in 15 turns...suffice to say that was impossible.
-Lastly, I won a supremacy game and it turned around and told me to go to the score screen, only to sit on the loading menu for 3 minutes and never load it at all.
End of Update
In summary, I want to reiterate that overall I do like the game. I feel the best way to describe Endless Space 2 is it feels like a AAA company made it, but it's as if they've never done anything even remotely similar to this game before. I enjoy the game for only as long as the events can be kept at bay (Which they often can't) and the AI stays competent(which again it often doesn't).
I'm going to have to say that even on sale, you might be disappointed with the state it is in, despite how visually appealing it is and how great the core gameplay itself still is too. I would check back and see if the devs have been able to alleviate at least the AI in the future.
After all the stuff I posted in the update section, I have to say this is an even greater disappointment than I thought. It's a shame because Endless Space 1 is great. You are better off just playing the original, as this sequel doesn't deserve to be in the same series.

I am very happy with Endless Space 2. I liked the original game, have truly enjoyed the refinements added in Endless Legend, with faction specific quests and overall improvements made. Now, ES2 is another improvement made on the series.
+ absolutely crisp, elegant graphics (as always, style is a personal preference and I like it)
+ very interesting races, with their own playstyle. Entangle systems in the "roots" of a giant tree? Buy whole planets with cash? Twist time or simply play the science game?
+/- As always, the tech tree is a bit of a challenge. So many options, radial progression along spokes of a wheel. Interestingly enough, you have to balance. Terraforming or a new weapon? Happyness for your pops or a new space ship class? The search function helps to find important things like command points.
- Spaceship design. Yes, all the basics are there. Hulls, thruster types, special resource weapons, armor and shields. But they all are a bit too generic, no really surprises. Lazors, slugs or torpedoes? What about time bending local distortion cannons, swarm launchers, acid goo? A bit more daring and faction unique designs, please.
+/- Space combat. While an improvement over the old system, the tactics are not a bit better. It is still an absolute passive, coffee-brake-sit-back-and-enjoy-the-show event. Mass usually wins.
+/- Ground combar. The ground combat is actually more challenging as you have to assemble enough starship troopers to invade and the ground resistance can be pretty tough. You even can invest in all three forces, soldiers, tanks, air crafts. The "simple graphics" are fine for me. I still yearn for special troopers here as well. Stellaris shows the way. Psi corps, alien bug riding cavalry, smart killer bots, you name it.
Overall, I am very pleased with ES2 and will enjoy the occasional round here and there until I played through most factions.
Recommended, if you like Stellaris, Endless Space 1 or Master of Orion. I would rate is as my second best 4 X after Stellaris.

Coming in as someone who absolutely loved Endless Space 1 I just can't recommend the sequel. The biggest problem is certainly the user interface, it is vastly inferior to Endless Space 1s even after several improvements. Everything from the tech tree to the system view to the battle windows has been made more complex for little gameplay benefit. The increased focus on "quests" is also a definite minus it was tolerable in Endless legend but here the system just seems poorly implemented, I shouldn't be getting a quest about how the Amoeba are bloodthirsty arena masters and want me to be a militarist to assimilate them. It seems to more spit on the lore of Endless 1 than enhance it. The new factions and faction changes are also annoying, they just don't have the wow factor of Endless 1 and the minor factions just pollute the game map with inconsequential annoyances. Overall the game feels like Endless Space and Endless legend had a baby and like some other cases of inbreeding it turned out deformed.

Okay! So this is my first review but I REALLY wanted to say a few things about the game and what I think could be done to improve it! Sorry for any errors, I want to make this review as clear as possible.
First off its a great game. I love the sims and it reminds me so much of that, combined with the tycoon games that I also love. I haven't gone too in depth as far as relationships in this game so I have no note of that, besides possibly making there more ways to interact with another character in the game. I have high hopes for this game and would just like to throw out some reccomendations!
-It's probably just me, but I get so OCD about having a bunch of videogames I never play. I'd like an option where I can sell a group of them!
-As stated previously, more talking or interactive options with characters
-Maybe not such a rush to advance so quickly in the game, if someone wants to live in their mommas house for a while they should!
-Which brings me to another thing, maybe I'm not as far as I thought but I don't think "study" ever comes back into the game. I'd like to see more of that and not just in the beggining. Or at least have gotten a degree for it. I feel like my studying was for nothing but a mere $50 (although at that time, I needed it)
-MORE EVENTS! They're so fun, and I feel like there isn't enough of them
-I know it makes the game more challenging, but maybe an in-game pause would be nice. Or a "stop the clock" while you're making purchases. Sometimes I just feel so rushed as far as looking through games that just came out or the best games I could buy at the time.
-In addition to a calender, why not make an actual in-game time? It reminds me a bit of Harvest Moon as far as the time translates into real life, but probably a lot faster. I just feel like it would make the game more organized.
This was probably a lot but I just had a few ideas I wanted to share. Again, this is my first review but I really felt strongly about this game considering I see a lot of potentional in it. I reccomend this game to any fellow Sim or Tycoon lovers! Maybe wait a bit till it's released because $15 was quite a bit for me personally but honestly, it's a fun time. Thanks for reading :)

Have you ever wanted to lop someone's head off? Have you ever wanted to taste the glory of the battlefield? If you salivate at the prospect of a competitive, online, medieval-style war game with siege warfare and bloodcurdling screams,  then BUY THIS GAME!!!  I'd give it a 8.5/10, but incredibly addicting!  Most players you will notice have 1k+ hours.
I will give you some deets if you are on the fence/generally interested but not convinced. Slightly lengthy but compiled well.
--------
<PRO'S>
--------
COMBAT:
-The combat system is more robust than anything else out there.
-Ability to drag (slow down) and accelerate (speed up) attacks by moving your mouse certain ways.
-Overheads, stabs, and horizontal attacks are all in melee possibility along with kicks and shield bashes.
-Spacing, positioning, situational awareness, teamwork, dodging projectiles, siege warfare, timing, and skill are pivotal.
-Ability to parry attacks, block with a shield, riposte attacks, and dodge (if Men At Arms)
-Your attacks seem to have real weight and consequences to missing as opposed to something like mount & blade or war of the roses.
GAME MODES:
Each game mode benefits a growing player's skills as each will get you good at certain aspects of the game.  There are also a few different mods out there. Some for competitive play (mercs), and some for fun (black knight, giantslayer, laserswords, horde)
-Team Deathmatch-----(Good at building teamwork and straight-to-the-point kill tactics)
-Free For All------------(Better for learning situational awareness and being "in the♥♥♥♥♥♥quot;)
-Capture the Flag-------(Also good at building teamwork and battle tactics)
-King of the Hill---------(Helps build team engagement prowess and situational awareness)
-Duel Yards-------------(Good at learning 1vs1 tactics and the nicities of fighting an opponent/parrying)
-Team Objective-------(the longest and most fun/immersive IMHO. Promotes teamwork towards a common goal.)
VOICE ACTING:
Now this is something you wouldn't think would be a huge part of the game, but it adds a lot of depth. Especially when used in the right context by players. each class for both Agatha and Mason have about 20 different voice commands, each with 5 varieties of what is said for that "command", along with a battlecry.  This brings a new level of immersion to the battlefield
CLASS SELECTION:
Fairly simple, but effective class selection.  Four classes, each balanced in their own respect with a different playstyle for each.  Tons of weapon selection with a basic enough principle for each. Different Damage, Reach, Speed, and preferred attack for max damage. (For examples spears have better stab attacks while axes have better overheads.)
-Knight    (most health and armor, heavy hitting, slower weapons and run speed)
-Vanguard    (Moderate health and armor, very long weapons, cannot combo with spears-types, charge attack)
-Men At Arms    (Low health and armor, very fast attack/movement, can use firepots, has dodge)
-Archer    (piddly health and armor, 1shot by almost all knight weapons, medium speed, excel at killing from afar)
------------
<NEUTRAL>
------------
ADVANCED TACTICS:
The game has a lot of fine nuances. This actually fleshes out the combat system even more for competitive purposes, adding a lot of depth. Tactics that have been adapted over the game's lifetime are utilized by a lot of high-tier players. These include:
-The fabled reverse overhead
-Head Feints
-Feinting
-Rubberbanding
-Target switching
-Combo-feint-to-parry
The reason this is neutral is because on one hand, I don't think a lot of these tactics were intended, but rather were discovered throughout the community to be effective means of utilizing the game mechanics. On the other hand, they really start to take away from the game's immersive nature. In rare situations, with desync, these can seem like exploits.
---------
<CON'S>
---------
NEW PLAYERS:
This game has a fairly unforgiving learning curve. I suggest any new player play the tutorial before playing online against other players, and to experiment with all of the classes while playing until you find the class that best suits your playstyle.  This will ensure 1.) that you end up playing the class you were fated to and 2.) that you at least understand from firsthand experience what the other classes are capable of when you are fighting them.
GLITCHES & DESYNC:
-Every now and again you will get caught in an odd place, possibly something like a step, an awkward corner, a small rock, an odd crevice. In this situation you'll have to press F10 to kill yourself or someone can kick you out of it if you're lucky.
-Desync will occur sometimes. This basically means your game client and the server don't agree on what is going on, despite what may appear to be happening on your screen.  Sometimes you will experience a stab that seemed way too freaking fast, an animation that didn't seem to quite play, or someone rubberbanding around somehow.  It doesn't happen enough where it's overwhelmingly noticeable. In fairness, these issues can be expected in any online game, but are only particularly frustrating in chivalry because time, space, and visuals are such an important element in the complex combat system.
All in all, if you are even slightly interested in the aforementioned aspects of a medieval deathfestival, you cannot pass this game up if it 50% off or more.
It offers the most emmersive medieval melee combat experience out there.  It has the capacity to be both hilarious as all hell and competative to a stressful point (if you pursue competitive). There have been games where I have gone ten+ lives in a row without killing a soul.  Then the next life, by the grace of valhalla, I will go on a 7 man killing spree involving a legitimate 4v1 situation and lop a few heads, and it gets me rock hard.  These are the moments I live for in chivalry.
You need a surplus of time or money to be able to progress in this game very much at all.

I first played this game with its newest patch of 1.06x. This happened due to not having access to a computer that was resourceful enough to run the game. After it has been released, both performance and content have been vastly improved.
This game is very giid, it looks promising with further content added, but some things really buged me while testing it.
1.: Random pirate attacks ruin you in early game - and you have no idea how to defend with just a single patrol ship at your dispose. Really makes you want to quit. (And nooo, this is balanced comments, please, it was not!) Hence, even as a peaceful nation, you MUST muster some ships with some reasonable equipment. Do not build laser frigates with ballistic shields against missile and kinetic armament ships with strong deflectors.... really, do not do it.
2.: Techtree looks great, but I, as a new player, have no idea what technology allows me to do what. The recommendation tags are really not helpful - I miss the old Endless Space research screen. (Working search function now - still overwhelming but you can search even for components and get highlighted results.)
3.: Sudden bankruptcy - really sudden. No idea what or why, and when I managed to buy a dust generation improvement, the game still scrapped an improvement despite generating enough cash. (More cash-generating buildings, better knowledge of the techs and upkeep costs makes it far easier to have a well balanced economy. Search for endlessly repetable constructions in the techtree... )
4. Vast galaxy, 10 players, and yet in turn 5 I got visitors that started colonising right infront of my core world. Plus, you are stuck if they block you. Normal AI, so again really makes you want to quit. Hard AI+, that is ok, but not on the standard AI and difficulty setting. - This has also been dealt with, with proper map positioning for example.
I give the game a thumbs up, not just because I see great promise, even with new content, but I really tested it and can say: good game, great time.
After a long time, with access only to decade old hardware, I started the game anew, and I was truly astonished how much since the old beta I had played had been done. More content, FREE, heroes, talents, fighters, systems, improvements, technologies, tech-tree search function, and many more bigger and smaller issues were all fixed.
My recommendation: play one or two games on easy with your desired faction before you start playing them against more capable AI or human enemies, so you get to know how to deal with threats both economically and hostile, be it rebels, enemies or pirates.

So I decided to pick Endless Space 2 up in a recent sale, having really enjoyed the original.
I'd heard it had some issues and the devs were tending to it, but I thought it had been long enough as well that anything serious would be done.
Unfortunately I feel I was wrong in that hope.
So to start with the positives, Endless Space 2 feels as if a AAA company took ES1 and spent 2 years focusing on nothing but pure immersion. The game looks spectacular and the old narrative feeling is back.
Gameplay is relatively similar, though combat has been overhauled to some extent, with tactics being a once-a-battle thing now and it's decided before-hand not mid-battle.
The new combat is great by the way. The new land battles helps add to the flavor of the game, though sometimes I feel it doesn't make sense, such as when you want 30% of your army to be aircraft and you end up with loadouts you can't control where you might have 80 infantry, 30 tanks, and 2 aircraft.
From there we get onto some more disappointing points.
Firstly is performance. A game of Endless Space 2 is meant to run about 300 turns. If you play on slow, about 450 turns. But with my own specs of an i7-6700K, GTX 1080Ti and 16GB RAM, on top of having the game on an SSD, performance becomes sloppy inside 150 turns with ease. Battles start having random stutters and turns themselves slow down to some extent (Though I will give it credit for not being anywhere near as bad as Firaxis' trademark mega waits for Civilization turns)
We come to the two points now that I feel are the most critical in why I'm unfortunately disappointed so far:
1: The AI.
The AI feels incomplete. It mocks you every few turns like clockwork, simply tells you what it's going to do in a few turns (Like going to war), and its ability to build up its own empire is...strange at best.
The AI manages to expand rapidly at the start. I'm not the most experienced player but on normal I definitely felt the AI outpaced me by miles in the early-game periods. However that quickly changes as the AI gets bogged down over nothing and thus doing nothing. An AI can go to war with you and simply never try to attack, or when they do it's for the one system they seem to want and that's it, or they just want to abduct people for 30 turns.
From a diplomacy standpoint the AI is full-on idiotic. An AI declares war on you due to having the opportunistic trait and you are at war already, but you take 10 systems off of them and they will still simply refuse peacedeals point blank when the war is about to wipe them out the game. It simply feels like the AI barely takes anything into account, and ultimately after about 100+ turns I feel like the AI just falls apart entirely.
On a side note, if you get an AI ally, they will go to war without saying anything, then insult you for not helping every 3-4 turns, but there is simply no way to be asked to join a war or offer, you just have to know who they are at war with and do it manually. It might work but it's impractical in this day-in-age for a 4X game.
For the second point, we have UI and events.
I enjoy the atmosphere of Endless Space and I like the overall gameplay, but I swear that I have *never* seen a game with such blatant disregard for player input as Endless Space 2. The standard 4X events are practically full-screen on this game, and they will pop up almost randomly. Sometimes a start-of-turn event will popup 10-15 seconds after you are navigating some other menu. There is no coherency between menu panels because you will get an option to go see something, click it, and then it has simply replaced it with a new event to go see something else.
Ultimately the events could outspam a dedicated spambot on reddit, with the game basically mandating that you try and manually turn off as many of the more pointless events as possible so you can feel sane when you click end-turn.
Update: So I've put a bit more time in, another 5-6 hours and found a few new issues. Some petty, some outrageous:
- The AI shutting its borders whilst you blockade them appears to despawn your blockading fleet from the game, but it keeps it in your lists and keeps charging you for it, you effectively lose the ships permanently. If this is otherwise, the game is not saying. (So I just lost about 1.2M dust worth of ship value and it's now draining 9,000 manpower a turn at random. Seems to be 100% broken)
-AI's late-game tactics appear to be trying to spam one planet with 5-6 bad fleets so that they can keep it permanently guarded and keep getting land battles in, even though they cannot win a single space battle
-Even trying to work out what treaties you have with everyone is a serious hassle. You might as well write them down because unless you are allowed to cancel it right now, you can't see what treaties are there.
-Performance has become cripplingly low in terms of turn timers and just trying to get battles to load, this is by turn 200-210 on a 300-turn game on a large map with 8 players...
-Nothing and I mean *nothing* scales properly in this game. I make 9,000 dust a turn but the AI offers me peace and 39 dust per turn. At the start of my latest game, with 3 systems in my empire, a minor system asked me to build 18 buildings in 15 turns...suffice to say that was impossible.
-Lastly, I won a supremacy game and it turned around and told me to go to the score screen, only to sit on the loading menu for 3 minutes and never load it at all.
End of Update
In summary, I want to reiterate that overall I do like the game. I feel the best way to describe Endless Space 2 is it feels like a AAA company made it, but it's as if they've never done anything even remotely similar to this game before. I enjoy the game for only as long as the events can be kept at bay (Which they often can't) and the AI stays competent(which again it often doesn't).
I'm going to have to say that even on sale, you might be disappointed with the state it is in, despite how visually appealing it is and how great the core gameplay itself still is too. I would check back and see if the devs have been able to alleviate at least the AI in the future.
After all the stuff I posted in the update section, I have to say this is an even greater disappointment than I thought. It's a shame because Endless Space 1 is great. You are better off just playing the original, as this sequel doesn't deserve to be in the same series.

I am very happy with Endless Space 2. I liked the original game, have truly enjoyed the refinements added in Endless Legend, with faction specific quests and overall improvements made. Now, ES2 is another improvement made on the series.
+ absolutely crisp, elegant graphics (as always, style is a personal preference and I like it)
+ very interesting races, with their own playstyle. Entangle systems in the "roots" of a giant tree? Buy whole planets with cash? Twist time or simply play the science game?
+/- As always, the tech tree is a bit of a challenge. So many options, radial progression along spokes of a wheel. Interestingly enough, you have to balance. Terraforming or a new weapon? Happyness for your pops or a new space ship class? The search function helps to find important things like command points.
- Spaceship design. Yes, all the basics are there. Hulls, thruster types, special resource weapons, armor and shields. But they all are a bit too generic, no really surprises. Lazors, slugs or torpedoes? What about time bending local distortion cannons, swarm launchers, acid goo? A bit more daring and faction unique designs, please.
+/- Space combat. While an improvement over the old system, the tactics are not a bit better. It is still an absolute passive, coffee-brake-sit-back-and-enjoy-the-show event. Mass usually wins.
+/- Ground combar. The ground combat is actually more challenging as you have to assemble enough starship troopers to invade and the ground resistance can be pretty tough. You even can invest in all three forces, soldiers, tanks, air crafts. The "simple graphics" are fine for me. I still yearn for special troopers here as well. Stellaris shows the way. Psi corps, alien bug riding cavalry, smart killer bots, you name it.
Overall, I am very pleased with ES2 and will enjoy the occasional round here and there until I played through most factions.
Recommended, if you like Stellaris, Endless Space 1 or Master of Orion. I would rate is as my second best 4 X after Stellaris.

I am a HUGE Endless Legend fan and thought Endless Space 2 would be a no brainer as a game I would love.  Unfortunately, that was not the case.
Pros:
Individual factions have trully unique qualities and play styles
Cons:
-The actual "space" feels small and crowded.  You start off only getting to explore a half dozen stars, by the time you get to 10 stars the game will inform you that you have discovered 20% of the map.  Oh, you're also surounded by other empires at that point.  This is the recommended size for a large game.  Other games have 300 stars in a small game.  Space games are supposed to give you a sense of space and distance, of nothing, this game doesn't do it
-There is very little strategy in how your empire grows, you have no choice but to work with the neighborhood you landed in.  You just add modifiers with no strategy or purpose, you are just clicking buttons
-The science/research tree is PAINFUL to work with.  Over complicated, over crowded, hard to read, difficult to understand when you can read it.

I took a risk way back when and bought endless space 1. I was at first equally thrilled and bewildered by the game experience. The same applies to endless space 2. Theres a lot of creativity and imaginiation put into this game that makes it shine. But lets explore further:
Pros:
1) If you like civs series you will probably find this enjoyable. Lots of empire managment that when done right, makes you a galactic powerhouse. Unique buildings and wonders also make this game a lot of fun to plan years ahead for your empire.
2) Space exploration mixes well with grand strategy and it shows well in this game. I mean sometimes i stare at the descriptions of planets and my imagination becomes intrigued. Its hard for games to do that to me these days. So props to ES2.
3) lots of imaginiation put into the Endless civilization. you can see it evidently in the artwork, and the diversity of the species they have created for their univers.
4) The planets are pretty @ exactly 4:20 pm.
5) Lots of intresting factors to planets that can oddly at times make or break your empire. i had a solar system that was doing soo poorly it crippled my economy at times and even made me consider abandoning it all together.
6)FlyByNo is easily THE BEST choice for a soundtrack for grand strategy games. FlyByNo will hopefully be ES2 ONLY choice in music for future games, you can get lost in empire management and great music.
Cons:
1) the fighting can be a bit dull. BUT i knew what i was getting into. If you're a total war fan you probably wont like the combat in this game. Its more cinematic mixed with strategy and fleet compisition. it is beautiful to watch though.
2) Much of the political intrigue is intresting at first but turns tedious and dull fast. Its more like "Choose this for this buff" or "choose this for this negative effect.... but you can keep some gold". There are no Petyr Baelishs hiding in this game.
3) They used to have carriers with smalls bombers and fighters in endless space 1. However, there are carrier but no sub-ships in sight in this game. Whats the point of an aircraft carrier if it doesnt have aircraft?
4) inter-species relations in the game seem a bit dull. Humans hate each other over everything including (but not limited to)  when to worship, how to worship, who to worship, who to cheer for at the super bowl, when to wear a hate, when not to wear a hat, when to kneel during the national anthem, when not to kneel during the national anthem, whos better Mcgregor or merryweather. The species on your planets (even memeber of a race your currently at war with) seems to just accept life and each other. I cant understand why happiness isnt affected by jingoism, xenophobia, and or racism. Something that Witcher 3 tackled head on.
Conclusion: i beleive you will not dislike this game. but if your unsure. try ES1. its cheaper and much the same to a degree. if you like civs more and cant stand space exploration try Endless Legend.

Well, after being very disappointed a few months ago in early access and right at release, I decided to give ES2 another try after some major patches.
And boy, did they really make some improvements. The AI is much, MUCH better than before, as they actually do things and can actually *gasp* win the game if you allow it! The save game bug that corrupts saves is gone. I have successfully played 4 full campaigns with no issues. The awful slowdowns in combat and in later stages of the game is gone. I can play with most of the galaxy discovered with tons of fleets and things moving around and it's still totally playable.
All the races are quite unique from each other, and a lot are fun to play. I will admit, some seem a bit weaker than others, like Unfallen, the slow trees of do-nothing. But overall, they're all very cool and fun to play. This is one of the biggest points of the Endless games, the asymmetrical races.
There are some glaring balance issues. Currently, Trade Companies are ridiculous in their exponential growth. You just start maxing yourself out of luxury resources and start raking in an unimaginable amount of Dust. The AI will actually do this too, and most people currently have economic victory turned off. If you play a 450 turn game, it is very easy for a Lumeris who spawned across the galaxy to win by turn 200~, from straight economy. On higher difficulties this is more of a problem because of the innate AI bonuses.
TL;DR
Overall, so much has improved for free, and the game has changed quite a bit. 4 months ago I probably would not recommend this game to anyone. But now, after replaying it a bunch, I can confidently recommend this to anyone. Big updates like fighters/bombers are also coming soon, and for free.

I've played a few games so far, and I have had quite a bit of fun.  The differences between the various races are pronounced enough that your strategy with them changes enough.  I am a huge fan of Civilization, don't get me wrong, but often the civs there aren't different enough to change game strategy.  Playing a game as the unfallen is quite a bit different than playing a game as the Sophons.
I also like how the devs are testing patches as mods.  Its easy for them, and those who want to can test the patch and report bugs.  It makes for smoother patch releases with less bugs.  I wouldn't be surprised to see more devs doing this.
This game is a step up from its predecessor.  I would recommend it for anyone who has the patience for turn based 4X games.

I spent days playing this game,and I enjoyed myself. Playing with a friend or two is highly recommended,given they can afford all the DLCs.
In CK2,you are in control of the ruler that rules an empire,kingdom,duchy or county. You have relations with everyone character from your castle and others'. The idea here is,your character dies (or gets killed),your successor has to be one of your dynasty,and needs to make your primary title his/her primary title,and you get to continue playing with your new ruler. Game has succession, diplomacy,laws,plots,titles,religions,cultures,claims and many more medieval times mechanics.This can make the game a little overwhelming for new players,but as you begin to see the cogs that work the machine that is CK2,you start to enjoy the game.
This game is also notorious for it's insane number of DLCs.Some of them are great additions that add new mechanics to the game,and allow the game to keep going after all these years,but the sheer amount of them makes the game inaccesible for some.
Definitely recommended if you are a grand strategy fan.

This game has been a great experience when it hasn't been loading or lagging, which means after I got my GPU upgraded to a Gigabyte GeForce GTX 1050 Ti d5 4Gb, the game has been running a stable 60fps on little over the medium settings and I've been able to fully enjoy this game. Playing with friends on a dedicated hosted server would be an absolute blast, I'd imagine, it's just that not all of them would be able to run this game on their PCs.
One thing that is on the other hand, great, but can get really annoying are the constant 500Mb updates almost every other day.
There is a LOT of stuff you can do while playing ARK, like taming the best dinos, exploring caves, building cool bases and killing bosses, but when you're not doing that, everything can feel just too grindy. That's why, if you're playing singleplayer, I highly recommend you to turn the resource gathering/taming speed/xp gain way up for you not to lose your interest in the game.
The developers have made a great job making this game good for the multiplayer experience, but also have made it enjoyable for singleplayer with the adjustable speeds of doing stuff and the storyline.
As a final conclusion i've listed the pros and cons as my opinion on the game.
Pros:
- Lots and lots of gameplay to experience
- Constantly updated (also a con)
- Even better with friends
- Not that hard to climb back up if you die and lose your stuff
- You can get the feeling "Hey, I know that dino!" and it feels really good
- Lots of options for doing stuff, like how will you build your base and where
- Steam workshop mod integration if you get bored to the main game
Cons:
- Can be a really laggy game on older PCs due to poor optimisation
- Constant updates (also a pro) because they can be really annoying to download almost every other day
- Very grindy game when the harvest speeds are lower
- There are still a lot of bugs to fix

Easily one of my most favorite games ever. So much time spent on it, and you don't notice the hours fly by. The game is very much oriented around your dynasty, establishing alliances and relationships with other lords, manuevering your family in position to expand, and then, once your current ruler dies, having to struggle to ensure you don't lose it all. A very in-depth game with a steep learning curve, but a truly rewarding experience once you've figured it out, and endless replay value. The combat aspect isn't nearly as strong, mostly comes down to who has the bigger army (obviously a few other factors, the terrain, who is leading the army, attacking / defending), but the game's strength is clearly in the diplomatic aspect. If you have the opportunity to pick this up, do so.

The top space 4x right now or perhaps just 4x for that matter. If you are a player of games where you build empires and maintain resources in a turn based format then this is about the best on the market. Other games this compares to are Civilization, Stellaris, Sins of a Solar Empire.
If you are familiar with 4x games then this should be a fairly easy game to pick up as you will quickly recognize tools available to you empire. If you are new to empire building one of the more brilliant moves Endless titles use are simple mnemonic art and icons for everything. Will this tech increase production? Yes, because it has a gear and it's artwork is orange, just like the planets that increase production, just like the production icon everywhere else. Will this building increase science? Yes, because it's blue and it has a beaker icon listed as output, the same as the bar that tracks your overall empire science output. Despite these visual hints being hidden all over the art style is smoothly stylized and the UI clean.
Game balance and a lack of unique civilizations are perhaps the only drawback at the moment. From my own experiece, certain races are just really better off due to their racial abilities, however it seems the developer may still be tweaking these slightly. The majority of the factions are quite different so that each one is almost like learning to play a new game. however there are only 8, which seems like not a lot compared to Stellaris and Civ. This is likely an area where more factions will be added, likely as small DLC's as they were with Endless Legend.

Honestly one of the best games I have played in a LONG time. There are very few games that I sink a lot of time and dedication into, and this is one of them. 500 hours played so far and I'm more than happy to put in 500 more.
Some of the things I love about this game are:
- Extremely well optimized, even for lower end computers and potatoes. This is because of DE's Evolution Engine, which is their own engine that they have spent a lot of time developing and perfecting. The game runs extremely smoothly, with beautiful visuals on all settings. The only place where it might start to lag on lower end PCs is the Plains of Eidolon, but the plains are a super large open area, so that is to be expected.
- Super fun PvE (and PvP if you're into it) gameplay. You have a super large variety of weapons to choose from, for primaries, secondaries, and melees, including your standard assault rifles, shotguns, SMGs, bows, and even a f***ing laser cannon of death. Melee play is also really fun, especially if you have Volt. Every warframe is fun in its own way, and serves a primary purpose (killing lots of enemies, keeping enemies away, or supporting teammates through buffs, heals, energy, etc...), but can also take on other roles.
- No defined endgame. The endgame can be anything for the player; it is solely up to them to decide. Some decide to go through the entire star chart, from Earth to Sedna and into the Void. Some have gone to far lengths to design the best looking warframes (fashionframe!) and share their designs with others. Some might decide to get the highest mastery rank, or play with all the weapons in the game! No matter what your end goal is, there is definitely something out there that you can do after clearing the star chart.
- An extremely supportive and active community, with very few toxic people. The amount of toxic people I've met in my time in Warframe I could probably count on two hands. Meanwhile in games like Overwatch and League, which I've got similar play time on, I see toxic people almost every other match. I've never seen a community more supportive than Warframe's. Going on the WF subreddit there are a large amount of resources and support you will get from many people, including tutorials, advice, builds, and occasionally the super nice people who will get you started with basic mods and are willing to help you out with your first few planets. Chances are you'll meet many people who are like this in your WF time, so if you are ever stuck or need help, feel free to simply ask!
- Beautiful cinematics and deep lore if you know where to look for it. The Second Dream and The War Within quests are simply some of the best ones I've ever seen in WF and I can certainly appreciate the time and effort that DE took to perfect these quest lines. I'm super excited for the next main story quest line (Umbra if i remember correctly) too! There's also some really good lore out there that you can read. Scan as many cephalon fragments as you can!
- The fact that Platinum (the premium currency) can be traded between players. Basically, you don't need to actually buy plat, although you certainly can if you want to support DE and keep the flow of plat in the economy going strong. The only thing that have to be bought using real money are things like TennoGen skins, many of which are relatively cheap. By buying them you support the people who designed these skins, which is a huge plus!
There's a lot of other great things about this game, however I need to talk about the main problem with WF.
For new players, it's a huge timesink. You will need quite a large amount of time invested to truly have fun. When you first get started, you start off with weapons like the Braton and Kunai, which are good in early levels but afterwards you'll start getting bored with them. The stats on these early weapons are bad (2% crit chance and status chance are painful), and modding them is a nightmare as you cannot make them viable above level 30 enemies (Uranus onward). However once you have higher mastery ranks, you'll get access to much more powerful weapons. By MR4, you'll be able to get weapons like the Hek, Lex, and Atterax, all of which are very strong weapons that are also easy to get for beginners.
Warframe rewards patience and time. The more you put into it, the more it gives back. I'd 100% recommend this game to anyone who wants a fun PvE shooter with lots of mobility and dashing around. Super satisfied with everything so far. Seriously, give it a go. You won't be disappointed.

Never do you play a game that has no clones, or at least not as good as it. That game is L.A. Noire.
Lets look at the Pros, Mixed, and Cons.
+ Very fun gameplay. I want to let you know that this game IS a puzzle game, but not as you might expect. You have to find certain clues, not doing any stupid pushing ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t. It's very fun and addictive, and wants me to have more of it. Also, there is some shooting and driving involved. However, if you wanted this to be a GTA in 1940, then you will be disappointed. However, you should love it, even if puzzles are not your thing.
+ The Sound if FANTASTIC. If I had to rate this game on Sound, it would be a 10.5/10. It's that DAMN GOOD. The soundtrack is great and so 1940s! In fact, I noticed a lot of music from Fallout 3 in here, which also has awesome music. The voice acting is also perfect. It sounded like it could have been real detectives.
+ The graphics are pretty dang sweet. The character models, especially their faces, are great. I never noticed bad lip-syncing, unlike most other games. I know there is one issue invloving graphics, but I will later address that in the review.
+ A long story. It took me around 24 hours to beat L.A. Noire, and I was not rushing. It's fantastic well it lasts. However, well it lasts.
+ Side Missions. They are not that good, but not bad either. It is nice that they added this, so this will not go against the review.
Mixed:
- 30 FPS capped. This would be a huge con IF it were not for a damn good explanation. So, this game was originally a console game, just like Red Dead Redemption (By the way rockstar, add it onto Steam. I don't care that it's almost 5 years old, I really want to play it) As we know, a lot of console games are locked at 30 FPS (Destiny, Fallout 4, etc.) However, Rockstar noticed there was a huge problem. The lip-syncing on PC was not good at all. They had a total of 4 choices: 1. Let there be bad lip-syncing, removing points from the PC review. 2. Redo THE ENTIRE GAME FOR PC, which could have taken a long time. 3. Make the gameplay 60 FPS, but the faces 30 FPS, possibly making bad lag, as well as confusing most people. 4. Keep it the same, but face there will be only be regular players who will outrage. I think 4 was the safest bet, plus it does not run that bad. At 30 FPS, it is fantastic. However, I still wish there was at least an option.
Cons:
- The gameplay gets boring a bit fast. After the 30th time of having a shoot out, it gets tiring. However, only the shooting. The interviews and car driving never get old.
- This game has glitches, which might not seem bad, until I tell you. Screen-tearing, graphical glitches, and more are only uncommon, not rare.
- Very little replay value. There is no second route, like GTA, Fallout, or Elder Scrolls. The next time you play it, it will be the same, which makes it boring. However, there is DLC if you can not get enough, which you would have to be crazy to not be.
FINAL VERDICT
9/10

This is the type of game that features excellent acting, story, writing, and dialogue, but is missing the most important element of any video game: good gameplay. Slogging through each and every case in L.A. Noire felt like an absolute chore, and the thing that kept me going was my desire to view the story. This is one of the few games where I was more interested in the cutscenes than the actual game itself.
My primary issue with L.A. Noire was that everything felt very forced. I started playing under the impression that I would be filling the role of a detective and be forced to think and make choices with every seemingly minute detail possibly being important. That is simply not what happens. The game does not let you come to your own conclusions and it does not let you be the detective. Rather, everything has been decided in advance and you are simply shuffled along through the story. For every action you take, every choice you make, there is a right one and a wrong one.
A good example of this would be accusing the wrong man. Let's say that, after reviewing the evidence, you come to the conclusion that person X is guilty. So you accuse person X. If person Y was the right choice, then your boss will give you a scolding about how you've destroyed the whole case. This makes little sense. It gives the impression that throughout the whole case, your boss already knows who is truly guilty.
This becomes even more of a problem as cases start to get more and more complicated. In one instance during the game, I knew a certain character was guilty. Let's call him Bob. The evidence, combined with a gut-feeling, gave me the impression that Bob was my guy. Unfortunately, the game did not want me to pick Bob. The only 'right' choice I could make was to accuse the other guy (call him Steve). So I went against my own judgement and picked Steve. Later on, I learned that, lo and behold, Steve was innocent the whole time. Instead of letting me accuse the guilty man, the game forced me to accuse the innocent one just so that later on my 'mistake' could play a role in the plot.
That is the biggest issue with L.A. Noire. The story is fantastic, but it is very force-fed and you are not allowed to deviate from it all. This raises the question of why L.A. Noire needed to be a video game to begin with. I would much rather have been allowed to simply press play and watch it, instead of having to work my way through its gameplay. I felt like an actor; like I was being made to follow a script.
Another issue of concern I will speak to briefly is the control. Having to rotate pieces of evidence instead of simply picking them up is tedious and unnecessary. I found myself constantly frustrated by having to painstakingly rotate an object to the exact correct angle before the game counts it as being seen. The cover and fighting mechanics also could have benefited from some polishing. Many times I died simply because the player character downright refused to follow my commands.
To conclude, L.A. Noire has an excellent story to tell, and characters with plenty of depth that are all uniquely interesting. Unfortunately, it is plagued by hand-holding and terrible gameplay. L.A. Noire is an excellent example of why games should be games, and movies should be movies.

Pros

The short and sweet: if you love space themed 4X turn-based grand strategy, you have to play this game.
It has scratched every itch I have for spaceships, space exploration, all-other-space-stuff AND galaxy-spanning empire building with planetary colonizing/development, technology research, resource management, ship/fleet customizing, and of course cinematic combat. I'll go into more detail about a few of my favorite things in ES2.
FLEET/SHIP CUSTOMIZATION:
---------------------------------------------------
This is the stuff I eat up. I've spent countless hours designing variants of each ship class/hull to fulfill a need; scouts with more firepower to ward off pirates as they explore, destroyers with more shielding to counteract my energy-weapon fleeted galactic neighbors, trimmed-down battleships with enhanced engine drives and sensor-boosting support modules for quick reaction and response fleets, and of course my personal favorite the supermassive "dreadnought" heavy weapons platform.
COMBAT:
---------------------------------------------------
Very similar to ES1 in that you make your tactical decisions when the battle begins, then watch it unfold cinematically. The tactical options available to you are chosen and "equipped" from a larger pool of available tactics, with new tactics and more equip-slots being unlocked as you progress. Personally, I love this system. Most of the work is done in my fleet design and composition; I choose the tactical option best suited to the situation or my fleet type, then watch the fruits of my labors as I turn opposing fleets into floating bits of molten slag.
VISUALS:
---------------------------------------------------
The tremendous variety in planet types, star types, anomolies you encounter, and detail is fantastic. As your planets develop and prosper, you will see lights from cities and the circling dots of spacecraft orbitting it. When you discover planets with an anomaly or special attribute (such as rings, moons, storms, etc...) they will actually have that detail visually present. When your fleet is waylaid by a pirate ambush while passing by a blackhole or nebula, you will see the battle take place in that setting.
EMPIRE BUILDING/RESOURCE MANAGEMENT:
---------------------------------------------------
The depth and detail here is astounding. ES2 should be a gold standard to follow for space-based 4X games in the future. The different resource types, effects, and uses, offers a great deal of flexibility in how you can build and develop your empire. The types of planets you colonize can have benefits and drawbacks in certain areas, for example; snowy/cold worlds are well suited for the construction of research buildings and increasing scientific output of your empire, but food production and happiness of your colonists will slow growth potential and will need special consideration. The racial composition of your populations on each planet will have an effect (some alien races are better suited to industry, war, science, etc etc) and can also be micro-managed. Did you assimilate a people living on a fertile planet whose innate talents can increase food production on barren/infertile planets? You can move your population around to maximize your empire's efficiency.
I could go on and on.
With the amount of fun I've had playing this game, I have to recommend it to anyone even mildly interested in it.

I am a HUGE Endless Legend fan and thought Endless Space 2 would be a no brainer as a game I would love.  Unfortunately, that was not the case.
Pros:
Individual factions have trully unique qualities and play styles
Cons:
-The actual "space" feels small and crowded.  You start off only getting to explore a half dozen stars, by the time you get to 10 stars the game will inform you that you have discovered 20% of the map.  Oh, you're also surounded by other empires at that point.  This is the recommended size for a large game.  Other games have 300 stars in a small game.  Space games are supposed to give you a sense of space and distance, of nothing, this game doesn't do it
-There is very little strategy in how your empire grows, you have no choice but to work with the neighborhood you landed in.  You just add modifiers with no strategy or purpose, you are just clicking buttons
-The science/research tree is PAINFUL to work with.  Over complicated, over crowded, hard to read, difficult to understand when you can read it.
- Ship design is ridiculously simple and you really get few options for meaningful customization.  One of the biggest failings.  Ship design is more about your research speed than any "design"
- The general flow of the game is not intuitive and the tutorial is horrible.  I've played hundreds of hours of Endless legend, the land based fantasy 4x game from the same publisher.  I've played many hundreds of hours of other space 4x games.  I should be able to relatively easily figure out this game, it should be intuitive.  It is not.  I tried using the tutorial to figure it out and it is really bad.  A good tutorial walks you step by step through the process.  This one has you do a couple steps, then doesn't tell you what to do/learn next, then while your working through another screen it pops up again.
I had been looking forward to this game.  I wanted to LOVE this game.  I tried playing four different games, four different factions, and all of them were clunky, difficult to figure out, and it just wasn't fun.  After about ten hours it was clear that all you really do is click buttons without really paying attention to what they do, and click through your turns.  Wish I could write a better review, I really wanted this to be my new go to space game, but after just a few hours it's doesn't have it.

To resume L.A. Noire quickly, it's the story of a LAPD cop named Cole Phelps and his rise & fall in the police system, all while questioning a bunch of people about various crimes. This game manages to immerse you into the past, in the late 40's as a LA police officer trying to climb the ladder.
I like alot of things about this game: The ambience, the music, the facial system, the captivating storyline, the relevance of almost everything placed in the decor, the dialogue, etc, and the list goes on. Rockstar/Team Bondi (R.I.P.) have done an amazing job on this game, making sure to create a different feel than in their previous games (such as Bully or GTA). There is no other game like this one, and that's a quality I love when it comes to good games.
The story will run you at the very minimum at least 26 hours (DLC included) and you can then retry past cases individually to try and get better. I like to play through L.A. Noire about once every 1/1,5 years (it's kinda like a movie, where it's as enjoyable as the first time once you let some time pass and come back to it).
I would recommend getting the complete edition of this game to any fan of Noire TV series or movies, and fans of well scripted detective games. DO NOT come into L.A. Noire expecting exactly the same as GTA but as a cop in the 40's because you will be very dissapointed. That being said, the game is amazing, probably the most immersive game i've played.

This game is like Marmite, you either love it or you hate it.
Personally, I love it, but I can understand why people hate it.
You can build huge bases with rainbow lighting and fill it with lots of wacky dinosaurs. You can raise your own dinosaurs too, which is time consuming, but rewarding. There's an awful lot to do, and you can easily sink hundreds or even thousands of hours into it, but it has some serious downsides:
- The glitches. So. Many. Glitches. Regular glitches ranging from simple crashes to rexes permanently stuck in a cliff face. I wish the devs would focus on these rather than just releasing more DLC's.

First, a brief history of my experience with 4x. I've played a lot of Civilization, from 1 up through 5. I've played a passable amount of Sins of a Solar Empire. I dabbled with Endless Space 1 and Endless Legend, but couldn't really get into them.
Endless Space 2 has grabbed my attention like few 4x games ever have. The tech web, while intimidating at first (especially because I picked Sophons to start), feels very well balanced. There are so many interlocking systems at play here that there does not feel like any catch-all, formulaic strategy - I really feel like I'm adapting to the needs of my fledgling space empire.
The setting, time wise, is pretty cool. Your people just became warp capable, essentially. Like in Endless Legend, you get faction quests that tell the story of how your people develop and adapt to their new environment. Unlike Endless Legend, you get some choice in how things play out. That often takes the form of a choice between political factions, just one of the various interdependent systems that make this game so neat.
In Endless Space 1, the combat felt really shallow and dull. It was the main reason I couldn't into that game. Here, it feels like there is better balance and more reason to bring a variety of weapon types, have multiple flotillas in a fleet, and maneuver them differently. I'd complain that the formula of "scouts with guns, frigates with missiles" is a little too effective, but honestly, that was a winning formula in Sins of a Solar Empire too.
I'm seeing a bunch of negative reviews lately. I'm not really experiencing the complaints, other than a minor de-sync issue in multiplayer. I'll allow that I may not be a good enough 4x player to notice if the AI isn't very strong. However I never play 4x solo anyway - I'm not so focused on AI behavior, but rather on just trying to make my own civ run smooth as butter while I build as tall as I can get away with, hopefully achieve a bonkers science or economy score, and win a non-aggressive victory. Between politics and approval, colonization, industry and influence, manpower, economy, various luxury resources and system development levels, planetary anomalies, trading companies, population redistribution, ground battles with customizable troop composition, cooperative and competitive universal quests, you name it - Endless Space 2 just carries this awesome feeling of managing a living, breathing empire in a way that no other game I've played has ever managed.
In my experience with these devs they always support their 4x games very strongly. This game is deep and the underlying systems feel very strong and well developed. If some feel Endless Space 2 lacks polish, then all I can say is - this game has already blown my mind. When future patches inevitably address more experienced players' concerns, I can confidently say something I never say on Steam - that the result will surely be worth full price!

Having as many hours as I have I think I am qualified to tell you if the game is good.
Ark is a great game, if you play on a private server. Official servers are a slow laggy mess run by chinese alpha tribes who spam the servers with so many people no one can muster enough people to take them on. The rates are abysmally slow to the point where the game can feel like a full time job.
I played about 150 hours on Official 78 before moving onto an accelerated private server. The game felt brand new again, with me being able to experience things that are typically blocked by alphas - caves, tamed gigas, wyverns, defendable bases and the like. A dedicated team of admins also prevents hacking and griefing by randoms.
PvP has always been kind of a beautiful chaotic mess in Ark, from stabbing a guy on the beach with a spear to a full on raid with Quetzals and explosives. Finally breaking the walls down and raiding a vault to find those resources and blueprints feels like a very real accomplishment and reminds you to keep your own base well defended!
Boss battles, while gated heavilly, are fun and challenging! Taking on the dragon with your carefully bred menagerie of various dinos truly feels epic and a culmination of everything you have worked towards. Finally ascending to the Tek Tier is one of the most rewarding experiences I have ever had in gaming!
In short, Ark is a very fun game so long as you find a good private server with a few friends. Official servers are a mess and will likely be for a long time if not forever, but that won't stop you from having a great time.

I’m going to start this review out by saying that I was somewhat on the fence before my purchase of L.A. Noire.  I’m a fan of Rockstar and the majority of their games, but there was something about this game that had me a little anxious.  Now that I’ve played it, here’s what I think.
This is, no doubt, a detective game.  There’s no pusyfooting around that fact.  Most of your time will be spent doing one of three things.  Running down escaping felons, performing interrogations where you have to judge the honesty of the witness/accused, and searching for clues.  That pretty much sums up the game.  Oh, and there’s driving.
I want to focus for a moment on the interrogations.  The faces of the characters in L.A. Noire have been very highly detailed.  It’s these details, as well as the way the individual sounds and acts, that give you clues if they’re telling you the truth when they answer your questions.  If you suspect they’re lying, it’s up to you to then link one of the clues to the lie.  You succeed, you catch them in the lie.  You fail, you lose the ability to use that question again.  This is probably the most difficult part of the game, and I failed miserably on my first 8 tries at the “tutorial” interrogation (which loops until you get it right).
While I found the interrogation aspect of the game to be a rather successful way of immersion into the role of a detective it seemed the rest of the game somewhat broke that immersion.  It was almost like playing two games that really weren’t meant to be played together.  On one hand you had the GTA style game play that we all know, and on the other hand this extremely high level of story-based investigative detail.  I found myself wanting to “GTA” the hell out of this game whenever I was driving around or trying to stop an escaping felon, but this game punishes you for doing so.  Everything that was fun in GTA is basically prohibited from the “GTA” side of this game, thus making that entire portion of this game very boring.
Talking about the GTA aspects of this game, I found the driving to be very awkward.  This game is supposed to be replicating cars from the 40’s but they certainly don’t act like cars from the 40’s.  The most unbelievable aspect of these cars is how tight they can turn.  I mean, you can be flying along and the dam things will almost turn on a dime.  The same can’t be said for stopping.  I know early cars were heavy, but these things stop worse than an overloaded big-rig.  I highly doubt any car, from any time period, would slide an entire block on pavement when you slam on the brakes.
All in all this game felt like a rollercoaster.  Whenever you were talking to a witness or searching for clues you were almost on the edge of your seat with anticipation and enjoyment, but when you were playing “GTA” you were so restricted from having fun that you ended up bored to hell just waiting for it to be over.
So what’s the verdict?  Do I regret my purchase?  Well… No, because I got it on sale for 80% off.  Would I buy it at full price?  Again, No.  The game has a lot of positives but some aspects of it are so boring that you have trouble staying interested in the game as a whole.  Sorry Rockstar, I just can’t recommend it.

I'm giving this a thumbs-up because I like Amplitude and feel that I have gotten my money's worth from this game, but wow - Endless Space 2 is a real disappointment. It's a beautiful game that suffers from very poorly thought-out mechanics and a lack of real substance. Amplitude need to shake things up and just start over with their next title - if ES2 is the epitome of where they are headed from a mechanics standpoint, they are in trouble.
Pros
- Fantastic production values - great graphics, music, etc.
- Interesting factions, as usual with Amplitude games
Cons
- The writing is mind-bogglingly puerile. Seriously, who wrote the text for this game? A twelve year old? The comically juvenile writing completely clashes with the otherwise serious tone. It reminds me of the best man speech at a recent wedding - funny, but in an embarrassing, groan-inducing way.
- The tech tree is, quite frankly, incredibly boring. In good 4x games, the tech tree forces the player to make interesting, difficult decisions and trade offs. Here, it just felt incredibly bland, and a great deal of it is simply unlocking the ability to actully utilize planets in systems you've already colonized.  Boring.
- The tactical combat elements are really bad.  Like the first Endless Space, the player has no real control - battles are basically cinematics with no player interaction. Yet somehow, the devs have managed to make space (and ground) combat even less interesting than in Endless Space 1.  Very disappointing.
- The new political aspects of the game (elections, factions, etc.) are a complete train wreck. They add very little and are simply annoying.
- The interface is very slick-looking, but at the same time rather obtuse.  At several points I stared at it and just scratched my head wondering how the devs intended the information presented to be useful.

Do not play this game expecting a GTA+Mafia hybrid.
Though it is closer to Mafia than it is to GTA, it still stands on its own.
Now I wanted to recommend this game, I really did, but there are more things wrong than there are good, which tips my scale towards not recommended.
@Pros:
+Provides a great social commentary on 1940s Los Angeles, I believe it very well captures the good and the bad about people's mentality of that time.
+Great map design, even the map captures 1940s very well.
+Great attention to details, basically everything in this game describes 1940s very accurately, details like traffic lights, cigars, cars, news papers, music, clothes, guns and much more.
+Facial expressions recorded from real actors, giving realistic expressions, making the "Lie", "Doubt" or "Truth" choice system be based on people's facial expressions, as much as it is based on facts you've collected.
+The game does not hold back, they didn't cheap out for the PG rating, it is very dark in nature, and does not make an attempt in giving you false hope or flowery\holding-hands endings to the cases, from beginning to end it is very dark and realistic, just how you'd expect from a homicide investigation and chasing a serial killer, dead bodies, children burnt to a crisp and naked bodies of dead and r@ped women, kinda reminds me of the movie Se7en actually, it is SO dark in fact, it might be borderline depressing for some people.
I find this quote from Chris Stuckmann's Sicario review describes the darkness of this game well: "
" -->from 2:45 to 3:03
@Cons:
-The gameplay gets very repetitive very fast.
-The story is too linear.
-Disappointing ending.
-You can't explore the map after finishing the game, you'll have to load the save before the final mission and play from there.
-The game is god damn dark (see my Pros above)
-The game feels like it was left in the middle of development, side tasks that lead to nowhere and subplots that don't take you anywhere.
In short, if you think you can handle the dark story and imagery of this game, and you're looking for a story driven game rather than a GTA-like game, maybe grab L.A. Noire on a sale.
Otherwise I generally do not recommend it.

I can't say much about others' personal experiences, but I've totally loved the game so far. I've played a four to five hour session every time there's been a major update, and so far i'm very pleased with my purchase. It improves on the first game in every way that I can think of. The governmental system is interesting, and I love the way solar systems develop over time. Quests related to history of the Academy and the individual species are actually pretty good. I found myself continuing to play new games simply to finish the questlines. It's gorgeous to look at and the colonization and planetary specialization aspects are on point. My only complaint is that I wish there was more customizability to custom races. Stellaris has spoiled me there.
I, personally, have not had much issue with the game. A lot of reviews mention save corruption, and in my experience that's just part of the territory when it comes to early access. It hasn't happened to me since the game released in full, so I can't say much about that. I did have one issue with an earlier build where the game would crash right after launch, but that was corrected by release.
In short, it does it's own thing. It looks incredible and has some interesting aspects that are, as far as I can tell, unique to this series. It's much better than most 4X's, but it doesn't quite stack up to the greats like Galactic Civilizations II or Master of Orion II. Overall, highly recommended.

I just finished the game and I'm looking for a word to describe it but I can't find any other than 'masterpiece'. I got the Complete Edition, invested 40+ hours in it and enjoyed every single bit. I am going to write some  pros and cons and I want to mention that the cons are purely subjective.
+ Remarcably designed city and cars.
+ Formidable and progressively complex cases.
+ Well made characters and personalities.
+ Tons of historical, cinematical and musical references. I believe the work invested in the game's documentation was huge.
+ Educational stuff.
+ Much attention payed to the details even if sometimes there are mismatches.
+ Intermission movies.
+ Great soundtrack.
+ Jack Kelso .
- Car control (sometimes). It is true that the game's main goal are the cases themself but the cars and the driving  constitue a substantial part of it. The cars doesn't feel heavy enough and the driving is really arcadish especially during some chases. I don't say that it's ruining the game, it's not a car simulator, but it was a bit disappointing.
- Enemies never shoot you when you are climbing a drain pipe.
- The gunfights are pretty much easy. Except for a few, gunbattles are not challenging at all. Taking less damage before you fall it could have been more interesting or bad guys with better accuracy.
- Jack Kelso parts. Too short and too few. I loved that character and his side of the story and it wouldn't hurt to add a bit more of it.
- The ending. Left me with many unanswered questions. I was waiting for a more detailed explanation of the latest events. But I won't give any spoilers.
Overall this game was a great experience. I would give it a 10 for the design, 9+ for the action and 11 for the research behind it. Therefore I recommend it with great, great pleasure.

Similar to all of Paradox's other grand strategy titles, Crusader Kings 2 places you in the boots of one of the rulers of a medieval Duchy, kingdom or empire and playing from 1066 to 1453.  The large difference between this grand strategy and Paradox's others, is that you actually play as a character, instead of the embodiment of a nation.  Whenever you die, you play as whoever is in your line of succession.  If someone who is not part of your dynasty is your heir and you die, it's game over.  Along with this feature, you must also manage your family as well as your vassals, keeping them happy.  Nothing is more annoying than having to open up the vassal tab, sort them by the lowest opinion and then having to funnel money to 6 people to keep them happy, only to have them send you a message, labeling you a pretender of the throne a few minutes later.  Something in the game is still appealing however, and is making me reccomend it.

I think the only way to sum up my feelings for this game is that I'm tsundere for it.
I mean sure, the premise is kinda dumb. You click things. You also hire heroes to click things for you, and then you upgrade them, and then you have ancients to do cool things, you stop playing the game and you still make progress anyway, it's what you would expect from the clicker genre. Or is the genre called "idle"? But that sounds too much like "idol game" as in Idolmaster or Love Live, so I think "clicker game" is a better name.
Anyway, this does have a bit more to it than other games. More heroes, you have mercenaries to send off on quests to get stuff, there's a lot of depth.
But I still feel a bit miffed about how they patched mercenaries back whenever that happened. They made it so that they only live for a certain amount of time no matter what quests you send them on.
It's taken me a while (a long break from the game, actually) to finally accept this, because I'm a sulky little♥♥♥♥♥♥ I mean yeah, I can see why they needed to nerf them.

I can't stay mad at this game. Every time I come home from work, I always go and check on my progress. It's become sort of a comfort zone for me. No matter what happens in life, no matter how bad my depression gets, Clicker Heroes will always be there for me when nobody else was.

I'm giving this a thumbs-up because I like Amplitude and feel that I have gotten my money's worth from this game, but wow - Endless Space 2 is a real disappointment. It's a beautiful game that suffers from very poorly thought-out mechanics and a lack of real substance. Amplitude need to shake things up and just start over with their next title - if ES2 is the epitome of where they are headed from a mechanics standpoint, they are in trouble.
Pros
- Fantastic production values - great graphics, music, etc.
- Interesting factions, as usual with Amplitude games
Cons
- The writing is mind-bogglingly puerile. Seriously, who wrote the text for this game? A twelve year old? The comically juvenile writing completely clashes with the otherwise serious tone. It reminds me of the best man speech at a recent wedding - funny, but in an embarrassing, groan-inducing way.
- The tech tree is, quite frankly, incredibly boring. In good 4x games, the tech tree forces the player to make interesting, difficult decisions and trade offs. Here, it just felt incredibly bland, and a great deal of it is simply unlocking the ability to actully utilize planets in systems you've already colonized.  Boring.
- The tactical combat elements are really bad.  Like the first Endless Space, the player has no real control - battles are basically cinematics with no player interaction. Yet somehow, the devs have managed to make space (and ground) combat even less interesting than in Endless Space 1.  Very disappointing.
- The new political aspects of the game (elections, factions, etc.) are a complete train wreck. They add very little and are simply annoying.
- The interface is very slick-looking, but at the same time rather obtuse.  At several points I stared at it and just scratched my head wondering how the devs intended the information presented to be useful.
