Decent clicker game. I currently have around 200 hours on the game, and I thought it would be smart to make a review.
Graphics.
The 2D design is well produced and is enertaining, however, with a clicker game that goes on for as long as clicker heroes does, it would be good to see more variation with colour, shape and size within the monster sprites, to encourage more active (still idling though) gameplay. It would also be also interesting to see different animations for the monsters, but I do understand that there are limitations to things like this. Expanding upon the subject of the monster sprites, it would also be cool if there were different backgrounds or different colours for the small floating backgrounds. It's not much to improve on, but it would certainly make it more interesting.
Gameplay.
I get that it is and idle game, and so there must be a degree of repetitiveness, however, I would also enjoy the game more if there were some different gameplay aspects to make it a bit more niche. It would also be good if there were more online user to user participation, so that  teamwork become a more important aspect of being in a clan.
Music.
I think most people who play clicker heroes do not listen to the music, and that can be said for most idle games for obvious reasons, but I think tweaking the soundtrack would make a world of difference towards clicker heroes, I'm not saying the music is bad, but you wouldn't listen to the music without it being inside of the game itself.
Conclusion
Clicker heroes is a functionally adept game with good gameplay and enjoyable visuals with  a mediocre track. Its addictive gameplay features make it a must try for most gamers both new and experienced with the clicker/idle/incremental genre, to play and enjoy. 3.5/5

I have to say despite being somewhat 'shallow' I am enjoying the s h i t out of Endless Space 2. Maintaining approval rating may still be an utter pain in the arsye and the AI is reeeeeeally quick to go from friendly ally to warmonger fast (and the abilty to form alliances should not have to be on the farcking pointy end of the tech tree) but this is still a brillant combat-focused 4X that is excellent as a MP game.
Aformentioned combat is smooth and fluid, with postioning, formation, and tactical options all availible . They fixed the issue of ES1 of kinetic weapons being overpowered by completely changing the weaponry system and while I don't like the limit on strategic options availble I do like that Amplitude has completely redesigned them as well.
The solo and co-operative missions are rather well designed, as is the stream of events, and while they both peater off after mid game they really flesh out the universe and your empire's own story while they are there. Do wish there was more of them though.
Finally the new political system is interesting. It's not quite as well done in games like Civ II for example and often times you will be stuck with nothing but Millitants in your senate because you've been building warships for 50 turns straight. But for what its worth the laws do make a real impact on your empire. Though Amplitude really should have made buildng warships worth a lot less as their political value overpowers pretty much everything else you build. Enless, of course, you just don't build warships for a few turns...
Other things that I don't like are the rather limited options when dealing with the AI, which is probably the weakest part of the game. You can declare war/truce, cold war, peace, open/close borders., create a 'trade agreement' (which does very little), trade resouces, ships, and maps, and join an alliance. With most of these options having to be unlocked as you go.
I'm ok with diplomatic tech trees in games like Civ where it makes sense. But I'm not in a Space-Based 4X game with intergallatic empires. It's just a pointless piece of padding that I think should be removed entirely so you can access what limited options there are from the get go.
Also dealing with approval ratings on systems is sometimes an unwinnable battle if you expand too much with only a few improvements you can build to increase it before your system heads into a death spiral of overcrowding and growing resentment. This is something that could really use some free DLC as systems can now revolt if approval dips low enough. As far as I have found the only way to fix this is to stock up on luxuries that can be used to pacifcy your citizens and then terreform every world you can into something with less or no negative planet traits. Wanna keep that Barren planet you have optimised for science output? Nope! Better turn it into a Terran planet for your citizens! Of course you could always just not go too far over your limit and both the Peaceful and Warlike law trees have laws to provide massive happiness boosts but still, you will find it very hard to own every planet in this game.
Ultimatly Endless Space 2 is no Master of Orion 2 or Alpha Centauri in the cannon of Space-themed 4X games. But it does nail the process of developing systems and fighting fleet-based combat. Get it if you can convince your friends to get it or if you just want to see pretty cinematics of lazers and missles destroying huge ships and you like farcking with mathmatical improbablities.

For those who enjoy intra-family politics, feudalism, and the occasional plague, then Crusader Kings II is for you.
The game plays like most other Paradox strategy games: in real-time on a top-down board with an event driven game engine with the twist of playing as the head of a royal family in medieval Europe. In other words, it plays like if you were to mash The Sims with RISK or if The Sims Medieval were more fleshed out.
CK2 has a lot of DLC, but don't let that be too daunting. The base game is a fine game on its own. With CK2, only about a third of its DLC is gameplay affecting, and by "gameplay affecting" I mean that they unlock the ability to play characters outside of Christian Europe or earlier start dates.
Crusader Kings II can feel like a Game of Thrones emulator. So much so that there is a mod for the game that turns it into that world which is a testament to Paradox's continued support for their committed mod community.
If you're a fan of long-term strategy games like the Civilization series or enjoy generations of political and family intrigue, then this may be a game for you.
Recommended DLC:
1. Way of Life (Enhances the base game by adding a "focus" for your character, which fleshes them out and adds more interactions with other characters. Adds more depth to the game.)
2. Sons of Abraham (Adds more depth to Christianity, Islam, and adds Judaism.)
3. Legacy of Rome (Adds standing armies and factions system. Adds more depth to the Byzantine Empire and Orthodox Church.)
4. The Republic (Unlocks the ability to lead a Patrician family. Great for when you want to make loads of money not war.)
5. The Old Gods (Unlocks the ability to lead a Pagan family. Unlocks the 867 AD start date.)
6. Charlemagne (Unlocks the 769 AD start date (does not unlock the 867 start date). Charlemagne story event series. Ability to create ahistorical, fantasy kingdoms.)
7. Sword of Islam (Unlocks the ability to lead a Muslim family.)
8. Rajas of India (Unlocks the ability to lead an Indian family.)
9. Sunset Invasion (Unlocks the zany what-if scenario of Aztecs invading Europe.)

Admittedly I did get bored with the grind (again, after about 500 hours of play), but there is always new content whenever I come back to play the game. I have only paid some money for the game once to get some cosmetic items and item slots (yes, you are limited to the number of items you can hold and plat can buy you more), but I figured after the 300 or 400 hours I had already played by that point, it was worth throwing a little money their way on a 50% off deal!
So again. The grind is real. But it is not a boring grind just sitting there hitting the same button over and over again like other MMORPGs. You are an acrobatic god!

This is a stellar game for anybody who is into history or politics. One thing to keep in mind with the game is that it is a Grand Strategyu simulator, so you will not be directing battles or micromanaging troops, as combat is handled in an abstract manner.
The real appeal to the game is the alternate history and the geneology portions. Since this game is about forging a dynasty, and watching it grow, as long as you do not lose your last landed title, the game continues. This results in a style of game where you might make decisions that are ultimately not as good for your country, but benefit your family or children in the long run.
The alternate history really comes into play when you look at how the world changes based on the decisions you make, as well the decisions of the AI, or other players in a multiplayer game. For example, maybe you have a game where you're trying to unify Britain, and you glance over to the mainland for the first time in 100 years, to see Muslims on the other side of the channel, and an early ottoman style empire, or maybe you're playinbg byuzantium, and suddenly an Indian Hindu army comes rampaging across Persia.
One of the best parts of this game is that there is no defined objective, or way to play, meaning that you can do anything you want to. Do you want to conquer the world as reformed Norsemen, or try to unite all of christendom under the sole rule of the Emperor in Constantinople? Or would you rather start as a minor duke in the Holy Roman Empire, and merely maintain control over your ancestral lands? You can do that, in CK2.

Clicker Heroes starts off simply enough, a few clicks here, a few there and you've slain your first handful of creatures and netted yourself a handful of gold. Now with cash in hand, you can buy your first upgrade and increase the damage your clicks do, or hold out a little longer to buy a hero that will automatically dish out the pain. Every fifth level features a boss creature, these monsters have much more HP than a monster on a regular zone, and they have to be defeated within 30 seconds, meaning that a certain amount of damage per second needs to have been achieved in order to continue.
This cycle continues, and soon enough you'll have a small group of heroes dealing damage by the millions, billions, trillions etcetera, but that is all there is to it, no plot, no story, just endless creatures and constantly depleting health bars. You wait until you have enough gold to buy upgrades that increase your damage output so that you can progress to levels that require even more damage to pass. Then you wait some more. It's highly repetitive, and once you clear the first hundred or so zones, they repeat themselves too, but this time with more powerful creatures, which again are just the same ones as before but with more health. The background music is repetitive too, with only one track on a constant loop, but thankfully it can be turned off in the game menu.
Certain heroes will grant players additional abilities, such as Clickstorm that automatically clicks 10-times a second for 30 seconds, or Power surge that doubles your hero's DPS for 30 seconds. These extra abilities can be useful in a pinch or for taking out boss creatures whose health is otherwise too high for you. They can't be used constantly, as each one is on a cooldown that varies between 10 minutes and eight hours, forcing you to wait for the right time to use them. It adds a little bit of additional player interaction to the game, but once you have your heroes leveled up enough, the game largely plays itself.
Once level 100 has been cleared, passing every 10th level for the first time grants players with a random hero becoming gilded. Once gilded a hero receive a 50% increase to their damage, this bonus stacks each time they receive a new gild, providing a decent damage boost, and one that persists through ascension, but more on that in a moment. Gilding a hero will also give them a new appearance, but you don't really spend much time looking at the heroes small artwork in the menus so this goes mostly unnoticed.
Clicker Heroes lures you in, constantly promising that the next upgrade is just a few minutes away and it will provide enough of a boost to your DPS to propel you further, that the cooldowns you are waiting on will be enough to tip the scales on the next boss. It's this that makes the game addictive, you always feel like you will be able to make some progress if you just wait a little while longer, and the fact that the game mostly plays itself means that you can go off and cook your dinner, or do some chores that you've been putting off, and come back to an extra chunk of gold to spend on something else and somehow feel like you've actually achieved something. Even when the console is turned off the game continues to generate gold; returning to the game after a few hours or the next day grants you a hefty chunk of money based on your level and the amount of DPS your heroes deal. In the end, though, you will be doing a lot of waiting.
Invariably there comes a time where your damage just isn't cutting it anymore, or the next upgrade is just too far away. It's at this point where players will choose to ascend, an ability granted to you by Amenhotep, one of the many heroes. When a player chooses to ascend, everything resets apart from any gilded heroes, collected relics or unlocked Ancients. Now back at Level 1, Enemies will die quicker, money will come faster and more progress will likely be made on the next playthrough before the grind once again hits and you’ll need to ascend again. It’s a good way to add replayability, but with at least 3600 levels, according to the achievements, it seems like a little bit of overkill to require players to replay levels over and over gain in order to progress further and adds to the already massive amount of time players will need to sink into the game in order to progress.
Ascending also grants players Hero Souls, an extra currency that can be spent on buying and levelling up the aforementioned ancients. The number of Hero Souls you receive when you ascend is proportional to the total number or levels your heroes have gained, the more money you have spent on your heroes, the more Hero Souls you will receive. Ancients grant various bonuses, such as Fragsworth, Ancient of Wrath who increases click damage, or Libertas, Ancient of Freedom who increases the amount of gold received while the game is idle. Unspent Hero Souls grant a bonus to your DPS, so choosing between upgrading your Ancients or holding on to the extra damage can be a difficult decision, and it seems that the best way to proceed is to only spend a few on bonuses that will help you to proceed quickly and keep some Souls back to boost your damage. Unfortunately, the game doesn't give you any hints on how best to proceed and much of it comes down to trial and error, or some extensive research online.
Clicker Heroes is a freemium game, so of course, it has microtransactions. Rubies are the special currency that players can buy with their own real world money to speed proceedings up, and they can be spent on bonuses such as gilding three random heroes, or advancing the time by eight hours to reset your cooldowns and receive a large boost to your gold. You don’t have to purchase them, as they can also be earned through general play. When a little fish — or a fish made out of an orange, I'm not completely sure what it is supposed to be — appears on screen, inputting the displayed button command, will grant players a small boost to their gold, but on occasion will also reward them with a ruby or two.

Early Access Watcher Reviews Youtuber Life
Update Version: 0.7.4
Disclosure: This game copy was bought by the reviewer.
Message to the Developer: I usually never try to make something stand out like this, but I am urging you to be extremely careful with some of the items in your game. The "Pikachu" hat for instance can lead down some dark holes considering how trigger happy Nintendo can be.
Message over.
YouTube has created an opportunity for normal people to become famous with the simple creation of visual media. Let's Plays to politics, culinary excellence to downright stupidity, a video has been enough to make a person immortal in this day and age. That fame is not always easily won and it can take years of slow, painful dedication before getting the right boost needed to start raking in the subscribers. From the bedroom of your mother's home to a luxurious house, Youtuber Life descends into the story of the worlds greatest Youtuber's rise to glory. Is this rarely used premise the cornerstone of a enriching new life simulator or just another poorly edited idea with poor views?
The visual approach to this game looks similar to a crossbreed of the Sims and the Miis used for the Wii. Furniture, environments, people and items all have this cel-shaded look with very refined structure detail. Lighting effects are well implemented to display the passage of time and while the facial animations feel stiff, movement is agile with little input delay. Animations from talking, laughing, playing and even eating are just as natural. The music, on the other hand, is very limited with one track used for each scenario. This is not as big an issue with say, parties or the movies, but when you have the same background music looping for a long period of time in your bedroom, it can get extremely monotonous and downright annoying. Sound effects are not as bad, but there are some choices used that can be very grating such as the speaking voice used for speakers at reveals. It has a great visual appeal, but hopefully they will tune the audio some more in the future.
Similar to the Sims, you will be controlling the many everyday activities of your character as they play games for content, eat and sleep, shop for new computer parts, socialize at parties and take courses to improve their skills. Everything starts out rather slow as you strive to make a name for yourself, but as you gain more followers and better income, you can move into bigger apartments, romance friends, hire constituents and attend game shows. All of this builds up experience that in turn levels up your character with every odd level providing a task point. You can uses these points to unlock new game coverage methods (reviews, speed runs) or getting discounts on games. You can also work part time jobs and accept requests from people to help get more money. The only downside to all of this is how grindy it starts to feel and the possible boredom from it. There is a lot to keep track of in such short amount of time that things can get chaotic if not managed properly, but that is part of the fun as well.
The lifeline to your channel is with your computer and every component needs to be upgraded. The better your equipment, the more stats are placed into your video and the better the final product. When a video is recording, a small puzzle game starts that involves matching cards to their respective scenes in order to produce a better flowing video. The cards feel extremely random, which can be a problem when you are dealt three copyright infringements that will force you to pay a increasingly expensive fine. It would be nice if you could build decks with the cards instead or add a symbol to a scene with a copyright in it so you can avoid adding it into a video. Vlogs of your other Youtubers can also be made and uploaded, which has a similar issue.
This is an early access product, so that means there are indeed some issues that need to be nicked. Crashes (even with the new update) occur frequently and mostly at start-up. The game has a nasty habit of slowing down to a crawl when selecting games for reviews, accessing the computer to shop and when going to select something to eat. I had a few cases of the game just stopping all together during loading screens between parties and the movies. Text and update windows are also a gigantic annoyance with them popping up to cover selection options for current tasks and requiring to restart the whole task due to them not disappearing.
There are minor issues with items not being added to the collection, friends stuck on chat while you are shopping or editing a video (a useful bug), and collaborators not finishing products. One giant bug I noticed when I played through I for the second time was a issue where my character would not receive the option to progress in the story (no objectives being produced). I continued to play for about an hour before giving up, knowing in my first play through the option was provided on cue with completion of the prior objective.
It is great to see some different ideas being tossed around when the game market is so over saturated with first person shooters, survival sims and MOBAs. The daily grind of video making and maintaining friendships is quite a challenge when you have rent and other expenses to worry about. Problems are still very visible including the frequent crashes, slow downs and annoying text bugs. There is quite a bit to do with several other lifestyles planned for release, but at the moment I still cannot recommend this game. The really annoying issues just make this a poor purchase in its' current state, but I will be checking up on it to see if these problems manage to get ironed out.
Pros
- Character models, environments are appealing
- Challenging life management
- Tutorial is rather helpful
Cons
- Crashes, slowdowns and bugs!

The game had a bit of a shakey launch, but has grown leaps and bounds, all in good ways. Amplitude has proven once again how much they care and how passionate they are. As a fan of 4x games, I highly recommend this.
The UI is amazingly well done. Other than a couple very minor things, the UI tells you everything you need to know. Sometimes it might feel hidden in a menu, but it doesn't take long to find. It is designed so you can quickly get used to it and find what you need when you need it.
You have a lot of control over everything. Even though battles play out in a space theater, your choices before hand make all the difference. There are so many factors in the outcome of battle, but perhaps the best is that you learn from your failures. When you lose a battle, you can easily see why and how to counter it. The AI tries, and for the most part succeeds, at doing this as well.
Which brings me to my next point, the AI is very well done and constantly being improved.
The races are interesting, each with their own mechanics and storylines. The writing on everything is top notch. The best part really is the writing and the details. It feels like it is out of a scifi novel from one of the greats. Everything, even that which is alien, feels to have a founding in reality because of the scientific details.
There is a lot to love about this game. If you played Endless Legend and liked it, then get this game. If you played Endless Space and either liked it or thought it was OK, then get this game. If you like turn based 4x, I know, i'm repeating myself, get this game.

NOTE: I am not an expert on 4X games, I've only extensively played one other 4X game other than Endless Space 2 (ES2), Endless Legend (EL).
Coming from EL, I was a bit familiar with the UI, how resources worked, and etc. But, being ES2, I was greeted with a lot of new features that kept the game feeling fresh. Not only that, but the graphics and UI are extremely nice to look at and navigate with. Learning this game might take a bit, depending on the person and your familiarity with 4X games., but that's because it is quite complex. There's so many different things to manage; fleets, ship designs, elections/politics, heroes, diplomacy, resources, trading companies, and etc. To help with this, they've incorporated one of the best UI's I've ever had the pleasure to use. The UI might feel daunting to the eyes at first, but it's easy to learn and everything makes complete sense to why it is placed where it is in the UI.
The glorious part of this game is that every single faction feels completely different than the other. You have the Vodyani, who use their Ark ships to take resources from systems instead of colonizing systems. The Unfallen, who are extremely passive and use their vine ships to connect systems to one another in order to colonize and gain resources (keep in mind this entire faction was almost entirely made by the community). The Cravers, who need to constantly expand and demolish their opponents with their insane military and "depletion bonuses" on their colonized systems. The Riftborn, who literally build their population with industry and use singularities to increase/decrease production on systems. The lore for each faction is completely unique and quite interesting (I usually could care less for the lore in games). Of course the major factions are more in-depth than that, but the list goes on. This part of the game, is what makes me keep coming back to it.
I can't say much about how good the AI is in this game, not being a 4X veteran. But I can say they do give me quite some challenge around the "hard" and "serious" difficulties, depending on how familiar I am with the faction I am playing.
Victory conditions are where this game gets a little iffy. Economic and Score victory are far too easy to achieve, hoping for the devs to balance these victories is not a longshot though. It has become widely accepted to just disable those victories in your game settings. Without those victory conditions, you're looking at achieving one of the other victories around turn 120-200 (on normal game speed settings). Of course you can keep playing after achieving a victory condition.
Developer support is top notch, as they are entirely focused on ES2 currently. Bug fixes and optimization are a priority as of this review's writing. Each update makes a substantial difference on how the game runs or plays, they are by no means "light" updates.
At the end of the day though, this game is DEFINITELY worth $40. Tbh I'm surprised this game doesn't cost more for the amount of content and replayability this game provides.
TLDR:
Pros:
- Amazing lore
- Versatile/unique factions
- Logical and intuitive UI
- Plethora of game settings
- Customizable factions
- Mod support
- Top notch dev-support
- Only $40
- Devs are known to give free content in future updates
Cons:
- Score/economic victory is too easy currently.
- Released with some bugs, but dev-support is top notch.
- Trading companies are op as all hell currently.
- Still ironing out balancing issues.

As many other reviewers have said, the grind is real.

Admittedly I did get bored with the grind (again, after about 500 hours of play), but there is always new content whenever I come back to play the game. I have only paid some money for the game once to get some cosmetic items and item slots (yes, you are limited to the number of items you can hold and plat can buy you more), but I figured after the 300 or 400 hours I had already played by that point, it was worth throwing a little money their way on a 50% off deal!
So again. The grind is real. But it is not a boring grind just sitting there hitting the same button over and over again like other MMORPGs. You are an acrobatic god!

L.A. Noire has some seriously high production values.  For the time, the graphics were excellent, and the lighting and voice acting are universally superb.  If L.A. Noire were a movie, it would be a really good looking movie.
However, L.A. Noire is not a very good game.  The primary problem is a lack of focus.  The gunplay isn't very good, but it's not the focus.  The cars don't handle very well, but they're not the focus.  The focus is the story, but the story is so scattered that it becomes impossible to care about what's happening.
Because of the episodic nature of the game (each case is a self contained unit) you never really get to know any of the characters.  There are a few exceptions, including a mob boss who gets lots and lots of development, then vanishes with zero resolution in the last hour of the game.  Also, the game is CONSTANTLY throwing flashbacks at you to build up the villanious pop psychologist Fontaine, who has been telegraphed from day 1 to be the chief antagonist.  Then, he dies at the last moment to a character we know nothing about, and the final battle is with a bunch of faceless mooks.  Yay?
The story was clearly what L.A. Noire was riding on, and the story is bad.  I cannot recommend this game.

Crusader Kings is an AMAZING grand strategy game from Paradox Interactive. You play as any lord or lady between 867 (1066 without DLC) to 1453 in Europe, the Middle East and North Africa. With all the DLC you can play as merchant republics, pagans and muslims as well as the default feudal christian lords. It's sort of like an RPG Strategy game in that you don't play a nation, you control one character of a dynasty. So long as your heir is always a member of your dynasty when your character dies and you control at least one county you can do whatever you like until the game end, there are no set victory conditions. I've put over 200 hours into this because it's so amazing, there's tons of variety in the form of random events, scripted events, and different play styles with different religions and cultures. Definitely buy it during the summer sale with as much DLC as you can.

There is also decent modding support, which helps insure replayability for years into the future.
Overall, this sequel is a solid improvement over the first ES.

Прелюдия
Итак, в этом обзоре я постараюсь затронуть все аспекты этой игры. Первым делом, поэтапно подам информацию, а потом дам пару советов.
Обзор
Боевка
Прекрасный слэшер. Помимо того, что в ней есть стандартные пять направлений удара так еще и многое зависет от работы ног и тела. В отличии от схожих игр здесь можно двигать туловищем и приседать, что позволяет уворачиваться и усложнять свои удары. Если вы устали от безумной мясорубки, то есть множество дальнобойных орудий убийства, начиная от стрелковых с метательными и заканчивая ловушками и артилерией. Также стоит упомянуть пинок с кулаками и классовые способности. Играя за пехотинца доджи напомнят вам о Dark Souls, а за авангарда вы почувствуете себя берсерком.
Звук
Несомненно одна из лучших частей игры. Конечно, музыка тут хороша и разнообразна, начиная от эпика в главном меню и заканчивая трубой на зеленой поляне.
Самый сок - это озвучка персонажей. Для некоторых игроков, голос одного из воинов определенной фракции становится любимым и почти, что родным, а многие даже и минуту не могут продержаться, что-бы что-либо не сказать, но это и хорошо. Голосовые команды, что говорит твой воин в принципе понятны и многие это используют для атмосферы и указания команд. К примеру, гуляешь ты себе, и тут, вдруг слышишь пронзительный крик о помощи, прибегаешь на звук и СПАСАЕШЬ СОЮЗНИКА! разве это не круто?
Картинка
Карты здесь очень разнообразны. Вас может закинуть в любую из климатических зон, а локации наполнены деревушками, замками, вулканом, колезеем, руинами и прочим. Все выглядит красиво и самое главное практично.
Персонажи игроков могут сильно отличаться друг от друга. Кастомизация позволяет перекрасить своего персонажа почти как хочешь, но подстать фракции, а разнообразие скинов на оружие и доспехи доставляет.
Кастомки и моды
Помимо стандартных режимов в игре присутствует приличное разнообразие модов и кастомных карт благодаря воркшопу. Одни просто меняют боевку перебалансируя ее или вовсе изменяя, вторые же создают моды где надо отбиваться от орд ботов, третие же меняют самих персонажей уменьшая вас до клопов или перенося в эпоху лазерных мечей и т.д.
Спорт
Хоть в игре и не предусмотрено наличие кланов игроки все равно собираются в группы и участвуют в междуклановых войнах, турнирах и прочих мероприятиях. Для этого создаются все условия, возводя спортивный интерес на достойный уровень.
Советы
Начиная играть в Chivalry заходите только на зеленые сервера и не забудьте пройти обучение. Это золотое время когда вам позволяется расслабиться и насладиться игрой среди новичков. После 15 уровня птенцов выкинут из гнезда в суровый мир и вернуться вы не сможете, поэтому цените возможность побегать среди зеленых. Чтобы выдержать натиск суровых обросших бородой скилла игроков вам нужно найти наставника, который выпрямит вам руки. Вы можете искать кланы или просто бегать с друзьями. Chivalry кооперативная игра, но никто не запрещает развлекаться в дуэлях.

NOTE: I am not an expert on 4X games, I've only extensively played one other 4X game other than Endless Space 2 (ES2), Endless Legend (EL).
Coming from EL, I was a bit familiar with the UI, how resources worked, and etc. But, being ES2, I was greeted with a lot of new features that kept the game feeling fresh. Not only that, but the graphics and UI are extremely nice to look at and navigate with. Learning this game might take a bit, depending on the person and your familiarity with 4X games., but that's because it is quite complex. There's so many different things to manage; fleets, ship designs, elections/politics, heroes, diplomacy, resources, trading companies, and etc. To help with this, they've incorporated one of the best UI's I've ever had the pleasure to use. The UI might feel daunting to the eyes at first, but it's easy to learn and everything makes complete sense to why it is placed where it is in the UI.
The glorious part of this game is that every single faction feels completely different than the other. You have the Vodyani, who use their Ark ships to take resources from systems instead of colonizing systems. The Unfallen, who are extremely passive and use their vine ships to connect systems to one another in order to colonize and gain resources (keep in mind this entire faction was almost entirely made by the community). The Cravers, who need to constantly expand and demolish their opponents with their insane military and "depletion bonuses" on their colonized systems. The Riftborn, who literally build their population with industry and use singularities to increase/decrease production on systems. The lore for each faction is completely unique and quite interesting (I usually could care less for the lore in games). Of course the major factions are more in-depth than that, but the list goes on. This part of the game, is what makes me keep coming back to it.
I can't say much about how good the AI is in this game, not being a 4X veteran. But I can say they do give me quite some challenge around the "hard" and "serious" difficulties, depending on how familiar I am with the faction I am playing.
Victory conditions are where this game gets a little iffy. Economic and Score victory are far too easy to achieve, hoping for the devs to balance these victories is not a longshot though. It has become widely accepted to just disable those victories in your game settings. Without those victory conditions, you're looking at achieving one of the other victories around turn 120-200 (on normal game speed settings). Of course you can keep playing after achieving a victory condition.
Developer support is top notch, as they are entirely focused on ES2 currently. Bug fixes and optimization are a priority as of this review's writing. Each update makes a substantial difference on how the game runs or plays, they are by no means "light" updates.
At the end of the day though, this game is DEFINITELY worth $40. Tbh I'm surprised this game doesn't cost more for the amount of content and replayability this game provides.
TLDR:
Pros:
- Amazing lore
- Versatile/unique factions
- Logical and intuitive UI
- Plethora of game settings
- Customizable factions
- Mod support
- Top notch dev-support
- Only $40
- Devs are known to give free content in future updates
Cons:
- Score/economic victory is too easy currently.
- Released with some bugs, but dev-support is top notch.
- Trading companies are op as all hell currently.
- Still ironing out balancing issues.

Прелюдия
Итак, в этом обзоре я постараюсь затронуть все аспекты этой игры. Первым делом, поэтапно подам информацию, а потом дам пару советов.
Обзор
Боевка
Прекрасный слэшер. Помимо того, что в ней есть стандартные пять направлений удара так еще и многое зависет от работы ног и тела. В отличии от схожих игр здесь можно двигать туловищем и приседать, что позволяет уворачиваться и усложнять свои удары. Если вы устали от безумной мясорубки, то есть множество дальнобойных орудий убийства, начиная от стрелковых с метательными и заканчивая ловушками и артилерией. Также стоит упомянуть пинок с кулаками и классовые способности. Играя за пехотинца доджи напомнят вам о Dark Souls, а за авангарда вы почувствуете себя берсерком.
Звук
Несомненно одна из лучших частей игры. Конечно, музыка тут хороша и разнообразна, начиная от эпика в главном меню и заканчивая трубой на зеленой поляне.
Самый сок - это озвучка персонажей. Для некоторых игроков, голос одного из воинов определенной фракции становится любимым и почти, что родным, а многие даже и минуту не могут продержаться, что-бы что-либо не сказать, но это и хорошо. Голосовые команды, что говорит твой воин в принципе понятны и многие это используют для атмосферы и указания команд. К примеру, гуляешь ты себе, и тут, вдруг слышишь пронзительный крик о помощи, прибегаешь на звук и СПАСАЕШЬ СОЮЗНИКА! разве это не круто?
Картинка
Карты здесь очень разнообразны. Вас может закинуть в любую из климатических зон, а локации наполнены деревушками, замками, вулканом, колезеем, руинами и прочим. Все выглядит красиво и самое главное практично.
Персонажи игроков могут сильно отличаться друг от друга. Кастомизация позволяет перекрасить своего персонажа почти как хочешь, но подстать фракции, а разнообразие скинов на оружие и доспехи доставляет.
Кастомки и моды
Помимо стандартных режимов в игре присутствует приличное разнообразие модов и кастомных карт благодаря воркшопу. Одни просто меняют боевку перебалансируя ее или вовсе изменяя, вторые же создают моды где надо отбиваться от орд ботов, третие же меняют самих персонажей уменьшая вас до клопов или перенося в эпоху лазерных мечей и т.д.
Спорт
Хоть в игре и не предусмотрено наличие кланов игроки все равно собираются в группы и участвуют в междуклановых войнах, турнирах и прочих мероприятиях. Для этого создаются все условия, возводя спортивный интерес на достойный уровень.
Советы
Начиная играть в Chivalry заходите только на зеленые сервера и не забудьте пройти обучение. Это золотое время когда вам позволяется расслабиться и насладиться игрой среди новичков. После 15 уровня птенцов выкинут из гнезда в суровый мир и вернуться вы не сможете, поэтому цените возможность побегать среди зеленых. Чтобы выдержать натиск суровых обросших бородой скилла игроков вам нужно найти наставника, который выпрямит вам руки. Вы можете искать кланы или просто бегать с друзьями. Chivalry кооперативная игра, но никто не запрещает развлекаться в дуэлях.

It takes forever to build (or get the parts/resources for) anything in this game, but you get used to it. It takes forever to level up your gear to Rank 30 (to then sell it and get new gear), which is required to progress your Mastery rank in the game, but you get used to it. The entire dang game is a grindfest, with a period maybe 50-150 hours in where it's actually legitimately fun, before you fall victim to the Affinity grind. I've spent all 1000+ hours of my playtime doing the same thing, making gear (warframes, weapons and sentinels/companions) and playing various but usually the same missions to level them up before selling them and continuing the process. But, you get used to it.
Obviously there's some inherent satisfaction to leveling things up and increasing your Mastery rank, or no one would do it. But I wouldn't call that fun. If you want to have fun in Warframe, you have to remember to have fun, which usually people don't. But if you get some good gear and good friends together and play some challenging missions (or just screw around looking for secret areas or something), you can have fun no matter how far into the game you are. And if you're in that transition-to-the-grind period, getting new Warframes and weapons that don't suck can be a ton of fun too.
Absolutely recommend playing with a friend that's ahead of you, unless you're a trailblazer. The game can be pretty hard to newbies who don't have decent gear, or know how to get it. But if you can remember to just have fun, you'll be used to the grinding before you know it.
Also, if you don't have someone willing to give you Platinum, the premium currency, and you're not willing to tough it out and sit in Trade chat for hours on end attempting to sell things for Plat (which is what most people do), be prepared to spend money. Wait until you get a 50% or 75% off Plat daily login reward, then buy whatever you're comfortable with. You can play the game without spending plat later on, but at first you are REQUIRED to spend some plat on slots for warframes and weapons. You CAN play with only two warframes and like eight total weapons, but at that point you're better off playing like, RuneScape. Buy some warframe slots, a few weapon slots, and a single color palette, and you're set for a very long time, long enough to know if you're willing to spend more money on the game. You do start with 50... Enough to buy a few slots with no color palette, I guess. But it won't be enough; DE wants your money.

Ark is a game that you can have a love-hate relationship with. There are both positive and negative points about this game (like any game).
- Taming dinosaurs is great fun, especially in the early and mid game. The challenge and time required are generally well balanced and you feel like you’ve really accomplished something when your new pet wakes up and prompts you for a name.
- If you can run the game on "Epic" settings then the game truly amazing, the devs paid amazing attention to detail.
-The early to mid game stages of the game are very well balanced. You rarely feel like you’re grinding because so much is happening.
- Like a lot of online survival games, when you first load in and someone who is already a high level with high level dinosaurs finds you, they will most likely kill you for no apparent reason.
- The dedicated servers are terrible.
Personally I think this game has a lot of potential, as long as the devs keep updating it and bringing out new maps. I also recommend playing this game with friends as it will give you many advantages.

I have lost countless hours engrossed in this brilliant game. Pick anyone throughout Medieval history and... go forth. Your lands will be inherited by your offspring, who you then play as.

However you are not a single unstoppable force, and the true art of war is to win without, or more realistically... with as little fighting as possible. Plots, schemes diplomacy and tactful marriages will net you with a land a lot more cheaply than conquoring it directly ever would.
I fully reccommend this game, but do not buy it without: Sword of Islam DLC, The Republic DLC, The Old Gods DLC, and arguably The Legacy of Rome DLC.
The same goes for all Paradox games, they need to be patched to true greatness... and this game is truely great.

Ever dreamt about becoming the world's #1 YouTuber or been curious about what the life of a YouTuber actually entails? Then this is the game for you! Welcome to Youtubers Life! The first 100% REAL, ACCURATE and LEGITIMATE representation of what being a YouTuber is really all about! Well, it may not be "exactly" 100% accurate, but it's close enough, and what it lacks in legitimacy, it makes up in awesomeness!
In this game, we have one goal, and that is to become the #1 YouTuber in the entire world. I guess this game could in fact be called "Pewdiepie Simulator 2016", but without all the screaming lol. You customize your character at the start of the game, selecting from a generous variety of cosmetic features, and then select the type of channel you want to run, and your personality type. Currently, gaming is the only option available, but there are four other options in the works; though I can't really see these getting much attention as this game is clearly geared towards gamers.
We start off in a very small, basic bedroom, that REALLY reminds me of my bedroom back when I was at high school. I guess the developers are targetting a younger market with this title, as our character is a school kid living at home with mum and constantly getting scolded for using the computer too much (#relatable, AMIRITE?!), but that in no means makes it any less accessible or enjoyable to older audiences.
You have access to various online shopping stores via computer, where you can buy new release games, clothes and furniture for your room, among other things, all of which are unlocked as you level up through creating quality content. I even had an amazingly hot babe walk into my bedroom and ask me out on a date to the movies! FYI, that never happens to YouTubers irl.
The game is still in early access and has a long way to go, but it's looking VERY promising at this point, and if the devs keep working on it with the same mindset and approach that they have been up until now, there's a very bright future for this game. It really is, the best available YouTube simulator out at the moment, and a bloody good game, in and of itself.

Although i am giving this game a thumbs up, there are serious problems that need to be address.
First the Pros
This game is gorgeous. Enough said. the battle scenes and the artwork, desgin are beautiful. The combat is great as well. there is good balancing, and again, the combat cinematics make my day every time. The AI isnt bad as well. sometimes they make strange decisions, but generally, they act responsibly. The economy and the over-colonisation system are perhaps the most annoying, and most satifying systems in this game. The colonisation specfically, although continuley pisses me off, but its enough of a challenge to worry about, but not so hard that u cant counter it. Its not a broken or buggy feature. Its just a way of making you think about how your empire spreads. If you do it wrong, its going to hurt. The stories and quests for each faction are by far my favourite part of this game. And the final quest to find the secrects of the Academy was amazingly done, and i hope they make addition content to explain it in the wider Endless Universe
No for the Cons
There is something serouisly wrong with how the game runs. I have i i7 quad core, gtx 1080 and 12 gb ram, and this game lags to hell. and i mean badly. I turned the game settings down to "simple" to see if that would help, and there was barely any change in the games running. This is the fundenmental problem witht the game. even with a good computer, it runs worse than Batman Arkham Asylum in its early days.
This intensifises in the later game. I timed a turn once, and it took 1 min, 46 seconds to process and end the turn. some will say this doesnt sound like a long time. You try staring at a screen waiting for that long. its longer than you think. The dilpomatic system needs work as well. The Final academy quests ask u to take sides. But alliance members never join you, and when u need to occupy a system for the quest, and they are the enemy, u cant target them, causing the game to never end.
In short:
Beautiful game, some amazing mechanics and systems, but either horribly optimised or just has major graphic problems. If this game can be made to run smoother, then this will be one of the greatest 4x's ever, on par with Stellaris, the Greatest of Space 4X's

It's a fluffed up re hash with stupid AI and very slow gameplay that crashes (on MAC, probably Windows too, definately ES had major memory leak issues). I do love the fact they are using MONO on the MAC to run their .NET assemblies. But who else gives a fart about that eh?
Technologies are basically the same as ES, nothing new in that stagnant pizza, and, once you remap from ES, the tech path is pretty much the same. Punch in the tech build and hit end turn repeatedly. Also anomaly discovery of random tech module, too random and in need of rebalancing, since it makes some tech research more or less irrelevant. No sense of urgency or surprise is offered making the process of discovery dull.
The event manager contrives events that I'm pretty sure are designed to annoy the **** out of you.
For example:
Build a colony ship and send to nice system to colonise.
Oh no! 6k pirate fleet awaits hidden en route and destroys your colony ship.
I am sure the designers are trying to develop some kind of context here but it fails as the events appear random and disconnected that become irrelevant and plain annoying as the game progresses. Post-content ad hoc parody.
A major dissuasion is the insensitive user interface.
So many times I have clicked fleet presuming it registered but for some reason theres a long delay before it actually picks up your click and so you will inadvertently send the wrong fleet somewhere. This happens all the time. Usually into destruction. It happens even when creating fleets, like cicking four ships but it only adds three and before you know it those three are in combat with a roving band of reavers and not strong enough to defeat it.
Secondly, I have not figured out a way to disable the auto routing of a fleet, as by default it will navigate the shortest path, yep you guessed it, through the system where the pirates just ko'd your colonists. Not a damn thing you can do about it. There is not even a 'move preview' so you just have to pray they will avoid the pirates. They don't.
An annoying bug is fleets moviing along hyperlinks that if they are in exactly the same position only one fleet is accessible. You can right click to show fleets, yep, there they are but no way can you select anything but the top-most. The only way to regain control of the other fleets is to move the top fleet elsewhere.
Ship design is a joke, a few modules and slots all pretty much the same in 3 tiers, and it wont really matter much anyway as the space battles do not seem to reflect your design in any observable way.
Space combat is tedious (though pretty). All I ever seem to be able to choose tactically is one of three cards, whilst the computer has a wide choice. Even on advanced you have very little control. Can't even plot the curves of your fleets or their staring points. All so contrived and you know it when your fleet outgunning opponent 3 to 1 gets a draw or worse, annihilated.
Planetary conquest, wtf... More facepalming tactical card selection for what reason exactly? Unknown. Highly unsatisfactory number crunching with pictures.
Leaders... Essentially you will get enough skill points to fill all their skill slots. There is no sense of critical decision making here. Customising their ships.. Who cares?
Planetary Management is also stale and entirely an ES transplant. Queue everything up according to spreadsheet optimised build and hit end turn repeatedly.  Early game minor differentiation but end game tedium, which seems like a signature of space 4X these days.
Dont bother playing with 12 players or huge universes you will spend all your time looking at the hourglass.
In summary, while the game is visually a treat and offers some early game entertainment it fails to deliver the goods in the long run.

Chivalry is a game that is plenty of fun to play, once you get over the initial learning curve, and find a good team.
Pros:
+Combat system is very unique
+Abandons the norm for games set in this era by not having magic (Spells and so on)
+Feels more or less balanced (Minus a few areas)
+Each of the classes are balanced
+Team based game play (Minus free for all mode)
+Requires you to think in combat
+Map design is pretty well done
Cons:
-If something isn't balanced, then it is REALLY unbalanced (For better or for worse)
-The usual fault of team based games is present (The winning team is not the better one, it's the one that's less crap)
-Servers tend not to shift in terms of game mode
-If you have over a hundred ping, you are completely screwed
-You need a good computer to help ensure a low ping (I have a laptop. Trust me on this one)
-Nobody seems to realize that you need to vary your attacks. This isn't minecraft after all. Spamming against a good opponent equals death.
Points of note
~No other game offers a melee combat system this complex in a multiplayer setting
~If you have not figured out that all team based games share this same flaw yet, I don't know what to tell you (Yes, this is way off topic)
Summary: Chivalry is a great game whenever things are going your way. If your team is trying to work together, it never seams to feel bad playing, regardless of whether or not your team is winning. This is also the games biggest flaw. You need to be working together with others. Friends working together is a good start, but a whole team working together? Now that is awesome, at least when it does happen. Trust me on this, teamwork is rare.
Overall, this game deserves a solid 8/10 (6 or 7 out of 10 if your on a lower end computer)

This is the most complex, deep, and surprising strategy game I have ever come across.  Crusader Kings 2 has an extremely high learning curve and it takes many hours to pick up on what is happening in the game, but once you get past the initial hump there is a bottomless well of rewarding experiences.
The game is a turn based feudal lineage simulator.  You control a character with the goal of continuing your dynasty through the centuries, once you die you play as your heir.  You must attempt to expand your family’s holdings, keep your vassals happy, and increase your prestige.  Choose to start out as a lowly count and work your way up to being a king, or start as a lofty emperor and try and expand and maintain your empire...or play as anything in between.  You are able to plot against your enemies, arrange marriages for powerful alliances, and go to war for more land.
The game also has more than 30 DLC options to purchase and the list can be daunting at first, but the DLC fall into 2 main categories: cosmetic additions and gameplay expansions.  The cosmetic additions are the vast majority and include extra portrait options for characters from various regions, extra music tracks when playing as certain countries, and extra options for the dynasty shields that represent your family.  All of these add extra flavor to the game, but do not affect the gameplay mechanics at all.
The gameplay expansions are the larger and gameplay changing DLC.  These include: The Ruler Designer which allows you to customize your character, The Legacy of Rome which introduces retinues, The Sword of Islam that allows you to play as a Muslim character, The Republic which gives you access to playing as one of the trading oriented countries, and The Old Gods which opens up the option to play as a pagan.  All of these add a great deal of additional depth and replayability to the game, I would highly suggest picking these up.
If you are looking for a grand turn based strategy game with depth beyond compare you are looking in the right place.

The writing is excellent, the tech tree in-depth (having significant impacts), and the politics engaging. The races aswell are markedly different, which gives it a lot of replayability.
The combat has strategic elements through support modules, hull types and fleet interaction, but it didn't hold my interest as well as the other part of the game did and I found myself auto-resolving a lot to get to the better parts of the game. The combat visualiser (present in the previous game) was interesting for the first few times, but quickly became a bit irrelevant. Mostly because there's not much to do other than watch numbers drop on one ship or another.
Combat is only one small part of the game however, and could be improved to be suitably epic I feel, so don't let the above deter you.
All in all I love this game, and am excited for them to keep improving it.

I am writing this review fully expecting to remove points from it, and ultimately to change it to recomend the game. However, for now, I cannot recommend ES2 despite my love for the whole Endless universe and Amplitude in general.
The biggest issue with this game is very simple - it is unfinished and not fleshed out. I beleive it can be fixed by adding more stuff to the game and make its awesome features more complete and impactful.
With all of that in mind, here is my point by point analysis of Endless Space 2's features and systems which I have an issue with:
-Faction Quests. ES2 improves hugely on the faction quest system we saw in Endless Legend. Each faction has their unique storyline explaining who they are and giving player access to advanced faction powers upon completing quests. Compared to the EL faction quests, the ones in ES2 are a huge improvement - stories are a lot more interesting and engaging, you are actually given choice of how you want to complete quests, and the rewards are lot cooler. The problem is, those quests are SHORT. I completed the whole Riftborn storyline in under 100 turns, and was left thinking: What? That's it? When it got interesting? It is a huge dissapointment for a feature so well implemented to just... end, never to be seen again.
-Random Quests and Events. The problem here is similar to the faction quests issue - while the quests and events are really awesome, giving you a chance to roleplay or powergame with various choices and risks, there is just too damn few of them! Each faction has exactly ONE unique sidequest, it seems. Those are about as cool as the main storyline - giving the factions more character and story, but... one? Really? I only played for 8 hours and I already feel I've seen every event and side quests in the game - and every time I start a new game, I keep getting the same old events over and over again. It is boring and kills my willingness to come back to the game.
-Political System. Now this feature is really well done - you can manipulate your parliament to get access to the laws you want, you are given a pretty nice selection of laws for each political leaning. However, right now this feature feels a bit dry. I wish there were more political events based on what parties are represented in your parliament and what factions lack support. It would be so cool if having a certain type of government actually FORCED you into doing certain things, once they gain enough political XP, so that you might want to manipulate the politics to not let them grow out of control, unless you are willing to commit. Or for example there could be events which only come up once certain parties reach certain levels of support. Or even quests from certain political parties, which would give you unique laws for them upon completion. I feel like this system just has a lot of unrealized potential.
-Technologies. I think you might start noticing a trend here... The tech tree is fine, giving you quite a bit of freedom and choice, legendary deeds are great at giving the game direction, but... there are too few technologies! Where are epic techs giving me awesome overpowered options? Where are game-altering economic advances? I just don't feel like the game rewards you enough for fully dedicating to the scientific strategy.
So these are the main issues I currently have with ES2. As you can see none of those are unfixable - a few good content updates might make this game very close to the best Grand Strategy on the market.
And the rest of the game is very much fine - Empire management is fine, Combat system is unobtrusive, but gives you quite a few strategic choices based on how you build you ships and what strategies you use, diplomacy is simplistic but gives you all the options you need. Minor factions are not too fleshed out, but fullfil their role well enough (though there is, again, room for a lot of improvements). And obviously, the art direction is absolutely gorgeous with phenomenal art, great-looking map and sleek UI.
Right now, Endless Space 2 is a foundation for an absolutely phenomenal grand strategy. Once the features I mentioned are tweaked and improved, I will hopefully remove points from this list and will finally be able to reccomend this game.
Right now, though - the game is way too bare bones, and probably should have spent another couple of month in Early Access, so no recommendation for it - I love you, Amplitude, but this is a bit of a letdown, especially considering how good the content it teases is.

There's potential here but there're also a lot of problems. For me at the moment, these problems currently outweigh the pros. Let me expand a little on this (I do intend to keep it brief).
The game itself feels like a very stripped down version of The Sims. This isn't necessarily a bad thing but it is a comparison that will no doubt be made often. Another big frustration is that while editing things can just continue to happen and stop the process. Someone may decide to just walk into your room and ask you something, so you quit the editing process. of the indie-strategy hit Endless Space from 2012 comes the long awaited sequel Endless Space 2, and this time, with 5 years of additional experience, and direct input from a very passionate community, Amplitude Studios have created what could very well be considered the master in its genre.
Expanding on the ideas from the first game, and combining it with elements from its spin-off sequel Endless Legend, Endless Space 2 has found a beautiful balance of classic 4X strategy with light roleplay elements in the form of multi-resolution quests, heroes that can act as leaders of fleets or planets, and personalized unit upgrades where you decide how your ships should fight, fly, and function. These features are a staple of the Endless franchise at this point, and fans will feel instantly familiar, but new-comers to the series, either complete newbies or 4X-veterans, will certainly feel the breeze of fresh air blown into the genre.
you take charge of one of eight unique civilizations, and fight for rule of the galaxy. You can lead the
, the primary human faction, whose preferred means of domination comes through industry and military might. The
, little grey men, whose main pursuit is scientific discovery. The bio-mechanical abominations called
, created for war, whose only purpose is to eat and kill. The
, a race of interdimensional robots looking for their own place in our bizarre version of reality. The
, a society of amphibians ruled by gangsters, who want nothing but more power and more money. The
, a religious cult of semi-digital beings who revere the mythical Virtual Endless to the degree that they will level entire worlds in the name of their church. The
, possibly the oldest race in existence, but also the last to enter the galactic battlefield, are a civilization of Ent-like beings who worship the Fire and the Heart. And last, but certainly not least, the
– a civilization consisting entirely of Horatio, the most perfect being in existence, whose sole goal is to make the rest of the galaxy just as beautiful as he is.
Much of the gameplay of Endless Space 2 is exactly that of a typical 4X game. You build improvements in your cities (or systems in this case), train armies (fleets), set up trade routes, colonize new places, threaten or praise your neighbours, and all in all try to become the top dog. There are multiple ways of securing a victory, it can be through the usual means of total domination. Secure the home world of each player, own most of the available systems, or just straight up wipe out the other civilizations. But there are also less violent means. You may win through economic means, by making a set amount of gold (referred to as dust) in the game before the ending turn. You can also construct mighty wonders, or science the sh!t out of the game. There are even diplomatic ways to secure victory, and all of these can be shared with others by forming alliances. Gone are the days of having to betray your friend at the final turn so you can win.
. Endless Space 2 suffers from many of the same issues their previous games have around launch. There are game breaking bugs where a turn is unable to complete, where units become immobile, and quest objectives can’t be finished. And multiplayer is nigh unplayable, with near constant desyncs, and battles that take upwards of 10 minutes to finish. These are surely issues that will be finished in time, as it has with previous instalments, but it is nonetheless frustrating to see it happen again and again.
In the end however, the good heavily outweighs the bad. The new features bring a lot of fun and variation to the game, and I am certain the game will be a hit given enough time to shine. Amplitude have come a long way from being the little indie-studio that grew out of a handful of ex-Ubisoft employees looking to make their own mark on the industry. Spawning 4 games in half a decade, all well received by both gamers and critics alike, and now they’ve caught the attention of a larger publisher. With Sega at their side, Amplitude has a very bright future ahead of them, and I hope they get to continue to make the games they want for a very long time – and I will be there to cheer them along all the way.

This game has potential, but I cannot recommend it in its current form. I've played since early access started, and it's definitely addictive, however, there are some game breaking flaws for me.
Firstly, the AI is far too aggressive. Everyone but the Lumeris will literally delcare war on you a few turns after you meet them, for absolutely no reason, while the Lumeris are the opposite and will never become aggressive. It's a bit absurd.
Secondly, playing a huge map is basically useless, as there is an expansion mechanic, that even with advanced techs ruins the game. You can't expand past X systems or the penalites will bankrupt you in 2-3 turns and every system in your empire will revolt. Game over. It's profoundly annoying, luckily I was able to easily mod the file which controlled the expansion limit and set it to 9999 to make sure I can actually play large maps.
Third, the AI is annoying in other ways. If you even remotely outmatch it (this includes pirates which run around attacking your systems with one ship) they will just retreat. Now you take damage when you retreat, but by late game the problem is ships reapair within 2-3 turns because of tech, so what ends up happening is the computer will just build a massive fleet, attack your system, you respond. Since you can only attack one stack of ships per turn, the AI just retreats, leaving another 4-5 stacks left to invade your planets, the fleet that retreats comes back in 2 turns fully repaired from the previous retreat, with a full compliment of troops, rinse repeat. this causes you to never be able to destroy their fleets and they run amok invading all your systems. I have about 10 super fleets and I simply cannot destroy anything. It makes war totally pointless, and infuriating. A simple fix would be to implement a chance that a fleet wont be able to retreat, or if it's recently retreated it can't retreat. Problem sovled.
Combat suffers from the same problems as Endless Space 1. There's a few more mechanics, but basically its a back and forth cinematic with little to no control. If the enemy even slightly outmatches you in technology you will lose the battle, period. Essentially it comes down to, who has the next tier of tech first, or numbers. No tactics or strategy. Eventually, even if you're ahead in tech, the computer catches up, and once that happens combat becomes a useless back and forth of who has more ships. Endless Space 1 suffered from this same problem, and I have no idea why they didn't address this in the sequel.
Last, performance late game is awful (I have an inkling this has something to do with the Riftborn, as everytime I take one of their systems or destroy one of their fleets performance drastically improves). It's a massive lag fest, and I have a very good system. I'm fairly certain the program is riddled with memory leaks, which is what's causing the progressive slow down that eventually forces you to exit and boot the game back up (which then gets you perfect performance for a few turns before the leaks start screwing your system again).
It's a good game, but it has lots of problems. Wait for some patches.

CONS:

THis game is great - but... There always is a but in here.
1. The ships looking great - but: The shipbuilding is bland and easy going, Energy or balistic, that is it. Just 4 weapon types, repeating themselves.
2. The battles look great - but: They are often always the same and you just spam the same tactic. And there is also a retreat mechanic that makes finding a battle hard and annoys you with a thousnad battles never had.
3. The different factions are cool - but the AI housing them is lousy. Declares wars for one system and leaves them, gets themselves beaten to death before even thinking about a proposal for peace. ES2 could have learned so much here from Stellaris.
4. The population mechanics are cool - but: you can't just purge unwanted or harmfull population, kill them, or push them out, no you have to go trough some SJW tier Culling or find a way to work around.
5. The late game would be epic. - But there are so huge lags it can even be a problem to assemble a fleet with the UI hanging back. Really, it's nearly unplayable, and only SotSII is beating it in this regard, but(!) even that just by a little bit difference. Suddenly a faction controlling about 10% of the galaxy beats your empire by completing a wonder. Well, nice of you to sit through the 250 turns to get beaten by a random small empire. Still this is the one thing that ESII makes better than Stellaris
6. The Heroes are cool - but: They all come out of a cloning tube and get a different number. Human Hero#22 or Tree Hero #3? It really doesn't matter. Most heroes have only lack luster Skill sets that often have benefits in a layout making me uncertain if the devs realy want you to develop tem? Why do I have to skill my combat hero hero for population controll to advance into the next tier of combat skills? ES I did a much better job in this, making it easy to get the Hero you wanted. The cloning tube hero syndrom also permits that you get attachted to any of them. They all feature the same look and appearence, the same 3 classes and responding skill tress and ships. Really boring.
7. Diplomatic... - but: You can't bargain for systems you invade currently while leading in war and trying to get a peace going. Why? Why can' I take a planet that I already controll to 90%? So if you go to peace the invasion is stopped. Bamm. Also the AI gives you plantes as a price for peace that are inside their influence sphere and are autocaptured by them without even one ship asap, because this game has some nasty bugs and influence is certainly one of them.
Tl;Dr
This game has many flaws. Also it is buggy. If you want better combat, play SotS, if you want better Diplomatic, play Stellaris. If you want to stick with these guys, do so, this game has potential, but do so on your own risk.

There was a time where I could really recommend this game 100%. But not anymore.
As time has passed more people got good at the game resulting in a lot of higher ranked players.
Now you might think that that's a good thing. Well no, in this community it isn't.
Instead of good players playing against each other you have 90% of highranks (45+) playing in team objective servers and rank stacking on the same team (usually attack side). So basically instead of having balanced fun matches most high ranked players purposefully join the team with more highranks which ends up in very unbalanced teams and an almost guaranteed win for the stacked team.
You really only need to look at the rank distribution at the start of a match and you can predict which team wins with 99% certainty.
Not only is it unfair for the players on the other team but it makes matches just overall very boring. As someone who reached rank 50 I either join the stack and will not be challenged at all (imagine a pro soccer player playing against a 5 year old) or I join the other team and stand no chance at all.
It has been like this for quite a while but it's reached it's peak lately where you really have to search hard for a server where this doesn't happen every match. Sometimes I don't find such a server and end up not playing at all because of it.
The game has a lot of little flaws but in my opinion it's the community who in the end really ruins it. They call it a skill-based game but there is no skill involved in unbalancing teams as much as possible and winning without effort. In fact a lot of people who think that they are particularly good only think so because they simply stack all the time.
The only way to enjoy this game nowadays is if you like to play in a clan. If you are into that I can recommend it even though I'm not a huge fan of clans. Otherwise you can only join the stacking or lose nearly every match if you don't. I dont enjoy either of it and therefor this review.

This is the most complex, deep, and surprising strategy game I have ever come across.  Crusader Kings 2 has an extremely high learning curve and it takes many hours to pick up on what is happening in the game, but once you get past the initial hump there is a bottomless well of rewarding experiences.
The game is a turn based feudal lineage simulator.  You control a character with the goal of continuing your dynasty through the centuries, once you die you play as your heir.  You must attempt to expand your family’s holdings, keep your vassals happy, and increase your prestige.  Choose to start out as a lowly count and work your way up to being a king, or start as a lofty emperor and try and expand and maintain your empire...or play as anything in between.  You are able to plot against your enemies, arrange marriages for powerful alliances, and go to war for more land.
The game also has more than 30 DLC options to purchase and the list can be daunting at first, but the DLC fall into 2 main categories: cosmetic additions and gameplay expansions.  The cosmetic additions are the vast majority and include extra portrait options for characters from various regions, extra music tracks when playing as certain countries, and extra options for the dynasty shields that represent your family.  All of these add extra flavor to the game, but do not affect the gameplay mechanics at all.
The gameplay expansions are the larger and gameplay changing DLC.  These include: The Ruler Designer which allows you to customize your character, The Legacy of Rome which introduces retinues, The Sword of Islam that allows you to play as a Muslim character, The Republic which gives you access to playing as one of the trading oriented countries, and The Old Gods which opens up the option to play as a pagan.  All of these add a great deal of additional depth and replayability to the game, I would highly suggest picking these up.
If you are looking for a grand turn based strategy game with depth beyond compare you are looking in the right place.

Not really much story, but I'll try to explain the best I can. You defeat monsters in your way so you can get to a boss and kill the boss, you can get to the boss with help from recruited heroes, heroes will give you extra damage per second, except for the first one. the very first one gives clicking power. Bosses are every 5 levels. To progress through a level you must defeat 10 enemies. (Except for boss rooms, you'll only need to kill it once) Every hero has several upgrades which can be unlocked for leveling the hero up a few times. The upgrades will sometimes add story to heroes, not great, but it's alright I guess.

The gameplay is not very interesting, it's an Idol game so you can't really do much, incase you don't know what an idol game it is here is the definition, according to Wikipedia.
This entire game is either you waiting for your heroes to kill an enemy, or click the screen to defeat enemies yourself. That's about it though. After the first ascension (Explained later) you get a couple more tabs other than hero and stats. You get relics, mercenaries, ancients, and clans. Relics are rewarded from mercenary tasks, they give what certain ancients can do. Ancients are creatures summoned with Hero Souls (gotten from ascensions), and will help you progress faster or make the game easier. Ancients will help you get through the game faster. Mercenaries are recruited and will do tasks for you to get hero souls, or gold, or anything along those lines.As your mercanary goes through more quests, he levels up, making rewards greater. Clans are kind of self explanatory. In a clan you can get more hero souls and interact with clan members. To ascend you have to level up "Amenhotep" so you can get the upgrade, but don't use it right when you get it, because then you won't get hero souls most likely. Hero souls are gotten from primal bosses, which are bosses that can give hero souls after defeat, you actually only get them when you ascend though. After you reach level 300 you unlock Transcendence. Transcending is a difficult task, but it is well worth it, it's practically your ancients, but much much better. Transcending gets rid of
of your hero souls, relics,and a few other things, and restarts you at the beginning of the game. The upside to this is you get Ancient souls, which can be used on your ancient heroes. The gameplay is slow until you reach the higher levels, which you can get to in a fraction of the time. But that's about it. You just keep ascending and transcending.

You can influence this by using coercion (such as spending gold or influence) or by following the political party's agenda (building, doing research, going to war, ...)
There has also been numerous 'quality of life' improvements, such as the dynamic map overview that shows where your resources come from, who you are allied with, trade routes etc without going through a bunch of menus.
