Take on the role as Cole Phelps, an aspiring LAPD-detective, as you get to revisit the 1940's.
The whole game is highly inspired by classic Noire-films, as the title suggests, and the story is accompanied with smooth-jazz music, ranging from calm to dramatic, depending on the situation. It really adds to the feel alot.
Many of the cases you get to solve have interesting and really well-written plots, where you have to think outside the box to solve the murders, smugglings etc. You will also need to use your wits in order to get the most out of your suspects and witnesses while interrogating them.
The game is pretty long, it'll take around 25-35 hours to play, depending on playstyle (rushed or leisure)
and I kept wanting to come back for more every time I quit the game for the day.
My only really negative critique on the game is that there really isn't enough penalty for driving reclessly, or even destroying street lamps, driving into civilians and such. The only penalty is a  measly cash-penalty that shows up at the end of the case, and It doesn't really affect the Case's rating unless you really go batshit in the streets, running over grannies and destroying cars by the dozens. And also I might add that it's very un-even in difficulty when it comes to clues. Sometimes you will have to really give it your best to figure things out, whilst other times you will more or less get the explanations handed to you in small cut-scenes or comments by NPC's. Over all it's a really entertaining game, filled with memorable characters and innovative concepts that I really enjoyed. I really recommend this slow-paced yet very exciting third person detective game with action elements.

- Strong Story

cons :

Review :
In L.A. Noire you play as Cole Phelps, War Veteran Who fought in the Second world war in The American army in Japan.
After the war returned to Los Angeles he starts to work as a Cop, but after proving himself, he becomes a Detective...
In the game your main goal is to solve cases as good and as truly as possible...
in a City filled iwth Corruption and shady Characters...
One of the things you will be doing alot in this game is Looking around, looking for clues.
Interrogating people is also a big part of the game, Here is where the Face Animations play a big role...
it can be really hard to see if someone is lying or telling the truth.
Knowing this is a Rockstar game doesn’t mean its a shooting game or something like GTA
you're not allowed to just randomly kill people on the street or to carry a gun when you want.
As a LAPD Detective your job is to protect the people of Los Angeles.
There also isn't a Open world to this game, While doing mission you can have little sub mission in them,
i noticed when i was driving to my next location some random event could happen on the streets, and its my choice to do something or just keep driving.
this give it alot of replay value and just changed the passing abit.
Overall I really enjoyed this game, and i clocked 21 hours in my first Play
I also felt pretty sad and empty when the game ended.
Hope L.A. Noire 2 is on its way.

While most space 4x games try to make you feel like you're taking part in a giant space opera similar to The Culture book series, Endless Space 2 (ES2) is not afraid to be different. One way it does this is through it's races. You have your normal run of the mill Humans focused on conquring! Evil robots whose sole purpose is to kill and at one with the galaxy tree people.
But what about a race of people who are created in the image of Horatio as he believes he's pefect... yeah a race of self absorbed clones. Or a race of aliens who are literally to smart for their own good and had to create an AI to make sure they don't blow anything else up aside from their moon. OR how about a race of aliens who's run like an italian mob? It's unqiue but it doesn't stop there.
I'd say this is a story based 4X game. You can play to win through the normal victories like kill everyone, befreind all, science them to death but the fun here is the journey. You get quests through out your game and it's not like "hey, we found some thing go look at it." For one of the races you're given almost a noire story of 3 famlies who all want somethign diffrent to be done with the dust, the currency and power of the game. You pick one and it progresses the story. It doesn't feel like an afterthought but like someone put time and effort into each story to make it as interesting as possible.
this game is great. If you're looking for a 4x game in space but want something a bit different than Gal Civ or Stellaris, check this out!
